# The wallet web app: what gets built

One Angular app with a small Express proxy, at wallet.masterpod.com one
day and on this machine now, that does everything the three test apps do
(test-web-app for anos, masterpod-test-web-app, keyholder-test-web-app) in
one flow: create an anoPod, get vouched, give the identity record, set up,
fill the security buckets, make anos accounts, send anos, chat, trade.
Beside it, a signing server (a stand-in until 2026-11-13, section 3), and
the changes to masterpodsoftware and anossoftware the wallet needs.
keyholdersoftware does not change.

Every shape not written here is exactly as the three architecture record
folders describe it (~/Desktop/Z/masterpod_software_architecture,
keyholder_software_architecture, anos_software_architecture). Where this
document differs from them, this document wins; the records get updated
at the end of the build. The public ledger id is in
docs/public-ledger-id.md.

Shapes are written as in the records: hex is lowercase hex of raw bytes,
an id 32 bytes; a route is "POST /path (level)"; a refusal "<status>
<reason>". Levels: the masterpod's none / session / vouched / setup; the
validators' new "account" level (section 5.3).

## 1. The pieces, and who calls whom

    browser (the Angular app)   the wallet origin only:
                                GET  /api/config
                                POST /api/masterpod/<route>
                                POST /api/anos/<n>/<route>
                                POST /api/keyholder/<n>/<route>
                                POST /api/sign/<n>, GET /api/sign/<n>/public-keys
    the proxy (server/)         masterpod :3100, validators :3001 to :3005, keyholders :3201 to :3205,
                                the signing server :3300 (two signing servers on the network, section 3)
    a validator                 the masterpod, POST /get-anos-account (new); the other validators, as today
    a keyholder                 the masterpod, POST /get-anopod-session-keys, as today
    a signing server            the masterpod, POST /check-signing-passkey: whether the passkey's answer that came with
                                a request is good (section 3 and 4.11; 2026-11-20, from the signing servers' own
                                update on); on the network also Google Cloud KMS, which holds its wallet pairs

Ports on this machine: 4200 ng serve (the user runs it), 4300 the proxy,
3300 the signing server, the rest as they are.

Folders

    ~/Desktop/Z/web_app           the Angular workspace, project "wallet": src/, server/, docs/, proxy.conf.json
    ~/Desktop/Z/signingserver     the signing server, its own project (the stand-in until 2026-11-13)

Both are new and not git repositories yet; the user runs git init and
commits.

## 2. The proxy (web_app/server/)

Express 5 and http-proxy-middleware, ESM, three files: server/index.js
(listens), server/app.js (createApp: the routes below), server/config.js
(the variables, every one with a local default, so no env file is needed
on this machine).

    variable            default                                              meaning
    PORT                4300                                                 where it listens
    MASTERPOD_URL       http://localhost:3100                                the masterpod API
    VALIDATOR_URLS      http://localhost:3001,...,http://localhost:3005      comma separated, in validator order
    KEYHOLDER_URLS      http://localhost:3201,...,http://localhost:3205      comma separated, in keyholder order
    SIGNING_SERVER_URLS http://localhost:3300                                comma separated, the signing servers in order (2026-11-13, below)
    SHARE_THRESHOLD     3                                                    how many shares rebuild a secret
    DEPOSIT_FLOOR_PERCENT  80    how many of the keyholders must store a share for a deposit to go through, in percent, 1 to 100 (section 6; 2026-11-07)
    DEFAULT_VALIDATOR   1                                                    until 2026-11-10 the validator the wallet posted to; it no longer picks the validator (below)
    DIST_DIR            dist/wallet/browser                                  the Angular build it serves
    RP_ID               localhost                                            the relying-party id the browser uses in both ceremonies; the masterpod's RP_ID
    GUARDED_LOCK_MINUTES  1    the validators' time lock on a guarded account, in minutes (a week, 10080, on the network since 2026-11-12; 10 on the testnet before that)
    VAULT_LOCK_MINUTES    2    the same on a vault account (30 days, 43200; 20 before)
    LOCK_OFFSET_MINUTES   1    how much more than its lock a guarded or vault transfer may be dated ahead (10; 5 before)

The three lock numbers are the validators' (anossoftware's
network/testnet.env); the wallet dates a guarded or vault transfer the
lock plus the offset ahead and a validator refuses one outside its
window, so the two files are changed together (2026-11-06, section 11).

DEFAULT_VALIDATOR no longer picks the validator (2026-11-10, section 11):
the browser picks one of the listed validators per session, at random,
and moves to the next one when it does not answer (8.3). The variable
stays, with its boot check that it is not larger than the list, and
/api/config still answers it as defaultValidator, for a tab that was
loaded before that change and still posts to it. The browser's code no
longer reads defaultValidator. Taking both out is a later clean-up.

SIGNING_SERVER_URLS is a list (2026-11-13, section 11): the signing
servers, in order. /api/config answers how many there are as
signingServers, and the browser picks one per session, at random, and
asks the other when it does not answer (8.3). An empty list is refused
at boot, "SIGNING_SERVER_URLS must list at least one signing server".
Until 2026-11-13 the variable was SIGNING_SERVER_URL, one address; that
name is no longer read.

Routes

    GET  /api/config                  200 { validators, keyholders, signingServers, shareThreshold, depositFloorPercent,
                                      defaultValidator, edition, rpId, guardedLockMinutes, vaultLockMinutes, lockOffsetMinutes }:
                                      the three counts are the list lengths (signingServers since 2026-11-13); the browser
                                      never sees an address; defaultValidator is DEFAULT_VALIDATOR,
                                      still answered and no longer read by the browser (2026-11-10, above)
    GET  /api/health                  200 { status: "ok" }
    ANY  /api/masterpod/<path>        forwarded to MASTERPOD_URL/<path>
    POST /api/masterpod/ask-joy       a message to Joy (2026-11-24, 4.18; the point on a message to Joy, below): forwarded
                                      to MASTERPOD_URL/ask-joy as every masterpod path is, and its answer handed on as
                                      the stream of lines it is, application/x-ndjson, marked so that nginx does not
                                      collect it first
    ANY  /api/anos/<n>/<path>         forwarded to VALIDATOR_URLS[n - 1]/<path>; n not 1..count: 404 { error: "unknown validator" }
    ANY  /api/keyholder/<n>/<path>    forwarded to KEYHOLDER_URLS[n - 1]/<path>; likewise 404 { error: "unknown keyholder" }
    POST /api/sign/<n>                forwarded to SIGNING_SERVER_URLS[n - 1]/sign; n not 1..count: 404 { error: "unknown signing server" }
    GET  /api/sign/<n>/public-keys    forwarded to SIGNING_SERVER_URLS[n - 1]/public-keys; likewise
    anything else under /api          404 { error: "Not Found", path }; since 2026-11-13 that is also the answer to
                                      POST /api/sign and GET /api/sign/public-keys, the two signing routes until then,
                                      so a tab loaded before the change cannot sign until it is reloaded
    GET  /stickers/<set>/<number>     a sticker's picture (2026-11-23, 4.16; the point on the stickers' pictures, below):
                                      asked of MASTERPOD_URL/sticker-picture/<set>/<number> and handed on as image/webp,
                                      marked to be kept for a year
    anything else under /stickers     404 { error: "Not Found", path }, also for a method other than GET
    everything else                   the files of DIST_DIR; index.html for a path that is not a file (the router's deep links)

The Home Screen files (2026-11-21, section 11). Four of the files of
DIST_DIR are there for a phone's Home Screen: manifest.webmanifest, the
web app manifest (the name "anoPod wallet", the short name "anoPod",
the start address and the scope "/", the display mode "standalone",
white for both of its colours, and two pictures); icon-192.png and
icon-512.png, those two pictures, 192 and 512 pixels a side; and
apple-touch-icon.png, 180 pixels a side, the picture an iPhone puts on
its Home Screen. They are plain files of public/, which the build
copies beside index.html as they are. The proxy has no route and no
line of code for them: it serves them as it serves every file of the
build, the manifest as "application/manifest+json; charset=utf-8" and
a picture as "image/png", with the safety headers and the page's
content security policy of the points below. Four lines in the head of
src/index.html name them to a browser: the link to the manifest, the
link to the iPhone's picture, the name under the iPhone's icon
(apple-mobile-web-app-title, "anoPod") and the page's theme colour
(theme-color, white). The policy lets a manifest and a picture of the
wallet's own address through as it stands: it has no part of its own
for a manifest, so "default-src 'self'" decides, and a picture falls
under "img-src 'self' data: blob:". What the manifest changes on a
phone: on an iPhone with iOS 18 to 25, a wallet that a person adds to
the Home Screen opens as an app of its own, with no address bar, where
without a manifest the icon is a bookmark that opens Safari (since iOS
26 every site that is added opens as an app, webkit.org/blog/17333);
and to Chrome on Android the wallet is a site that can be installed as
an app, which by web.dev's install criteria takes a name, pictures of
192 and 512 pixels, a start address and a display mode. The icon
carries the name "anoPod" and the logo. The one manifest serves the
wallet, the moderator edition and the attestor edition, so all three
show "anoPod". No part keeps a copy of the wallet on the phone: there
is no service worker, and every load still comes from the proxy. An
iPhone settles at the moment of adding whether an icon is an app or a
bookmark (seen on iOS 18.6, section 11), so a change of the display
mode reaches only a wallet that is added after it.

Behaviour
- Bodies are streamed, never parsed: no express.json in front of the
  proxy, so a 70 MB bucket request passes through as it is. Of the
  browser's headers a backend gets three: Content-Type, Content-Length
  and Origin (2026-11-19, section 11; until then every header went
  through as received). Every other header of the browser stops at the
  proxy, the cookies, the Referer (the address of the wallet page the
  person is on), the browser's name and the person's languages among
  them. The Origin goes through as received, so the backends' CORS
  rules see http://localhost:4200 as they do today. The Connection
  header is the one the proxy library writes itself, for each side:
  "close" to the masterpod, a keyholder and a signing server,
  "keep-alive" to a validator (2026-11-11, the point on the connections
  below), and back to its caller what the caller sent. nginx in front
  of the proxy sends "close" with every call, so since 2026-11-19 the
  proxy answers nginx "close" after a call to a validator too, where it
  handed on the doorman's "keep-alive". nginx closed that connection
  itself either way.
- The backend's status and body come back unchanged. Of its headers the
  browser gets one, Content-Length (2026-11-19, section 11; until then
  every header of the answer came back as the backend sent it). Every
  other header of the backend is dropped, and the proxy writes
  Content-Type itself: "application/json; charset=utf-8" when the
  backend said application/json, "text/plain; charset=utf-8" for
  anything else. (Since 2026-11-24 one answer keeps a type of its own,
  the masterpod's stream of lines for a message to Joy: the point on a
  message to Joy, below.) So a backend cannot set a cookie, and a browser never
  draws a backend's answer as a page. A redirect from a backend comes
  back with its status and without its target, and the wallet's code
  treats it as any failed call. Every answer under /api carries three
  headers, the proxy's own answers too (/api/config, /api/health, the
  404s and the 502): "Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none';
  frame-ancestors 'none'; sandbox", "X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff"
  and "Cache-Control: no-store". They say: this is data, do not guess
  its type, do not keep it, and if a person opens the address, run
  nothing in it and give it none of the wallet's rights. A backend that
  does not answer: 502 { error: "<masterpod | validator n | keyholder n
  | signing server n> unavailable" }. Proxy timeout 120 seconds.
- The safety headers (2026-11-19, section 11). Every answer of the
  proxy carries three headers, the files of the build and the answers
  under /api alike, with the values of the validator monitor
  (monitorsoftware/server/app.js): "X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff"
  (the browser does not guess a file's type), "X-Frame-Options: DENY"
  (no other site can show the wallet inside its own page) and
  "Referrer-Policy: no-referrer" (the browser does not tell another
  site which wallet page the person came from). Under /api they stand
  beside the three headers of the point above; nosniff is in both
  lists and is sent once. A fourth header is not the proxy's: nginx on
  the wallet servers adds "Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000"
  to every answer under the three wallet names, where TLS is
  (deploy/nginx/wallet.conf), as on the monitor. A browser that has
  seen it uses https only for that name for a year. Accepted with it:
  if the certificate of a wallet name ever runs out, such a browser
  shows an error with no way to go on, where a browser that has not
  seen the header shows a warning a person can click through. The
  closed page and the folder /launch/, which nginx serves itself, get
  that one header and none of the proxy's three. The closed page takes
  nothing from a person and shows nothing from a backend, and it
  carries its own script inside the page, so a policy for it would be
  a piece of work of its own. The monitor's X-Robots-Tag is not
  copied: it is no safety header, and the monitor is a private page
  where the wallet is a public one.
  The page's content security policy (2026-11-19, section 11) is one
  header more of the proxy's, on every answer outside /api. It tells
  the browser where a wallet page may take each kind of thing from:
  its scripts, its style rules, its fonts, its pictures, and the
  addresses its code may call. It is the monitor's policy with
  "blob:" added for pictures: nine parts joined by "; ", listed
  below. It is in force since the build of 2026-11-19 that switched
  it on, step 4 of forclaude/wallet-headers-plan-1.md: the header's
  name is "Content-Security-Policy", and the browser blocks what the
  policy does not allow and says so in its console. For the one build
  before that it was sent report-only, as
  "Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only", under which the browser
  blocked nothing and only wrote into its console what the policy
  would have blocked. The policy names no address for reports, so
  such a line shows only in the console of the browser that drew the
  page. Under /api the policy of the point above ("default-src
  'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; sandbox") stands in its place: the
  proxy writes it over the page's policy on every answer under /api,
  so an answer there carries the one policy. The closed page and the
  folder /launch/ get no policy (above). "script-src 'self'" needs a
  build that writes no script into the page itself, so the production
  build has "inlineCritical": false under optimization.styles in
  angular.json, the monitor's setting: the built index.html links the
  build's style sheet plainly and holds one script tag, which names
  the build's file. Without the setting Angular writes a short script
  into the page that switches the main style sheet on; the policy
  would block it, and the style sheet would stay off. The development
  configuration of the build, which ng serve uses, is as it was. The
  nine parts, and what each is for:
  - "default-src 'self'": whatever no other part names comes from the
    wallet's own address and from nowhere else.
  - "script-src 'self'": a script runs only when it is one of the
    proxy's own files. A script written into the page itself does not
    run, nor one from another address, nor text that is turned into
    code as the page runs (eval).
  - "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com":
    style rules come from the build's style sheet; from style blocks
    in the page, which is what 'unsafe-inline' allows (the build
    writes the fonts' rules there, and Angular and Angular Material
    write theirs as the page runs); and from Google's font style
    sheet, which a development build loads.
  - "font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com": the font files of
    Roboto and Material Symbols Outlined come from Google's font
    host.
  - "img-src 'self' data: blob:": a picture is a file of the build, a
    data: address (a selfie inside an answer; since 2026-11-22 also a
    public room's picture, 4.15) or a blob: address (a
    picture opened in the browser: src/app/images.ts, the camera, the
    recovery page, the evidence pictures of the case pages). Since
    2026-11-23 a sticker's picture, /stickers/<set>/<number> (4.16), is
    one more picture of the wallet's own address, so 'self' covers it
    and the policy is as it was.
    Since 2026-11-25 a picture that Joy had made (4.21) is one more
    picture from a blob: address, so the policy is as it was.
  - "connect-src 'self'": the page's code calls only the wallet's own
    address, where every call goes to /api.
  - "frame-ancestors 'none'": no page may show the wallet inside a
    frame, which is what "X-Frame-Options: DENY" above says too.
  - "base-uri 'self'": the page's base address, which its relative
    addresses are read from, can only be one of the wallet's own.
  - "form-action 'self'": a form can be sent only to the wallet's own
    address.
- The connections to the validators stay open (2026-11-11, section 11).
  A call to a validator goes to its doorman on a connection that is
  open and waiting when there is one, so it does not open a connection
  and set up the encryption again. The proxy closes a connection that
  sat unused for 10 seconds (validatorIdleMs in server/config.js). The
  doormen close one after 15 seconds, so the proxy is always first and
  no call meets a closing connection. The proxy keeps at most 32 unused
  connections per validator (validatorIdleConnections), in each of its
  processes. That is no limit on the calls under way: a call that finds
  no waiting connection opens a new one. A new connection has the same
  10 seconds to open, so a validator whose machine cannot be reached is
  502 { error: "validator n unavailable" } after 10 seconds, where the
  call hung for the 120. A call that is under way still has the 120.
  For this the proxy sends "Connection: keep-alive" to a validator in
  place of the "close" that nginx in front of it sends with every call.
  The masterpod, the keyholders and the signing servers get a new
  connection for every call, as before.
- The stickers' pictures (2026-11-23, section 11; 4.16). One address
  outside /api is asked of a backend: GET /stickers/<set>/<number>, in
  front of the build's files. The set's name is 1 to 32 small letters,
  digits and hyphens and the number two digits, as the masterpod has
  them; the address is taken only in exactly that form, with nothing
  after it. The proxy asks the masterpod for
  /sticker-picture/<set>/<number>, a read that needs no login, and
  sends none of the browser's headers with it, not even the three that
  go with a call under /api. Only one answer is handed on as a picture:
  a 200 that the masterpod calls image/webp. It goes to the browser as
  "Content-Type: image/webp" with its length and "Cache-Control:
  public, max-age=31536000, immutable", and with no other header of the
  masterpod's: the browser keeps the picture for a year and does not
  ask in that time whether it has changed. That is safe because a
  picture never changes under its number (4.16). Every other answer of
  the masterpod's goes on with its status and its body, as JSON when
  the masterpod said JSON and as plain text for anything else, with
  "Cache-Control: no-store": a sticker that is not there (404 { error:
  "no sticker" }), an answer of another type, an error. The browser
  does not keep such an answer and asks again the next time the picture
  is to show. The same mark stands on what the proxy answers under
  /stickers by itself: 502 { error: "masterpod unavailable" }, and 404
  { error: "Not Found", path } for an address of another form and for
  any method but GET, HEAD among them, for which the masterpod is not
  asked. The masterpod answers 304 with no body to a caller that sends
  a picture's ETag back. That never happens here: the browser's
  If-None-Match stops at the proxy with its other headers, so the
  masterpod always answers with the whole picture, and the proxy hands
  the browser no ETag to ask with. A picture carries the three safety
  headers and the page's policy, as every answer outside /api does. The
  wait and what is logged are those of every forward: 120 seconds, and
  a line for a 502.
- A message to Joy (2026-11-24, section 11; 4.18). One answer under
  /api is handed on as a stream, with a type of its own: the
  masterpod's answer to POST /api/masterpod/ask-joy. The masterpod
  writes it line by line while Joy's answer is being written, with
  status 200 and the type application/x-ndjson (its spec, section 30).
  The proxy has a forward of its own for that one path and method, in
  front of the forward of the masterpod's other paths. The request
  goes on exactly as on those: the three headers, the body streamed,
  the prefix cut, a new connection. Of the answer, a 200 that the
  masterpod calls application/x-ndjson goes to the browser as
  "Content-Type: application/x-ndjson; charset=utf-8", and with one
  header more, "X-Accel-Buffering: no". Every other answer on that
  path, a refusal with its status among them, goes on as every answer
  under /api does, JSON or plain text, without that header. The
  header is for nginx on the wallet servers. nginx collects a
  backend's answer before it sends it on, unless it is told otherwise
  (proxy_buffering, on by default), and the words of an answer would
  then show all at once at its end. With "no" in that header nginx
  hands each piece to the browser as it comes, for that one answer,
  and it does not pass the header itself on (nginx's own page on its
  proxy module, read 2026-11-24). So deploy/nginx/wallet.conf did not
  change. The proxy holds nothing back on any forward: the proxy
  library hands each piece of an answer on as it arrives. The three
  headers of every answer under /api stand on the stream too,
  "Cache-Control: no-store" among them. The two time limits of a
  forward (120 seconds) count the time in which nothing moves, and so
  do nginx's 130 seconds; the masterpod sends an empty line every 10
  seconds while an answer is under way, so an answer that takes
  minutes is not cut. When the browser goes away in the middle of an
  answer, the proxy closes its call to the masterpod, and the
  masterpod then stops its call to Anthropic. (Since 2026-11-25, the
  masterpod's spec, section 36: its call to the company whose model
  answers, Anthropic or OpenAI.)
- The signed envelope's path is the backend path: the browser signs
  "/complete-setup" and posts to /api/masterpod/complete-setup; the proxy
  strips its prefix and the masterpod sees /complete-setup.
- Nothing is logged but boot lines and 502s.

Development: proxy.conf.json sends /api to http://localhost:4300, so ng
serve on 4200 goes through the real proxy; since 2026-11-23 it sends
/stickers there too, so a development page shows the stickers'
pictures. `npm run server` starts the
proxy; `npm run build` then `npm run server` serves the built app on 4300
for a production-like check.

## 3. The signing server: the contract

Rewritten 2026-11-13 (section 11; the plan is
forclaude/signing-server-plan-1.md, its decision 42). The signing server
is a project of its own, the folder signingserver beside this one, and
from that plan on its own README.md is its spec: its two key stores, the
checks it makes before it signs with every reason, the kinds it signs,
its settings, its log lines. This section keeps what the wallet needs to
know: the two routes, the request and the answers. Until 2026-11-13 it
described the stand-in, one server with one wallet pair that signed
whatever the wallet handed it; the notes of section 11 keep that record.
Since 2026-11-20 a request also carries the passkey's answer for the
thing to sign (forclaude/second-key-and-signing-passkey-plan-1.md; 4.11
and the note in section 11). The wallet sends it from its own update on.
The signing servers read it and have the masterpod check it from their
own update on, the third step of that plan; until then they read only
`transaction` and `creation`, and what is said below of `passkey` and of
the masterpod is not in force yet.

On the network there are two signing servers, the same software on both,
holding the same wallet pairs, 100 of them; on this machine there is
one, with one pair. Only the proxy calls a signing server: it lists them
in SIGNING_SERVER_URLS and forwards /api/sign/<n> and
/api/sign/<n>/public-keys to the nth (section 2). The browser uses one
per session and asks the other when it does not answer (8.3).

    GET  /public-keys       200 { walletKey: hex (33), walletPostQuantumKey: hex (2592) }: the public keys of
                            one of the server's wallet pairs, picked at random for every call. The wallet asks
                            for every new account and puts the two keys into the creation, so an account names
                            one wallet pair for life (section 7).
    POST /sign              body { transaction: { payload: object, signatures: object },
                                   creation: { payload: object },
                                   passkey: { assertion: object, covers: [hex (32)] } }
                            transaction: what the browser built and signed with its own keys: a creation, a
                            transfer, a transferToFund, a fundProposal or a follow-up.
                            creation: the creation of the signer's account, its payload alone (about 21 KB),
                            without its eight signatures, which the server does not read. It goes with every
                            request but a creation's own: there the transaction is the creation, and the
                            body is { transaction }.
                            passkey (2026-11-20): the answer of the person's passkey for the thing to sign.
                            assertion is the WebAuthn JSON of that answer, without its PRF results, in the
                            form /unlock takes one. covers is the list of the fingerprints the answer was
                            given for, 1 to 100 of them, each the SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of a payload
                            as 64 lowercase hex characters (section 7); the fingerprint of this transaction's
                            payload is one of them. It goes with every request but a creation's own, as the
                            creation does: a new account needs no passkey answer.
                            200 { transaction }: the transaction with signatures.walletKey (64 bytes r||s
                            over the SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical bytes of payload) and
                            signatures.walletPostQuantumKey (4627 bytes, pure ML-DSA-87, empty context, over
                            the canonical bytes) set, replacing any present; everything else untouched
                            400 { error: reason }: the server does not sign, and the reason says why
                            400 passkey answer is missing: reload the wallet: a request for anything but a
                            creation came without a passkey part; a wallet page loaded before 2026-11-20
                            sends none
                            400 passkey.covers must be 1 to 100 fingerprints of 64 lowercase hex characters
                            400 the passkey answer does not cover this transaction: the fingerprint of the
                            payload is not in covers
                            400 the passkey answer was refused: <reason>: the masterpod's no, with its reason
                            503 { error: "kms unavailable" }: the server could not get the two signatures
                            from its key store; the wallet counts it as no answer and asks the other server
                            503 { error: "masterpod unavailable" }: the masterpod gave the server no answer
                            about the passkey; the wallet counts it as no answer too and asks the other
                            server, and when that was the last one it shows the sentence
                            passkeyCheck.notChecked (8.3, 8.8)

Before it signs, the server checks four things from the request alone.
The signer's account id is the SHA-256 of pair one's two public keys in
the creation sent along. The wallet pair that creation names is one of
the server's own, which is also the pair it signs with. The person's
signatures on the transaction verify: pair one's two, or on a creation
the six the browser makes. And the transaction is a kind the server
knows, with the right shape and the right id. Then, for everything but
a creation, the passkey (2026-11-20), which the masterpod checks. The
fingerprint of the transaction's payload has to be in `covers`. The
server works the passkey's challenge out again from that list (section
7) and asks the masterpod, POST /check-signing-passkey with the signer's
account id, the challenge and the assertion, whether the answer is from
a passkey of the anoPod that made the account and is an answer to that
challenge (4.11). It signs on a yes. A no of the masterpod is the 400
with the masterpod's reason; no answer from the masterpod within 4
seconds is the 503. It does not check a
balance or the previous transaction id; the validators do. So a signing
server signs only what the holder of an account's pair one has already
signed and what a passkey of the account's anoPod has answered for. A
break-glass move and its cancel are signed by the break-glass
pair alone and are never sent to a signing server, which would refuse
them.

The signer is not always the account in accountId: on a fundProposal and
a guardianVote it is guardianId, on an attestation attestorId, on an
escrowVerdict arbitratorId. The page passes the signer's account id to
signing.service, which sends that account's creation (8.3).

## 4. Masterpod changes

### 4.1 identity_blob

anopods gets one column, identity_blob BYTEA CHECK (octet_length <=
1024), and the all-or-nothing CHECK becomes num_nulls(the seven,
identity_blob) IN (0, 8). Setup complete stays "blob2 set".

POST /complete-setup (vouched) takes an eighth field, identityBlob: hex,
1 to 1024 bytes (92 in practice: PLID || lookupId under the encryption
key, section 7), checked after chatPrivateKeyBlob (400 invalid
identityBlob), written with the others.

POST /unlock answers identityBlob: hex, or null before setup, beside
blob1 and chatPrivateKeyBlob.

### 4.2 The key id on the buckets

security_images and security_info each get key_id BYTEA NOT NULL CHECK
(octet_length = 32). The two add routes take keyId: hex (32), checked
right after the body shape (400 invalid keyId), stored on every row the
request writes. /list-security-records answers keyId on every image and
info. A moderator with the shares of key keyId knows which rows it opens.

### 4.3 Status counts

POST /check-anopod-status answers three more integers: bucketOneImages,
bucketTwoImages, bucketTwoInfos, the caller's rows in each. The wallet's
next-step rule reads them (section 8.1).

Since 2026-11-08 the answer also carries role, after isSuperSeed:
"moderator", "attestor", "validator", "masterPod" or null, the pod's live
appointment (masterpod spec section 16, forclaude/appointments-plan-1.md).
The names "validator" and "masterPod" came on 2026-11-10 (masterpod spec
16.7, forclaude/validator-masterpod-stake-plan-1.md): a pod appointed
for one of them may stake for it, and the appointment opens nothing
else. The account page's Stake for list reads the role (8.2). An older
masterpod sends no role field, and the wallet then shows daoVote and
guardian only (since 2026-11-10; until then it showed all six purposes).

### 4.4 anos accounts

A new table, one row per anos account a pod made, and a feature folder
src/anos-accounts/ (router, handlers, service, queries).

    anos_accounts
    account_id    BYTEA PK (32)                     SHA-256 of key1 + postQuantumKey1, as the validators compute it
    anopod_id     BYTEA NOT NULL (32)               the pod; index on it
    account_type  TEXT NOT NULL                     spending | guarded | vault | assisted (CHECK)
    key_blob      BYTEA NOT NULL (<= 1024)          pair one and pair two's private halves under the encryption key, 156 bytes (section 7)
                                                    since 2026-11-08 under the pod's key blob key, and no longer under the encryption key (section 7)
                                                    since 2026-11-20 a second column stands beside it, first_key_blob, pair one alone: 4.11
    creation      JSONB NOT NULL                    the signed creation transaction, all eight signatures, as posted to the validator
    submitted_at  TIMESTAMPTZ                       null until a validator answered the creation
    created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
    updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), the set_updated_at trigger

No foreign keys, never deleted. The masterpod never verifies anos
signatures; the validators do.

    POST /create-anos-account (setup)
    body { accountId: hex, accountType: string, keyBlob: hex, creation: { payload, signatures } }
      since 2026-11-20 the body also carries firstKeyBlob: hex, the account's first key blob, with one check of its own: 4.11
    checks, in order: the shape (400 bad request shape); accountId 32 bytes (400 invalid accountId);
      accountType one of the four (400 invalid accountType); keyBlob 1 to 1024 bytes (400 invalid keyBlob);
      creation.payload.accountId decodes to the same 32 bytes, creation.payload.accountType equals accountType,
      creation.payload.transactionType is "accountCreation", creation.signatures has the eight string fields
      key1, postQuantumKey1, key2, postQuantumKey2, breakGlassKey, breakGlassPostQuantumKey, walletKey,
      walletPostQuantumKey (400 invalid creation); no row with this accountId (409 account already registered)
    writes: INSERT anos_accounts, submitted_at null
    answer: 201 { accountId }

    POST /mark-anos-account-submitted (setup)
    body { accountId: hex }
    checks: the shape and the id (400); a row with this accountId and this pod (404 account not found)
    writes: UPDATE submitted_at = COALESCE(submitted_at, now())
    answer: 200 { accountId, submittedAt: ISO 8601 }

    POST /list-anos-accounts (setup)
    body { }
    answer: 200 { accounts: [ { accountId, accountType, keyBlob: hex, creation, submittedAt: ISO 8601 | null, createdAt } ] },
      the caller's rows, oldest first
      since 2026-11-20 the body is { firstKeyBlobs: true }, every account also carries firstKeyOnly, and keyBlob is the
      account's first key blob once it has one: 4.11

    POST /get-anos-account (none)
    body { accountId: hex }
    checks: the shape and the id (400 bad request shape); the row (404 unknown account)
    answer: 200 { accountId, anopodId, vouched: boolean }, vouched read from the pod's row. Unsigned, like
      /get-anopod-session-keys: for the validators.

Level setup implies vouched and setup complete, which is "they are
vouched" of the flow, and the encryption key the keyBlob is under exists.
(Since 2026-11-08 the keyBlob is under the pod's key blob key, which
comes from the passkey's PRF output, and no longer under the encryption
key: section 7.)

Since 2026-11-10 the masterpod lets a pod make at most 20 new anos
accounts in the last 30 days: /create-anos-account counts the pod's rows
as its last check, after the 409, and at the limit answers 403 account
limit reached (masterpod spec section 17); the wallet says it in one
sentence and shows no counter (8.2, Wallet).

### 4.5 Applying it

db/schema.sql changes; locally `npm run db:reset` (the table changes
cannot be added by db:setup), then the genesis super seed again with
make-super-seed once the first pod exists. The README, docs/schemas.md
section 11 and the records change with the code.

### 4.6 noted_transactions

Added 2026-11-07 (forclaude/wallet-notes-plan-1.md; section 11): the
wallet's memory of what a transaction was for, on the masterpod under
the person's pod. One row per note the person made on a ledger
transaction for their tax records: the ledger's facts in the clear (the
masterpod already links a pod to its accounts and every validator holds
the chain, so they are no secret from a snooper, and in the clear they
let the database sort, cut a date range and refuse a double note) and
the private part, the kind, the money, the currency, the memo and a typed
tag, as one blob under the pod's encryption key (section 7), which the
masterpod cannot open. The masterpod learns which transactions were noted
and nothing of the money. One note per pod, transaction and account,
enforced by the database: a transfer between two of the pod's own
accounts is one transaction that stands in both accounts' histories, and
it can hold a note for each (since 2026-11-20, section 11; one note per
pod and transaction before). A note's ledger facts never change once
written, only its blob; the row is deleted when the person removes the
note. A feature folder
src/wallet-memory/ on the masterpod (router, handlers, service, the two
tables' queries), in the shape of src/anos-accounts/.

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS noted_transactions (
      note_id          BYTEA       PRIMARY KEY CHECK (octet_length(note_id) = 32),
      anopod_id        BYTEA       NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(anopod_id) = 32),
      transaction_id   BYTEA       NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(transaction_id) = 32),
      account_id       BYTEA       NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(account_id) = 32),
      other_account_id BYTEA       CHECK (octet_length(other_account_id) = 32),
      position         BIGINT      NOT NULL CHECK (position >= 0),
      transacted_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
      amount           BIGINT      NOT NULL CHECK (amount >= 0),
      sent             BOOLEAN     NOT NULL,
      note_blob        BYTEA       NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(note_blob) <= 4096),
      created_at       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
      updated_at       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
      UNIQUE (anopod_id, transaction_id, account_id)
    );
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS noted_transactions_anopod_id_transacted_at_idx ON noted_transactions (anopod_id, transacted_at DESC);

note_id is random, minted by /add-noted-transaction; anopod_id the pod
that noted it; transaction_id the transaction's id on the validators;
account_id the pod's anos account the transaction belongs to (an
anos_accounts row of the pod's); other_account_id the other side as the
wallet shows it (the receiver when the pod sent, the sender when it
received), or null when there is none; position the transaction's
position on the ledger, as /list-transactions answers it; transacted_at
when the validators wrote it (createdAt); amount millionths of an anos,
as the ledger says it; sent true when the anos left the pod's account,
false when they came in or nothing moved; note_blob the ciphertext of the
private part (iv || ciphertext || tag), at most 4096 bytes, a few hundred
in practice; created_at and updated_at as every table, with the
set_updated_at trigger.

    POST /add-noted-transaction (setup)
    body { transactionId: hex, accountId: hex, otherAccountId: hex | null, position: integer, transactedAt: ISO 8601,
           amount: decimal string of millionths, sent: boolean, noteBlob: hex }
    checks, in order: the shape (400 bad request shape: the five strings, otherAccountId a string or null, position a
      number, sent a boolean); transactionId 32 bytes (400 invalid transactionId); accountId 32 bytes (400 invalid
      accountId); otherAccountId 32 bytes when not null (400 invalid otherAccountId); position an integer of 0 or more
      (400 invalid position); transactedAt parses (400 invalid transactedAt); amount digits only that fit a BIGINT (400
      invalid amount); noteBlob 1 to 4096 bytes (400 invalid noteBlob); an anos_accounts row with this accountId and
      this pod (403 not your account); no note of this pod for this transaction and this account (409 already noted;
      until 2026-11-20 any note of the pod for the transaction refused it), the unique rule as the backstop (a unique
      violation on the insert answers the same 409)
    writes: INSERT noted_transactions with a fresh note_id
    answer: 201 { noteId }

    POST /update-noted-transaction (setup)
    body { noteId: hex, noteBlob: hex }
    checks: the shape (400 bad request shape); noteId 32 bytes (400 invalid noteId); noteBlob 1 to 4096 bytes (400
      invalid noteBlob); the row exists and is this pod's (404 note not found)
    writes: UPDATE note_blob; the ledger facts never change
    answer: 200 { noteId, updatedAt: ISO 8601 }

    POST /remove-noted-transaction (setup)
    body { noteId: hex }
    checks: the shape (400 bad request shape); noteId 32 bytes (400 invalid noteId); the row is this pod's (404 note not
      found)
    writes: DELETE the row
    answer: 200 { noteId, removed: true }

    POST /list-noted-transactions (setup)
    body { from?: ISO 8601, to?: ISO 8601 }, both optional; null counts as absent
    checks: the shape (400 bad request shape); from parses when given (400 invalid from); to parses when given (400
      invalid to)
    reads: the pod's rows with transacted_at at or after from and before to, newest transacted_at first, then the
      highest position, then, of the two notes a transfer between two of the pod's own accounts can hold, the sent
      one (since 2026-11-20), 1001 rows at most
    answer: 200 { notes: [ { noteId, transactionId, accountId, otherAccountId, position, transactedAt, amount, sent,
      noteBlob, createdAt, updatedAt } ], more: boolean }: the first 1000, and more true when a 1001st row exists

The proxy forwards them as any masterpod path (section 2): the wallet
posts to /api/masterpod/add-noted-transaction and signs
/add-noted-transaction. The wallet's side is notes.service (8.3) and the
note form on the transaction history page (8.2).

### 4.7 wallet_settings

Added 2026-11-07 (forclaude/wallet-notes-plan-1.md; section 11): one row
per pod, one encrypted JSON object holding the small things the wallet
should remember, the Protect your passkey answer first; a later thing is
one more field inside the object, with no masterpod change. Written whole
by /set-wallet-settings, which inserts the row or replaces its blob in
place; never deleted. The masterpod cannot open it.

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wallet_settings (
      anopod_id     BYTEA       PRIMARY KEY CHECK (octet_length(anopod_id) = 32),
      settings_blob BYTEA       NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(settings_blob) <= 16384),
      created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
      updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
    );

anopod_id the pod; settings_blob the ciphertext of the settings object
(iv || ciphertext || tag), at most 16384 bytes, a few dozen in practice,
under the pod's encryption key (section 7); created_at and updated_at as
every table, with the set_updated_at trigger.

    POST /get-wallet-settings (setup)
    body { }
    answer: 200 { settingsBlob: hex | null, updatedAt: ISO 8601 | null }, null before the first set

    POST /set-wallet-settings (setup)
    body { settingsBlob: hex }
    checks: the shape (400 bad request shape); settingsBlob 1 to 16384 bytes (400 invalid settingsBlob)
    writes: INSERT or UPDATE the pod's one row, whole
    answer: 200 { updatedAt: ISO 8601 }

The proxy forwards them as any masterpod path (section 2). The wallet's
side is settings.service (8.3), the setup page's Continue and the Protect
your passkey page (8.2).

### 4.8 More than one passkey

Added 2026-11-18 (forclaude/add-passkey-plan-1.md; section 11): an anoPod
can have more than one passkey, and every passkey unlocks the same anoPod
and opens the same accounts. The masterpod's side is its own spec's
section 19, which holds the table, the checks and the refusals in full;
it was deployed before the wallet's step. The first passkey stays on the
pod's anopods row: it is the main passkey, and nothing stored before
changes. A passkey added later is one row of a new table, added_passkeys:
its passkey_id (what the wallet keys the passkey's name by), the pod, the
credential id and public key, and that passkey's own two locked copies,
the pod's encryption key under its own KEK_prf (its blob1) and the pod's
key blob key under a key from its own PRF output (section 7). The
masterpod can open neither. No route removes a passkey and there is no
cap; the finish of a recovery deletes the pod's added passkeys with the
old main one, so the recovery passkey is the pod's one passkey from
there, and its main one.

    POST /challenge (none), a sixth purpose
    body { purpose: "addPasskey", anopodId: hex }, the pod the passkey is added to
    checks: those of openCase for the anoPod id (400 bad request shape, 400 invalid anopodId, 404 unknown anopod);
            addPasskey reads no lookup id, so it has none of the three checks openCase gained with 4.9
    answer: 200 { challenge, expiresAt, anopodId }; the challenge is bound to that pod, serves both passkey steps
            of an add and lives ten minutes (ADD_PASSKEY_CHALLENGE_SECONDS, 600); the other purposes keep two

    POST /list-passkeys (setup)
    body { }
    answer: 200 { main: { credentialId: hex }, added: [ { passkeyId: hex, credentialId: hex, createdAt: ISO 8601 } ] },
            the added ones oldest first; the main passkey carries no date

    POST /add-passkey (setup)
    body { challenge: hex, assertion: the WebAuthn JSON of a fresh tap of a passkey the pod has, passkey: the
           WebAuthn JSON of the new passkey's registration, blob1: hex, wrappedKeyBlobKey: hex }
    checks, in order: the shape (400 bad request shape); blob1 and wrappedKeyBlobKey 1 to 1024 bytes (400 invalid
           blob1, 400 invalid wrappedKeyBlobKey); the challenge issued for addPasskey, unexpired and bound to
           the caller's pod (401 unknown or expired challenge); no PRF output in either JSON (400 prf output in
           request) and prf.enabled in the registration (400 passkey without prf); the fresh tap by the pod's
           main passkey or one it added (401 unknown passkey; 401 user handle mismatch when the tap carries a
           user handle that is not the pod's id; 401 passkey verification failed); the registration against the
           same challenge (401 passkey verification failed); the new credential id nobody's yet (409 passkey
           already registered)
    writes: one transaction: the challenge taken (gone meanwhile: 401 unknown or expired challenge), the
           added_passkeys row, one notification of kind passkeyAdded to the pod, its reference the passkey_id
    answer: 201 { passkeyId: hex, credentialId: hex, createdAt: ISO 8601 }

    POST /unlock (none), changed
    payload: may carry addedPasskeys: true; this wallet always sends it, and a masterpod of before ignores it
    checks: the passkey is a pod's main one or one a pod added (neither: 401 unknown passkey, as before); an added
           passkey from a payload without addedPasskeys: true is 409 reload the wallet
    answer: as before, with blob1 the copy of the passkey that signed, and a new field wrappedKeyBlobKey: hex
           for an added passkey, null for the main one

The old page guard. An anoPod has one key blob key for all its accounts,
and every passkey has to arrive at that same key. A wallet page loaded
before this build does not know the locked copy of it. Unlocked with an
added passkey, it would make a second key blob key from that passkey's
PRF output, one that nothing in the anoPod is locked with: every account
would show as "Lost with the old passkey", and an account made there
would be locked under a key the main passkey cannot make. So this wallet
says addedPasskeys: true in its /unlock payload, and the masterpod
refuses an added passkey without it. An old page keeps working with the
main passkey; with an added one it shows "/unlock: HTTP 409: reload the
wallet", and a reload brings the new page.

The proxy forwards the two new routes as any masterpod path (section 2);
nothing in server/ changed. The wallet's side is the unlock flow (8.2,
Landing), the Passkeys page (8.2), the four services of 8.3
(passkey.service, session.service, settings.service and
masterpod-api.service) and the two rows of section 7.

### 4.9 The passkey check and the open case check at a case's opening

Added 2026-11-18 (forclaude/recovery-passkey-check-plan-1.md; section
11): two checks at the opening of a recovery case, both through the
/challenge request for openCase. The masterpod's side is its own spec's
section 20, which holds the rule, the checks and what the two answers
give out. The masterpod gained two things there. Its answer for openCase
carries the credential ids of the pod's passkeys, so the wallet can hand
them to the device as the exclude list of the recovery passkey: a device
that already holds one of them makes no new passkey in its place. And
the body may carry the lookup id: when a case is already open for it,
the masterpod refuses at once, before any passkey is made. That is the
question /open-recovery-case asks at its end, asked sooner; it stays the
rule there. The masterpod stores nothing for either check. No new route,
no table and no env variable; the five other purposes of /challenge are
as they were.

    POST /challenge (none), openCase changed
    body { purpose: "openCase", anopodId: hex, lookupId: hex }; the masterpod takes a body without lookupId as
           before, and this wallet always sends it
    checks, in order, the new ones marked: anopodId a string (400 bad request shape); new: lookupId, when the
           body has one, a string (400 bad request shape); anopodId 32 bytes (400 invalid anopodId); new:
           lookupId 32 bytes (400 invalid lookupId); a pod has that id (404 unknown anopod); new: no case is
           open for the lookup id (409 case already open), and at that refusal no challenge is issued and
           nothing is written
    answer: 200 { challenge, expiresAt, anopodId, username } as before, with a new field credentialIds: [hex],
           the pod's passkeys, the main one first, then the added ones, oldest first, as /list-passkeys gives
           them
    a masterpod of before: ignores the lookup id and sends no credentialIds; the wallet then hands the device
           an empty exclude list, so both checks do nothing, as before this build

The proxy forwards the request as any masterpod path (section 2);
nothing in server/ changed. The wallet's side is the two recovery pages
(12.3), passkey.service (8.3) and masterpod-api.service (12.4).

### 4.10 Seen in chat

Added 2026-11-19 (forclaude/wallet-chat-and-passkey-plan-1.md; section
11): the masterpod keeps how far each member of a chat has read, so the
wallet can say "Sent" and "Seen" under a person's own messages. Until
then nothing said whether the other person had seen a message: each
device kept its own list, for its unread dot (8.2, Unread). The
masterpod's side is its own spec's section 21, which holds the rule, the
column and the checks in full. The masterpod gained three things there.
One column, seen_position on chat_room_members: the highest message
position the member has seen in the room, 0 until that member's wallet
reports one. One route, /mark-messages-seen, by which a member's own
wallet reports it. And one field more in the answer of /list-chat-rooms:
every member of a room reads how far every other member has read. A seen
position is never lowered and never above the room's newest message. The
masterpod keeps the number alone, with no time beside it, and still
learns nothing of what a message says. No table, no env variable and no
npm package.

    POST /mark-messages-seen (setup), new
    body { chatRoomId: hex, position: integer }; position is the highest message position the caller's wallet
           has shown, a whole number from 1 to 9007199254740991
    checks, in order: the shape (400 bad request shape); chatRoomId 32 bytes (400 invalid chatRoomId); position a
           whole number in that range (400 invalid position, and a body without a position gets the same); the
           caller a member of the room (403 not a member, and a room that does not exist gets the same)
    writes: the caller's own chat_room_members row, seen_position raised to position, or to the room's newest
           message position when position is above it; a position at or below what the row holds changes
           nothing; no notification and nothing else
    answer: 200 { chatRoomId: hex, seenPosition: number }, what the row holds afterwards

    POST /list-chat-rooms (setup), one field more
    answer: every entry of a room's members is { anopodId, username, seenPosition: number }, 0 until that
           member's wallet reports one; the entries of invited and the owner of a listing stay
           { anopodId, username }; nothing else in the answer changes
    a masterpod of before: answers /mark-messages-seen with 404 { error: "Not Found", path }, as it answers any
           route it does not have, and sends no seenPosition; the wallet then stops reporting from that page and
           shows neither "Sent" nor "Seen" (8.2, Chat)

The proxy forwards the new route as any masterpod path (section 2);
nothing in server/ changed. The wallet's side is the conversation (8.2,
Chat, the paragraphs "One conversation" and "Unread") and
masterpod-api.service (8.3).

### 4.11 The first key blob, and the passkey check for the signing servers

Added 2026-11-20 (forclaude/second-key-and-signing-passkey-plan-1.md, its
step 2; section 11). Why: an anos account has three signing pairs, and
the validators take any two. Pair one and pair two are the person's own;
the third is the wallet pair, which the signing servers hold. Until then
the wallet got pair one and pair two at every login, in one blob per
account, and the key that opens that blob stays in the browser tab. And
a signing server signed for whoever showed pair one's signatures. So a
copy of what an open tab holds was enough to move the person's anos, in
two ways: with pair one and pair two and no signing server, or with pair
one and a signing server. Each half of the plan closes one of the two
ways, and neither half works alone. The first half: the masterpod keeps
the blob with both pairs as it is, and hands the wallet a new, small
blob with pair one alone, the first key blob. The second half: a signing
server signs only when a passkey answer made for the exact thing to sign
comes with the request, and it asks the masterpod whether that answer is
good (section 3). The masterpod's side is its own spec's section 22,
which holds the rule, the column and the checks in full; it is deployed
before the wallet's step, and the signing servers' step comes after the
wallet's. The masterpod gained five things there. One column,
first_key_blob on anos_accounts: null until the wallet stores it,
written once and never changed, while key_blob is never changed at all.
One route by which the wallet stores it, /store-first-key-blob. One
optional field in the body of /create-anos-account. One field in the
body and one in the answer of /list-anos-accounts, with a refusal for a
wallet page of before. And one route for the signing servers,
/check-signing-passkey. No table, no env variable and no npm package.

    POST /create-anos-account (setup), one field more
    body: as 4.4, and firstKeyBlob: hex, 1 to 1024 bytes, 92 in practice (section 7); the masterpod takes a body
           without it, and this wallet always sends it
    checks: as 4.4, with one more after the check of keyBlob: a firstKeyBlob that is there is 1 to 1024 bytes
           (400 invalid firstKeyBlob); only a body without the field counts as none
    writes: the row of 4.4, with first_key_blob the blob that was sent, or null
    answer: 201 { accountId }, as before

    POST /list-anos-accounts (setup), one field in the body, one field more in the answer, one refusal
    body { firstKeyBlobs: true }: this page can open a first key blob; a wallet page of before sends { }
    checks: the old page guard: a body that does not say firstKeyBlobs: true, from a pod one of whose accounts
           has a first key blob, is 409 reload the wallet
    answer: every account carries firstKeyOnly: boolean beside the fields of 4.4. true: keyBlob is the account's
           first key blob. false: the account has none yet, and keyBlob is the blob with both pairs, as before.
           Once an account has a first key blob, its blob with both pairs is answered to nobody
    a masterpod of before: ignores the body and sends no firstKeyOnly; the wallet then opens the blob with both
           pairs as before and stores nothing

    POST /store-first-key-blob (setup), new
    body { accountId: hex, firstKeyBlob: hex }: one of the caller's accounts, and its first key blob, 1 to 1024
           bytes
    checks, in order: the shape (400 bad request shape); accountId 32 bytes (400 invalid accountId); firstKeyBlob
           1 to 1024 bytes (400 invalid firstKeyBlob); a row with this accountId and this pod (404 account not
           found); the row has no first key blob yet (409 first key blob already stored)
    writes: first_key_blob on that row, and only where it is null; key_blob is not touched; no notification
    answer: 200 { accountId: hex }
    a masterpod of before: does not have the route, and the wallet never calls it there, since that masterpod
           says firstKeyOnly: false for no account

    POST /check-signing-passkey (none), new; a signing server calls it, the wallet never does
    body { accountId: hex, challenge: hex (32), assertion: the WebAuthn JSON of a passkey's answer }
    answer: 200 { accountId, verified: true } when the passkey that answered is one of the anoPod that made the
           account, its main one or one it added, and the answer verifies against that challenge; else a
           refusal with its reason (400 bad request shape, 400 invalid accountId, 400 invalid challenge, 400 prf
           output in request, 404 unknown account, 401 unknown passkey, 401 user handle mismatch, 401 passkey
           verification failed), which the signing server hands on in its own 400 (section 3). It reads the
           masterpod's rows and writes nothing, so an answer is not used up

The old page guard. A wallet page loaded before this build opens a key
blob as the blob with both pairs and nothing else: on a first key blob
it throws "keyBlob must open to 128 bytes, got 64", and no account would
open. So this wallet says firstKeyBlobs: true whenever it asks for the
list, and the masterpod refuses a list without it once one of the pod's
accounts has a first key blob. A person meets that when they log in on
an old page after having logged in somewhere with the new wallet: the
Wallet page and Home show "/list-anos-accounts: HTTP 409: reload the
wallet", and a reload brings the new page.

What the wallet does with each.

- A login. unlockWithPasskey (unlock.ts), the one door of every login
  (8.2, Landing), ends with storeFirstKeyBlobs when the anoPod is vouched
  and its setup is complete. It reads the list. For each account that
  comes with firstKeyOnly false it opens the blob with both pairs, wraps
  pair one's two secrets again alone (the first key blob, section 7),
  opens the new blob again, and compares its two public keys with key1
  and postQuantumKey1 in the account's creation. Only a blob that passes
  is sent to /store-first-key-blob. After a store, and after a 409, which
  says that another login stored one meanwhile, the list is read once
  more, so the session keeps first key blobs only; when nothing was
  stored, the first list is the session's. An account whose blob does
  not open (a lost account, 8.2), one whose check fails and one the
  masterpod refuses are left as they are, for the next login. The person
  sees nothing of this, and nothing of it stops a login: every failure
  is passed over. The login waits for it, so no page reads the account
  list while the blobs are being stored. It costs one short call for
  each account, once; a later login finds firstKeyOnly true and stores
  nothing.
- A new account. createAccount (account-creation.service, 8.3) makes
  both blobs in its first step and sends both to /create-anos-account in
  its fourth (8.2, Wallet).
- Every read of the list goes through masterpod-api.service's
  listAnosAccounts (8.3), which says firstKeyBlobs: true.
- Opening pair one. The field keeps its name, keyBlob, in the answer and
  in the session's account list (session.service, 8.3), with
  firstKeyOnly beside it. pairOneFromKeyBlob (crypto.service) opens both
  kinds: 64 bytes inside, pair one alone, or 128, of which the first 64
  are pair one. So the thirteen places that open pair one from keyBlob
  did not change, and the lost check of balances.service opens with it
  too.
- The passkey check. The wallet's part is the answer it sends to the
  signing server with everything but a creation: askSigningPasskey (8.9)
  and signing.service (8.3).

Two limits of the first half, told to the user when it was planned. A
copy of a tab made before a person's first login after this build
already holds both pairs of the accounts they had then. And until a
person logs in again, the masterpod still hands their old blob to their
own wallet. Nothing hands the second key out yet: the blob with both
pairs lies at the masterpod, and the screen where a person asks for it
comes later (section 10).

The proxy forwards the new route as any masterpod path (section 2);
nothing in server/ changed. The wallet's side is the unlock flow (8.2,
Landing), the Wallet page's new account (8.2), the confirmation box and
the buttons that sign (8.9), the services of 8.3 (session.service,
signing.service, passkey.service, escrow-actions.service,
masterpod-api.service and crypto.service) and the rows of section 7.

### 4.12 The listing limit

Added 2026-11-20 (forclaude/listing-limit-plan-1.md; section 11): a pod
may have at most 10 listings open at one time, selling and buying
together. Until then nothing limited how many listings one pod opens.
The masterpod's side is its own spec's section 23, which holds the rule,
the check and what is left as it is. The masterpod gained one check
there, the last one of /create-listing: in one transaction, with the
pod's own row locked, it counts the pod's open listings and refuses at
10 or more. A closed listing does not count, so closing one frees a
place at once. A pod that had more than 10 open listings on the day the
limit went live keeps every one of them, and cannot create another until
it has fewer than 10. No new route, no table, no env variable and no npm
package.

    POST /create-listing (setup), one check more
    body and answer: as before ({ side, quantity, currency, country, price }; 201 { listingId, chatRoomId: null })
    checks: those of before, in their order, so a bad price is still told as a bad price; then the new last one:
           the caller has fewer than 10 open listings, else 403 listing limit reached, and nothing is written
    a masterpod of before: never refuses for it

/list-listings did not change. Since this build the wallet sends the
offset the route always took, for Show more on the marketplace's first
page.

The proxy forwards both routes as any masterpod path (section 2);
nothing in server/ changed. The wallet's side is the New listing page
and Browse (8.2, Marketplace) and marketplace.service (8.3).

### 4.13 Security alerts

Added 2026-11-21 (forclaude/security-alerts-plan-1.md, its step 1;
section 11): the masterpod tells a pod by email and by a notification on
the phone when a transfer starts to wait in one of its guarded, vault or
assisted accounts, when a recovery is started for it and when its own
alert list changes. It learns of a waiting transfer from the validators,
whose report is that plan's step 4 and was not built when the wallet's
step was: until the validators have it, nothing sets an alert about a
transfer off. The masterpod's side is its own spec's section 25,
which holds the rules, the four tables, the routes, the sender and the
words in full; it was deployed before the wallet's step. What the wallet
uses of it: eight routes at level setup for the pod's own list,
/list-alert-settings, /add-alert-email, /confirm-alert-email,
/remove-alert-email, /keep-alert-email, /add-alert-phone,
/remove-alert-phone and /keep-alert-phone, whose bodies, answers and
refusals are in 25.3 there; four more kinds under the bell,
transferWaiting, recoveryMoveWaiting, recoveryCaseOpened and
alertSettingsChanged (25.5 there); and the facts a phone is sent, which
the wallet's worker turns into a sentence (25.7 there; 8.3 here). A
masterpod of before answers the eight routes with 404, as it answers any
route it does not have: the Security alerts page then shows that refusal
in red, and the line on an account's page does not show. The proxy
forwards the routes as any masterpod path (section 2); nothing in
server/ changed. The wallet's side is the Security alerts page, the
Account page, the Notifications page and the account page (8.2),
alerts.service, masterpod-api.service and the worker file (8.3), and the
words (8.8).

### 4.14 Public rooms: a search, and the biggest first

Added 2026-11-22 (forclaude/public-rooms-plan-1.md, its steps 1 and 2;
section 11): the masterpod's list of public rooms takes a search word
and answers the rooms with the most members first. Until then it
answered the newest first and took no word, and the wallet showed the 50
newest rooms and no others. The masterpod's side is its own spec's
section 26, which holds the rule, the read and what is left as it is.
The masterpod gained one optional field there, `search`, on
/list-public-chat-rooms: a room fits when its name holds the word
anywhere, capital and small letters alike; `%` and `_` mean themselves;
the spaces around the word are taken off, and an empty word means no
search. The order is the most members first, then the newest, then the
room's id, with and without a word. A room's name stays free: two rooms
may carry one name. No new route, no table, no env variable and no npm
package.

    POST /list-public-chat-rooms (setup), one field more and a new order
    body: { limit, offset, search }, all optional; limit 50 by default and at most 200, offset 0;
          search a word of at most 100 characters, matched anywhere in a room's name
    answer: as before (200 { rooms: [ { chatRoomId, name, creator: profile, memberCount, createdAt } ] }),
            the rooms with the most members first, then the newest
    checks: those of before, in their order (400 invalid limit, 400 invalid offset), then the new last one:
            400 invalid search, for a word of more than 100 characters or a value that is not a string
    a masterpod of before: does not read the word, so nothing is narrowed, and answers the newest first

(Since the picture's step of the same day, 4.15, each room of that
answer also carries `pictureAt`, after `name`.)

The proxy forwards the route as any masterpod path (section 2); nothing
in server/ changed. The wallet's side is New chat (8.2, Chat) and
masterpod-api.service (8.3).

### 4.15 A public room's picture

Added 2026-11-22 (forclaude/public-rooms-plan-1.md, its steps 3 and 4;
section 11): a public room can have a picture. Its creator sets it, and
everyone who can read the room's name can see it. Until then a room had
no picture, and the wallet drew a grey disc with a globe for every
public room. The masterpod's side is its own spec's section 27, which
holds the rule, the table, the two routes and what is left as it is. The
masterpod gained three things there. One table, `chat_room_pictures`,
with at most one row per room and the picture in the clear, like the
room's name. Two routes at level setup, one that sets a room's picture
and one that reads it. And one field more per room, `pictureAt`, in the
answers of /list-chat-rooms and /list-public-chat-rooms: when the room's
picture was last set. The picture itself never travels inside a list.
Only the creator of a public room sets its picture, and can put another
in its place at any time; no route takes a picture away. A picture is
at most 320 pixels wide and high and at most 100,000 bytes there. No env
variable and no npm package.

    POST /set-chat-room-picture (setup), new
    body: { chatRoomId, picture: { contentType, image } }; contentType is image/jpeg, image/png or
          image/webp, image the bytes as base64
    answer: 200 { chatRoomId, pictureAt }, pictureAt an ISO 8601 string, the value the two lists then
            carry for the room; the same picture sent again answers the pictureAt of before
    checks, in order: 400 bad request shape; 403 only the creator sets the picture (also for a room
            that does not exist); 400 only a public room has a picture; 400 invalid picture: <why>
            (not one of the three types, more than 100,000 bytes, bytes that do not begin as a
            picture of their type, or more than 320 pixels wide or high)
    a masterpod of before: 404, as for any route it does not have

    POST /get-chat-room-picture (setup), new
    body: { chatRoomId }
    answer: 200 { chatRoomId, picture: { contentType, image }, pictureAt }
    checks, in order: 400 bad request shape; 404 room not found (also for a room that is not
            public); 404 no picture
    the caller need not be a member of the room
    a masterpod of before: 404, as for any route it does not have

    POST /list-chat-rooms and POST /list-public-chat-rooms (setup), one field more
    answer: as before, and each room carries pictureAt after name: an ISO 8601 string, or null for a
            room without a picture; in /list-chat-rooms it is null on every room that is not public,
            and the invites and the join requests carry none
    a masterpod of before: sends no pictureAt, which the wallet reads as null: no picture, no read

The proxy forwards the routes as any masterpod path (section 2); nothing
in server/ changed but the words of one comment (section 11). The
wallet's side is the chat list, the conversation and New chat (8.2,
Chat), room-picture-cache.service and masterpod-api.service (8.3), and
the room's round mark (8.6).

### 4.16 Stickers

Added 2026-11-23 (forclaude/stickers-database-plan-1.md, its steps 1
and 2; section 11): the wallet's chat has stickers, as LINE has them. A
sticker is a picture, still or moving, that the team makes; stickers are
free and the same for everybody. They are kept in the masterpod's
database, the pictures too. Until then the chat had text alone. The
masterpod's side is its own spec's section 28, which holds the three
tables, the two reads, the script that puts a set in and what is left
as it is. The masterpod gained three things there. Three tables:
`sticker_sets` (a set's name and its place in the row of sets),
`stickers` (a sticker's set, its number, its place in the set and its
picture) and `sticker_tags` (the words that bring a sticker up while a
person types). One read at level setup that lists every set, text only.
And one read with no login that hands out one picture, the masterpod's
first GET that hands out data. A set comes into the database by a
script that the operator runs on a masterpod server (`npm run stickers
-- look <folder>` and `-- write <folder>`); no route writes a sticker.
No env variable and no npm package.

    POST /list-stickers (setup), new
    body: {}
    answer: 200 { sets: [ { name, stickers: [ { number, tags: [ ... ] } ] } ] }: every set in the order of
            the row of sets, each set's stickers in their order, each sticker with its number and its tags;
            the tags in small letters; a set without a sticker is left out; no set at all: { sets: [] };
            about 23 KB for 200 stickers
    checks: the session's, as for every route at level setup
    a masterpod of before: 404, as for any route it does not have

    GET /sticker-picture/<set>/<number> (no login), new
    answer: 200, Content-Type image/webp, the picture's bytes; an ETag of its own, and 304 with no body
            to a caller that sends that ETag back as If-None-Match; no Cache-Control
    a sticker that is not there, and a name or a number that cannot be one: 404 { error: "no sticker" }
    an address with a part more or less, and any method but GET: the masterpod's plain 404
            { error: "Not Found", path }
    a masterpod of before: that plain 404

A set's name is 1 to 32 small letters, digits and hyphens. A sticker's
number is two digits, 01 to 99. A picture is WebP, at most 150,000
bytes and at most 370 by 320 pixels. A picture never changes under its
number: a sticker that is drawn again gets a new number. That rule is
what lets a phone keep a picture for a year (below).

A sticker that somebody sends is no new kind of message. It is an
ordinary chat message, sent with /send-message and encrypted like any
other, whose whole text is the sticker's code:

    [sticker:<set>/<number>]          for example [sticker:bun/07]

The masterpod stores it as it stores every message and cannot tell it
from a text. The reader's wallet draws the picture from that text
alone: it needs no list for it (8.2, Chat; src/app/stickers.ts).

The wallet asks for the list once after each login, when a conversation
is first opened: /list-stickers through the proxy, as any masterpod
path (section 2), signed like every chat call, and quiet. It keeps the
answer in the page's memory until the login ends. There is no timer. A
read that is refused or not answered keeps nothing, and the next
conversation that is opened asks again (stickers.service, 8.3). The
list is for what the wallet offers: the smiling face in front of the
message box, the stickers under the message box, and the suggestions
while a person types. While the masterpod has no set, the wallet shows
none of the three and the chat looks as it did before. A set that is
put in while a wallet is open shows in that wallet after its next
login; a sticker of that set that somebody sends to it is drawn at
once, since a picture needs no list.

A picture does not come through /api. Every answer under /api is JSON
or plain text that a browser may not keep (section 2), and a picture on
a page is fetched by its address alone, with nothing signed. So the
proxy has one address outside /api for it (section 2):

    GET /stickers/<set>/<number>      for example /stickers/bun/07
    asked of the masterpod as GET /sticker-picture/<set>/<number>, with none of the browser's headers
    the masterpod's 200 image/webp: handed on as image/webp, with its length and
            "Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable" (a year), and no other header of the masterpod's
    any other answer of the masterpod's, a sticker that is not there among them: handed on with its status
            and its body, as JSON or plain text, with "Cache-Control: no-store"
    a masterpod that cannot be reached: 502 { error: "masterpod unavailable" }, "no-store"
    an address of another form under /stickers, and any method but GET: 404 { error: "Not Found", path },
            "no-store", and the masterpod is not asked

A phone fetches a picture when it is about to show it, keeps it for a
year, and does not ask in that time whether it has changed. An answer
that is no picture is not kept, so the picture is asked for again the
next time it is to show. The question "has it changed?" never reaches
the masterpod: the proxy passes none of the browser's headers on
(If-None-Match among them) and hands the browser no ETag to ask with,
so the masterpod always answers with the whole picture, and its 304
never comes into play. Both wallet servers hand out the same picture
from the one database. nginx on the wallet servers hands every such
address to the proxy and adds no keep time of its own
(deploy/nginx/wallet.conf, `location /`), so that file did not change,
and the doormen in front of the masterpod pass a GET as they pass a
POST.

The wallet's side is the conversation and the chat list (8.2, Chat),
stickers.service, session.service and masterpod-api.service (8.3), the
words (8.8), and src/app/stickers.ts.

### 4.17 The chat list: only what is new

Added 2026-11-24 (forclaude/chat-list-plan-1.md, its steps 1 and 2;
section 11): the wallet's read of the chat list of every 5 seconds gets
only what is new. Until then every such read got the whole list: every
chat with this pod's wrapped key and every member, 21.8 KB for a person
with five chats of two people and 55 KB with nine such chats and a room
of 100 people, counted from the form of the answer. The user,
2026-11-23: "Usually the user's phone would check to see if there's new
data it doesn't have and grab that." The masterpod's side is its own
spec's section 29, which holds the rule, the counter, the numbers and
their triggers, the two reads and what is left as it is. The masterpod
gained four things there. One counter in its database, the sequence
`chat_change_seq`. Five numbers on four tables that take the counter's
next value when something of a chat list changes, set by triggers. One
field more in the body of /list-chat-rooms, `since`, and two in its
answer, `seq` and `counts`. And one field more in the body of
/list-messages, `seenSince`, and with it two in its answer, `seen` and
`seenSeq`. No new route, no table, no env variable and no npm package.

    POST /list-chat-rooms (setup), one field more in the body and two in the answer
    body: {} or { since }; since is the seq of the answer the wallet last put into its list, a whole number
          from 0 to 9007199254740991; a body without it, or with null, asks for everything; a since of 0 is
          a since
