    answer: 200 { seq, counts: { rooms, invites, joinRequests }, rooms, invites, joinRequests }
            seq: the highest number among the caller's own rooms, invites and join requests, 0 when there
                 is none; the number to send as the next since; it can be lower than the since that was sent
            counts: how many rooms, open invites and open join requests the caller has now
            without since: the three lists whole, as before (8.2, Chat), with seq and counts in front
            with since: rooms holds only the rooms that changed after it, in the whole list's order. An
                 entry is a room whole (it has type, hpkeKey, members and the rest) when its people or its
                 facts changed: a member joined or left, an invite was made or answered, its picture was
                 set, its listing was closed. It is { chatRoomId, lastMessage, lastPosition } when only a
                 message came. invites and joinRequests hold the ones written after since, the oldest
                 first. What was taken away is not named.
            nothing new: {"seq":9120,"counts":{"rooms":10,"invites":0,"joinRequests":0},"rooms":[],
                 "invites":[],"joinRequests":[]}, 105 bytes
    checks: those of before, then 400 invalid since
    a masterpod of before: does not read since, and answers the whole list with no seq and no counts

    POST /list-messages (setup), one field more in the body and, with it, two in the answer
    body: { chatRoomId, afterPosition, beforePosition, limit, seenSince }; seenSince is optional: 0 when
          the conversation is opened, then the seenSeq of the answer before
    answer with seenSince: 200 { messages, seen: [ { anopodId, seenPosition } ], seenSeq }
            seen: the members of the room whose seen position changed after seenSince, the caller's own
                 among them; with 0 every member who has seen anything (a member still at 0 is left out)
            seenSeq: the number to send as the next seenSince, 0 when no member has seen anything; it can
                 be lower than the seenSince that was sent
    answer without seenSince: 200 { messages }, as before
    checks: those of before, and 400 invalid seenSince, after limit and before the member check
    a masterpod of before: does not read seenSince, and answers { messages }

What the wallet does with it (chat.service, 8.3). It keeps the chat list
in memory, session.chatRooms, as before, and a number beside it,
session.chatRoomsSeq: the `seq` of the answer that was last put into the
list.

- The read of the whole list. The first read after a page load or a
  login carries no `since`, and its answer is the list. So is the read
  after a person's own action: accept, decline, approve, a new chat, an
  invite, Leave, a room's picture, Connect in the marketplace (the
  nineteen calls of `refreshRooms()`). Such an action can take things
  out of the list, and one read of the whole list is the plain way to
  drop them. It happens once for each tap.
- The read of what is new (`refreshNews()`). The shell's read of every 5
  seconds (8.1; 8.2, Notifications) and the Chat page's read at its
  opening (8.2, Chat) carry `since`. What comes back is put into the
  list. A room that came whole takes the place of the one the list
  holds, or goes to the front when the list does not hold it; several
  new rooms stay in the answer's order, the newest first. Three fields
  change that room's newest message and position. An invite or a join
  request goes to the end, or takes the place of the one with its id.
  When nothing came, the list is not set anew, so nothing that draws
  from it is worked out again.
- The count. After that the wallet counts its list. It reads the whole
  list, once, in three cases: a count differs from `counts`, which
  means that something was taken away that no answer names (a chat was
  left, an invite or a request was answered); three fields came for a
  room the list does not hold; `seq` is below the `since` that was sent
  (the entry that held the highest number is gone, or the database was
  put back from a backup). Otherwise `seq` is the list's next number.
  When that read of the whole list fails, the number stays, and the
  next read asks with the same `since` again.
- Answers in another order. An answer to a read with `since` is put in
  only while the list's number is still that `since`. Otherwise it is
  dropped: a read of the whole list came in between, and the next read
  brings whatever the dropped one held.
- A masterpod of before. An answer with no `seq` is the whole list and
  is taken as that, and the list then has no number, so the next read
  asks for the whole list. That is also a masterpod server that still
  runs the old code during the masterpod's own deploy: the wallet then
  reads as it read before this step, until an answer carries `seq`
  again.
- The seen positions. They leave the 5-second read. The open
  conversation's own read brings them (8.2, Chat, "One conversation"):
  its opening read asks with `seenSince` 0, each later read with the
  `seenSeq` of the answer before, and `seen` is written into the room's
  entry of the list in memory (`putSeen()`), where the conversation
  reads the positions for "Seen" and "Seen by" as before. An entry for
  a pod that the list does not hold as a member of the room is passed
  over; that room comes whole with the next read of the list. A room
  that comes whole still carries every member's position of that
  moment. In the list a member's position is only ever raised: an
  answer of the chat list can arrive after a newer answer of the
  conversation's read, and that read hands a position out only once.
  The masterpod itself never lowers one.
- The words that depend on today's date. A row of the chat list words
  its time by today's date ("14:32", "Yesterday", a weekday, a date),
  and a conversation writes "Today" and "Yesterday" over its days.
  Until this step those words were drawn again every 5 seconds, as a
  side effect of the list being set anew. Now that the list is set
  only when something in it changed, chat.service keeps the local
  calendar day as a signal, `today`. Every read of what is new looks at
  the clock, and the chat list's rows and the conversation's thread
  read the signal, so the words follow a change of the day within 5
  seconds, as before, with nothing else set anew. The plan does not
  name this: it is what its rule "when nothing came, the list in memory
  is not set anew" took away, seen in a trial and put back (section
  11).
- A read that is refused or not answered changes nothing, and the next
  one asks again.

What a person sees: nothing new on the screen. The unread dot, the bold
row, the number on the Chat entry of the menu, the sound, a row's line
and the order of the rows, a new chat, an invite or a request that
shows with no reload, the titles and the names are all drawn from the
same list by the same code. "Seen" and "Seen by" follow within 3
seconds, where it was 5. What changes is what travels down to the
phone: about 100 bytes every 5 seconds while nothing is new, about 540
once for a new message, and one room whole once when its people or
facts change. What goes up is as before: three signed requests every 5
seconds, about 9.6 KB each (section 10).

The proxy forwards both routes as any masterpod path (section 2);
nothing in server/ changed, and no request was added, so the doormen
count the same calls as before. The wallet's side is the shell's poll
(8.1; 8.2, Notifications), the chat list and the conversation (8.2,
Chat), and chat.service, session.service and masterpod-api.service
(8.3).

### 4.18 Joy, the wallet's AI

Added 2026-11-24 (section 11). There is no plan file: the talk with the
user is the plan, and its work note is
forclaude/notes/project-wallet-ai-joy.md. A member chats with an AI in
the wallet, named Joy, as with any AI chat. The user: "Basically
they're getting AI for free. They can use it for whatever the hell they
would use the free version of CHATgpt for." And: "I want this to be
cool, not just cheap." The answers are written by a model of the
company Anthropic, Claude Haiku 5.5, which the masterpod calls for
every message. The masterpod's side is its own spec's section 30, which
holds the rules, the two tables, the three routes, the request to
Anthropic, Joy's two tools for the memory file, the shared memory file
and what is left as it is. The masterpod gained there: two tables
(`joy_memories`, a member's memory file as a blob it cannot open, and
`joy_usage`, a count of messages and tokens for each pod and day),
three routes at level setup, five env variables, one file of text and
one npm package. The wallet gained no package and no env variable.
(Since 2026-11-25, the masterpod's spec, section 36: the model that
writes the answers is Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5 or OpenAI's GPT-6.2
Sol, by a setting of the masterpod, and Anthropic's when the setting is
not there. The wallet does not change for it: the three routes, the
request and the stream are as written here, and a chat that is open when
the company changes goes on, since the wallet sends the words of the
chat with every message.)

    POST /get-joy-memory (setup), new
    body: {}
    answer: 200 { memoryBlob, updatedAt }: the blob the wallet stored, hex, and when; both null before
            the first store
    a masterpod of before: 404, as for any route it does not have

    POST /set-joy-memory (setup), new
    body: { memoryBlob }: hex, 1 to 32768 bytes
    answer: 200 { updatedAt }; the blob takes the place of the one before
    refusals: 400 bad request shape, 400 invalid memoryBlob

    POST /ask-joy (setup), new
    body: { messages: [ { role: "user" | "assistant", text } ], memory }: the conversation, oldest first,
          the member's new message last, and the opened memory file as text
    refusals, each as JSON with its status, before anything is sent to Anthropic:
            400 bad request shape
            400 invalid messages (1 to 200 messages, each with a role and a text that is more than spaces,
                the first and the last the member's)
            400 conversation too long (the texts together over 120,000 bytes of UTF-8)
            400 memory too long (over 10,240 bytes of UTF-8)
            503 joy is off (the masterpod has no key for Anthropic)
            429 daily limit reached (the pod has sent its 300 messages of the day, a day of UTC)
    answer: 200, Content-Type application/x-ndjson, a stream of lines, each one JSON object:
            { "text": "..." }                                a piece of Joy's answer, as it is written
            { "done": true, "stop": "end" | "length" | "refused", "memory": "<the whole file>" | null }
                                                             the last line of an answer that ended
            { "error": "joy busy" | "joy unavailable" | "joy was cut off" }
                                                             the last line of an answer that failed
            an empty line may stand between two lines and means nothing; the masterpod writes one every
            10 seconds while an answer is under way
            since 2026-11-24 (4.20): one kind of line more, { "searching": true }, each time Joy starts a
            web search, and one field more in the last line of an answer that ended, `sources`
            since 2026-11-25 (4.21): two kinds of line more, { "drawing": true }, each time Joy starts on
            a picture, and { "picture": { type, data, description } }, one line with a picture that was
            made
            since 2026-11-25 (the masterpod's spec, section 36): the model that answers is Anthropic's or
            OpenAI's, by a setting of the masterpod. The request, the refusals and the stream are the same;
            "joy is off" then means that the masterpod has no key for the company that answers
    a masterpod of before: 404

What leaves the wallet. A message to Joy is the one thing in the wallet
that a member writes and the masterpod reads. The conversation and the
opened memory file travel in the clear inside the signed request, pass
through the masterpod's memory and go to Anthropic, whose model reads
them to write the answer. The masterpod writes neither into a table or
a log (its spec, 30.2). The Joy page says so in one line that always
stands under its header: "Joy is an AI. What you write to her leaves
your wallet to be answered." The page of the memory file says the same
of the file (8.2, Joy). (Since 2026-11-24, 4.20: Joy can search the
web. For a search she writes a query, which can hold words of the
member's message, and the query goes to a search engine that Anthropic
uses. What the wallet sends is as before, and the one line stays as it
is.)
(Since 2026-11-25, 4.21: Joy can have a picture made. For a picture, a
description that Joy wrote from the chat goes from the masterpod to a
second company, OpenAI. What the wallet sends is as before, with one
thing more in it, a note of the wallet's in front of an earlier answer
that had a picture. The one line stays as it is.) (Since 2026-11-25, the
masterpod's spec, section 36: the conversation and the memory file go to
the company whose model answers, to Anthropic or to OpenAI, by a setting
of the masterpod. The wallet cannot tell which: it sends the same
request and reads the same stream. The one line names no company and
stays as it is.)

The chat. There is one chat with Joy at a time, and the wallet holds
it: joy.service (8.3) keeps its messages in the page's memory, so an
answer that is being written goes on while the member looks at another
page of the wallet. A message to Joy carries the chat's newest messages,
oldest first: as many as fit the masterpod's limits, 200 messages and
120,000 bytes of text, and the first of them the member's. A message
with no text is left out (an answer that was refused or failed before
a word of it came). So in a chat that has outgrown those limits Joy no
longer reads the oldest messages; the chat on the screen is not cut,
and the member is not told. A new message that is over 120,000 bytes by
itself is not sent: the page says so (below).

The chat survives a reload. After the member's own message, and again
after each answer of Joy's, the wallet encrypts the whole chat with the
anoPod encryption key (`wrapJson`, section 7, as a note's private part
and the wallet settings are) and puts the blob into the browser's own
database, IndexedDB, the wallet's first use of it:

    database    anopod-wallet, version 1
    place       joy-chat (an object store), one entry for each pod
    key         the anoPod's id, hex
    value       the blob as bytes: iv || ciphertext || tag of the JSON
                { v: 1, messages: [ { role: "user" | "assistant", text, at, end? } ] }
                at: when the message was sent, or when the answer ended (ISO 8601)
                end: only on an answer that did not end as an answer should: "length", "refused" or "cut"
                since 2026-11-24 (4.20) a message can have one field more, sources: only on an answer of
                Joy's for which she cited web pages
                since 2026-11-25 (4.21) the database is version 2 and has a second place, joy-pictures,
                and a message can have one field more, picture: only on an answer of Joy's for which
                a picture was made

When a Joy page opens for the first time in a login, the wallet reads
the pod's entry and opens it. A blob that does not open under this
anoPod encryption key is passed over, and the chat starts empty. After
a Lock or a reload the blob stays in the browser, and nothing reads it
without the passkey, which is what brings the encryption key back.
New chat empties the chat and takes the entry out. The chat is in this
browser on this device only: the masterpod keeps none of it, another
phone does not have it, and a browser may clear its database by itself.
Where a browser refuses its database, the chat lives in the page's
memory alone and a reload loses it. Each person who logs in on one
browser has an entry of their own. Saved chats, kept on the masterpod
with a title, are the next build (section 10).
(Since 2026-11-25, 4.21: the pictures that Joy had made for the chat are
kept beside it, each as an entry of its own in a second place of the
same database, and New chat takes them out with the chat.)

The memory file. It is what Joy knows of a member from earlier chats:
plain text of at most 10,240 bytes. The masterpod stores it as a blob
it cannot open, the wallet's `wrapJson` of `{ v: 1, text }` under the
anoPod encryption key, hex, as it stores the wallet settings (4.7). The
wallet reads the blob with /get-joy-memory each time a Joy page opens,
unless an answer is under way, and opens it; no blob yet is an empty
file, and so is a blob that does not open. It sends the opened text as
`memory` with every message. Joy changes the file on the masterpod with
her two tools (its spec, 30.6), and when the last line of an answer
carries `memory`, that is the whole file after her changes: the wallet
takes it as the file, encrypts it and stores it with /set-joy-memory,
before the next message can be sent. A store that fails is said in red,
the wallet goes on with the new file, and the file is stored again
with the next answer. No message is sent before the file has been read
once in the login: an answer could otherwise put a new file in the
place of one the wallet never saw. The member reads the file, changes
it and empties it on its own page (8.2, Joy).

The stream. The answer is meant to reach the browser as the masterpod
writes it: through the doormen in front of the masterpod (HAProxy,
whose settings, as the file they are built from has them, hold no line
that collects or compresses an answer), through the proxy, which hands
this one answer on as a stream (section 2), and through nginx, which
that answer tells not to collect it. What of that was tried, and what
was only read, is in section 11. The browser
reads it with its own `fetch`, piece by piece, where every other call
of the wallet goes through Angular's HttpClient, which hands an answer
over only when it has ended (log.service's `postLines`, 8.3). The
wallet gives an answer up when nothing at all has come for 60 seconds
(JOY_SILENCE_MS): the masterpod's empty lines come every 10, so that
long a silence means a dead connection, and without the limit a phone
that lost its connection would show "Joy is writing…" for good.

What a member is told (the words are in 8.8). A message that the
masterpod refuses, and one whose answer fails before any of it came,
is taken out of the chat again and its text put back into the message
box, with the reason in red above the box:

    503 joy is off                 "Joy is switched off right now. Try again later."
    429 daily limit reached        "You have sent Joy as many messages as an anoPod may send in one day. You can
                                   write to her again after 7:00 AM." The time is the end of the masterpod's day,
                                   midnight UTC, on the member's own clock: 07:00 in Thailand
    400 conversation too long      "This message is too long for Joy. Shorten it, or send it in parts." The wallet
                                   says it by itself, without asking the masterpod, for a new message of more
                                   than 120,000 bytes; the rest of a conversation it cuts (above)
    400 memory too long            "Joy's memory of you is too long. Open Memory and take some lines out." The
                                   wallet says it by itself for a file over 10,240 bytes
    any other refusal              as the wallet shows every refusal: "/ask-joy: HTTP 403: setup not complete"
    { error: "joy busy" }          "Joy is busy right now. Try again in a moment."
    { error: "joy unavailable" }   "Joy cannot answer right now. Try again later."
    { error: "joy was cut off" }   "Joy's answer was cut off. Send your message again." Also for an answer that
                                   ended with no last line, and for one the wallet gave up after 60 seconds

An answer that failed after a part of it had come keeps that part in
the chat, with the last of those sentences under it in grey. Under an
answer that ended with another `stop` than `end` stands a grey line
too:

    stop: "length"                 "Joy reached the longest answer she can give, so this one stops here. Ask her to
                                   go on."
    stop: "refused"                "Joy did not answer this. Try asking in another way."

Decided while building, each a small thing the talk had not named:

- The Joy entry stands in the side list after Chat, with the icon
  `auto_awesome`, for every pod whose setup is complete, in all three
  editions: the list of such a pod is the same in each, and the
  masterpod's routes ask for no more than level setup.
- The memory file has a page of its own, /joy/memory, reached by Memory
  on the Joy page, so a phone's Back goes from it to the chat.
- New chat and Delete all each ask in the confirmation box first (8.9),
  since neither can be undone. The talk named neither question.
- The conversation is cut from its oldest end, anew at every message.
- The two blobs' forms and the names in IndexedDB, above.
- The 60 seconds of silence, above.
- The memory file is read at every opening of a Joy page, not once in a
  login as the wallet settings are, so a line that Joy saved on another
  device is there the next time the tab is opened.
- The Log's entry for /ask-joy holds the status and two numbers and no
  text (8.3).

Left as it is:

- A chat that has outgrown the masterpod's limits loses its oldest
  messages for Joy without a word to the member.
- The member's own message is kept when it is sent, and Joy's answer
  when it has ended: a reload in the middle of an answer loses that
  answer, and the chat comes back with the member's message last.
  (Since 2026-11-25, 4.21: a picture that had come for that answer is
  then an entry that no chat names, until New chat.)
- An answer cannot be stopped by the member.
- The memory file is the last one written (the masterpod's spec,
  30.10): two devices that write to Joy within the same minutes can
  lose a line that one of them saved.
- Joy's words are plain text: nothing is read as Markdown, and a web
  address in an answer is no link. (Since 2026-11-24, 4.20: the web
  pages Joy cited for an answer stand under it as links. An address in
  her own words is still no link.)

The proxy has one forward more for this (section 2), and nothing under
deploy/ changed. The wallet's side is the two Joy pages (8.1; 8.2,
Joy), joy.service, masterpod-api.service, log.service and
navigation.service (8.3), and the words (8.8).

### 4.19 A person edits and deletes their own chat messages

Added 2026-11-24 (forclaude/chat-edit-delete-plan-1.md, FINAL on the
user's word, its steps 1 and 2; section 11): in a chat a person gives a
message of their own a new text, or deletes it, and the others in the
chat see the new text, or a line that a message was deleted. The user,
in the talk that settled it: "In the marketplace, editing and deleting
of chats must be disabled, because those chats could end up being
evidence. I believe we don't have edits or deletes open on the chats,
so what we might have to do instead, is hide editied or deleted chats
so they don't show in the wallet, and the edited chat just replaces the
old one in the chat box." So an edit or a delete changes no row on the
masterpod: it is a new row of the chat, with a position of its own,
which names the message it is about. The masterpod's side is its own
spec's section 31, which holds the rule, the two columns, the check and
the index, the two routes, the changes of the two reads and what is
left as it is. The masterpod gained there: two columns on
`chat_room_messages` (`kind`, which is `edit` or `delete`, and
`target_message_id`), two routes at level setup, two fields more on
every row of /list-messages and a new form of `lastMessage` in
/list-chat-rooms. No table, no env variable and no npm package. The
wallet gained no package and no env variable either.

    POST /edit-message (setup), new
    body: { chatRoomId, messageId, message }: the message to edit, and the new text's ciphertext under
          the room key, base64 of 1 to 65536 bytes, as for /send-message
    answer: 201 { messageId, position }: the id and the position of the new row
    refusals, the first check that fails:
            400 bad request shape, 400 invalid chatRoomId, 400 invalid messageId,
            400 message must be base64 of 1 to 65536 bytes
            403 not a member
            403 editing and deleting are off in this chat (a chat about a listing, an old marketplace
                room, a chat about an attestor case)
            404 message not found (no message of that chat; the id of an edit or of a delete is none)
            403 not your message
            409 message deleted
            409 too late to edit (more than 15 minutes after the message was sent, by the database's
                clock; a second edit counts from the message too)
    a masterpod of before: 404, as for any route it does not have

    POST /delete-message (setup), new
    body: { chatRoomId, messageId }
    answer: 201 { messageId, position }: the id and the position of the new row
    refusals: those of /edit-message, without the 400 about `message` and without too late to edit: a
            delete has no time limit
    a masterpod of before: 404

    POST /list-messages (setup), two fields more on every row, and rows that are no message
    answer: as before (8.2, Chat; 4.17); `messages` holds every row of the room in the order of
            position, each { messageId, position, senderAnopodId, message, createdAt, kind,
            targetMessageId }
            kind: null on a message, "edit" or "delete" on a row about one
            targetMessageId: the message an edit or a delete is about; null on a message
            message: the ciphertext, or null once a later row of the room names the same message: a
                 message that was edited or deleted, an edit that a newer edit or a delete followed,
                 and every delete. The masterpod hands the old ciphertext to nobody any more.
            afterPosition, beforePosition and limit count every row
    a masterpod of before: sends neither field, and every row is a message with its ciphertext

    POST /list-chat-rooms (setup), `lastMessage` in a new form
    lastMessage: the room's newest message as it stands now, never an edit or a delete:
            { messageId, position, senderAnopodId, message, createdAt, editPosition, deleted }
            messageId, position, senderAnopodId, createdAt: the message's own, which no edit and no
                 delete moves
            message: the newest edit's ciphertext for a message that was edited, null for one that was
                 deleted
            editPosition: the position of the newest edit, null for a message that was never edited;
                 it stays what it was when an edited message is deleted
            deleted: true once a delete names the message; a deleted newest message stays the room's
                 lastMessage
    lastPosition: the highest position of any row of the room, as before: above lastMessage.position
            whenever the room's newest row is an edit or a delete, of the newest message or of an
            older one
    a masterpod of before: sends neither editPosition nor deleted

What the wallet does with it (8.2, Chat, "Edit and delete"; 8.3).

- Where a message has a menu. A tap on a bubble, a click on a computer,
  opens a small menu at the bubble when four things hold: the chat is
  none of the three kinds where the masterpod refuses (the chat's entry
  has no `listingId` and no `caseId`, and its `type` is not
  `marketplace`), the message is this pod's own, it has been sent, and
  it is not deleted. So the menu shows only where the masterpod would
  say yes. Its entries are Edit and Delete. Edit is in it only for a
  text that opened and is no sticker, and only for 15 minutes after the
  message's `createdAt`, by this device's clock (`EDIT_MINUTES` in
  chat-room.page.ts, the masterpod's own number). The masterpod decides
  by its own clock.
- Edit. The message's text goes into the message box, under a line
  "Editing a message". Send, or the Enter key, encrypts the box's text
  with the room key, as a message's, and sends it with /edit-message.
  From the 201 the bubble shows the new text and the word "edited" at
  once, in its place, and the edit ends. An unchanged text sends nothing
  and ends the edit; an empty box sends nothing. What the box held
  before Edit was tapped goes back into it when the edit ends. The box
  keeps the text until the masterpod has answered; when the person
  typed on meanwhile, the edit does not end with the answer: the box
  keeps what they typed, and the next Send saves it.
- Delete. The wallet asks once, with the confirmation box (8.9), and
  then sends /delete-message. From the 201 the grey line "This message
  was deleted" stands in the message's place at once.
- Two refusals have a sentence of the wallet's own, in the conversation's
  red line above the message box. `409 too late to edit`: "This message
  can no longer be edited."; the edit ends and the text stays in the
  box. `409 message deleted`, for an edit or a delete of a message that
  was deleted meanwhile from another device of the same person: "This
  message was already deleted."; the text of an edit stays in the box,
  and the grey line shows with the read that follows. Every other
  refusal shows as the page shows one, and an edit then goes on.
- The rows of an open conversation. The page's reads are the ones of
  before: the room's newest 50 rows when it opens, the 50 before the
  lowest position on scrolling up, and every 3 seconds the rows after
  the highest position. (Since 2026-11-25, section 11 and 8.2, Chat, a
  room that the browser has a copy of opens with another read: the rows
  after the copy's highest position, at most 100.) Their rows are now of
  three kinds, and the
  positions the page keeps for its reads are the lowest and the highest
  of the rows it read, drawn or not. So a page of 50 rows can show
  fewer than 50 messages. An edit or a delete is never drawn as a
  bubble. The page keeps, for each message, the newest row that names
  it: a delete, which is always the last, or else the edit with the
  highest position; an edit that came without its text is not kept,
  since a newer row names the same message. It is kept also for a
  message the page does not hold yet: a row that names a message has a
  higher position than the message, and the page reads a chat from its
  newest rows backwards, so it holds that row before the message comes
  with an older page.
- How a message is drawn, by the rule the masterpod reads by too (its
  spec, 31.4): the message is deleted when a delete names it; otherwise
  its text is the newest edit's; otherwise its own. Deleted: the grey
  line, the one of "Trade update" in a chat about a listing, small,
  grey, in the middle, with no name and no time, and the same line for
  the person who deleted. Edited: the edit's text, and the small word
  "edited" in the bubble after the text, where the tick stands, for the
  writer and for everyone else. A message whose row came without its
  text while the page holds no row that names it is not drawn until a
  read brings that row; this happens when a chat is opened in the
  seconds after an edit, and it lasts until the next 3-second read.
- This pod's own edit or delete is drawn from the masterpod's answer;
  everyone else's reaches an open conversation with its 3-second read,
  as a row like any other.
- "Seen" (8.2, Chat). A member has seen an edited message once that
  member's seen position has reached the edit's position, which is
  above the message's own. So an edited newest message reads "Sent"
  again until the other person's wallet has read the edit, and "Seen"
  stands meanwhile under the newest message they did read. A deleted
  message carries no word. The page tells the masterpod the highest
  position it has read, as before; that can be an edit's or a
  delete's.
- The chat list (8.2, Chat). The row's line is `lastMessage.message`
  decrypted, as before, which is the new text for an edited message,
  and the words "Message deleted" when `deleted` is true, with no "You:
  " before them and with nothing decrypted. The page keeps the decrypted
  lines by the message's id and its `editPosition`, since an edited
  message keeps its id. The row's time and the order of the rows go by
  `lastMessage.createdAt`, the message's own time, so an edit or a
  delete moves no chat.
- The unread dot goes by `lastMessage`'s sender and position, as before
  (session.service's `unreadRooms`), and neither moves: an edit or a
  delete lights no dot and takes none away.
- The sound (8.1). The shell rang when a room's `lastPosition` had
  risen; it now rings when the position of the room's newest message
  has (`lastMessage.position`). An edit or a delete raises the first
  and leaves the second, so it rings nothing.
- The pinned card of a chat about a listing (8.7) reads the chat's
  messages on its own. Editing and deleting are off in those chats, so
  no row there comes without its text, and the card is as it was.
  chat.service's `decryptMessage` answers null for a row with no
  ciphertext, as for one that does not open.

What a wallet tab does that was loaded before this step's deploy (the
plan's section 4, point 10; tried, section 11). It keeps the wallet of
before until it is loaded again. In an open chat it draws an edit as a
second bubble with the new text at the chat's end, and a delete as a
bubble "(cannot decrypt)" at the chat's end; a message that it had read
before keeps its old text, and one that was edited or deleted before
the tab read it is a bubble "(cannot decrypt)" in the message's place.
Its chat list lights no dot and moves no chat; the row keeps the text
the tab had decrypted, and after a reload of the same old wallet the
row of a deleted newest message reads "(cannot read)". It plays its
sound once for an edit or a delete in a chat whose newest message is
somebody else's, when that chat is not the page on the screen. Nothing
stops: the tab goes on reading and sending, and it is right after the
Update button or any reload (8.1).

What a wallet of this step does in front of a masterpod of before (not
the plan's order, which deploys the masterpod first; tried, section
11): every row is a message and every `lastMessage` is as before, so
the chat reads and sends as it did. The menu opens, since the wallet
cannot tell, and Edit and Delete end in "HTTP 404: Not Found" in the
conversation's red line.

Left as it is (the plan's section 6): no history of a message's earlier
texts; no taking back of a text that somebody has read, or that an old
tab still shows; no edit and no delete after leaving a chat; nobody
edits or deletes another person's message, a public room's creator
among them; a reply to a message. And one thing of this build: a chat
whose newest 50 rows are all edits and deletes, which takes 50 of them
in a row with no message between, opens with no bubble, the words "No
messages yet." and the button Load older messages, which brings the
rows before them.

The proxy forwards both routes as any masterpod path (section 2);
nothing in server/ and nothing under deploy/ changed. The wallet's side
is the conversation and the chat list (8.2, Chat), the shell's sound
(8.1), masterpod-api.service and chat.service (8.3), the confirmation
box (8.9) and the words (8.8).

### 4.20 Joy looks things up on the web

Added 2026-11-24 (forclaude/joy-web-search-plan-1.md, FINAL on the
user's word, its steps 1 and 2; section 11): Joy, the wallet's AI of
4.18, searches the web when an answer needs something recent or
something that changes, and answers from what she found. The user,
after day one: "So, why can't joy access the internet?" Anthropic's own
web search tool is added to the request that the masterpod sends
already, and Anthropic runs the search inside that request. The
masterpod's side is its own spec's section 32, which holds the rules,
the tool in the request and the ways a request ends, the stream, the
column that counts the searches, what Joy is told and what it costs.
The masterpod gained there: one column on `joy_usage` (`searches`), two
env variables and new words in its shared memory file. No table, no
route and no npm package. The wallet gained no package, no env variable
and no route. (Since 2026-11-25, the masterpod's spec, section 36: when
OpenAI's model answers, the search is OpenAI's own web search tool,
which OpenAI runs inside the request in the same way. The lines of the
stream and `sources` are the same. Two things can differ in what a
member sees: an answer from one of OpenAI's own services, such as its
weather service, has no source; and asked one more question about a
searched answer, Joy may search again.)

    POST /ask-joy (setup), the request as before (4.18), two additions to its answer
    body: { messages: [ { role, text } ], memory }, as before: of each message the wallet sends its role
          and its text and nothing else; the sources of an earlier answer are not sent back
    answer: the stream of 4.18, with one kind of line more and one field more in the last line:
            { "searching": true }                            Joy starts a web search. One line for each
                                                             search she starts, written before the search
                                                             runs, also for one that then fails
            { "done": true, "stop": "end" | "length" | "refused", "memory": "<the whole file>" | null,
              "sources": [ { "title": "...", "url": "https://..." } ] }
                                                             the last line of an answer that ended
            sources: the web pages Joy cited, in the order of their first use, each address once, ten at
                 most, only addresses that begin with https:// or http://. An empty list when she cited
                 none: an answer without a search, a search that failed, a request without the tool.
                 A title has at most 200 characters, and it is an empty text when the page gave none.
                 A page that a search found and Joy did not cite is not among them
            { "error": ... } has no sources
            when Joy wrote words before a search, her words after it begin a new paragraph: the blank
            line is in the text itself
    a masterpod of before: no `searching` line, and no `sources` in the last line

What the wallet does with it (8.2, Joy; 8.3).

- While a search runs. A line `{ "searching": true }` sets
  joy.service's `searching`, and the page says "Joy is searching the
  web…". While no word of the answer has come, that stands in the
  waiting bubble, where "Joy is writing…" stands. When Joy wrote some
  words before the search, the bubble holds those words and the
  searching words stand under it as a small grey line. The next piece
  of the answer takes them away, and so does the answer's end, however
  it ends; a search that follows a search keeps them. The line says
  that she asked, not for which words: her query is in no line (the
  masterpod's spec, 32.3). In the first real call Joy wrote nothing
  before the search, so a member mostly sees the waiting bubble.
  (Since 2026-11-25, 4.21: a picture's line takes the searching words
  away too, and while Joy is making a picture the words on a picture
  stand in their place.)
- The sources. The `sources` of the last line are kept with that
  answer, as one more field of the message, in the page's memory and
  in the chat's blob (below). A message for which no page is left has
  no such field: an answer without a search is kept exactly as before
  this step. Under the answer's bubble the page draws the word
  "Sources" and one row for each page (8.2, Joy).
- The check. The wallet checks the sources itself, when the last line
  comes and again when a kept chat is opened (joy.service's
  `sourcesOf`). The value must be a list. An entry is taken when its
  `title` is a text, which may be empty, and its `url` is a text that
  begins with `https://` or `http://` and that the browser reads as an
  address with a site. Each address is taken once, and the first ten
  are taken. Anything else is passed over. A title is kept without the
  spaces around it and cut at 200 characters, and an address is kept
  as it came. Sources stay only on an answer of Joy's. The masterpod
  sends nothing else (its spec, 32.3); the wallet checks all the same,
  so that a link on the Joy page is made of nothing else, whatever a
  line or a kept chat holds.
- A row. It shows the page's title and after it the page's site: the
  address's host as the browser reads it, without a leading "www.", so
  it names where the link leads. A page that gave no title shows its
  site in the title's place. The row is a link with the address as it
  came, `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener"`, as the wallet's other
  links to outside pages are (the meeting links of the case pages). So
  the page opens in a new tab, and the wallet's own tab stays as it
  is, with its login, which lives in that tab's memory. The opened
  page has no hold on the wallet's tab (`window.opener` is null) and
  is told nothing of where the visitor came from: the wallet's page is
  served with `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` (section 2). In the
  wallet opened from an iPhone's Home Screen the page opens in the
  app's own browser sheet over the wallet, and a cross closes it
  (tried, section 11).
- What is sent. The request does not change: of each message the
  wallet sends its role and its text (`conversationOf`). So a later
  message carries an earlier searched answer as its words alone, and
  Joy is told so in the masterpod's shared memory file (its spec,
  32.5).
- Which answers show sources. Every answer that ended, whatever its
  `stop`: one that was cut at the model's limit or stopped by the
  safety check shows the pages cited up to there, the rows between its
  bubble and the grey line that says how it ended. An answer that is
  cut off in the middle shows none: the sources travel in the last
  line, and such an answer has none (the plan's section 4, point 6).
- Past the daily number of searches, and with web search switched off
  on the masterpod, nothing tells the wallet. The message is answered
  like any other, with an empty list, and Joy says herself that she
  cannot search when a member asks her to (the plan's section 4,
  point 5). The wallet shows no red line for it.

The kept chat (4.18, "The chat survives a reload"), as it is since
this step. The database, the place, the key and the version are the
ones of 4.18:

    value       the blob as bytes: iv || ciphertext || tag of the JSON
                { v: 1, messages: [ { role: "user" | "assistant", text, at, end?, sources? } ] }
                sources: only on an answer of Joy's for which she cited web pages:
                [ { title, url } ], one to ten entries, as the wallet's check left them

A chat that was kept before this step has no `sources` and opens as it
is. The other way round holds too: a wallet of before this step opens a
chat that this step's wallet kept, reads the fields it knows, draws no
sources, and leaves the field on the message when it writes the chat
again (tried, section 11).
(Since 2026-11-25, 4.21: the database is version 2, with a second place
for the pictures, and a message can also have `picture`. The other way
round holds only in a browser where no wallet of 4.21 has opened Joy: a
wallet of before cannot open a database of version 2, and comes up with
an empty chat.)

What leaves the wallet. Nothing that the wallet sends changes. One
thing is new behind the masterpod: for a search Joy writes a query,
which can hold words of the member's message, and the query goes to a
search engine that Anthropic uses. The one line under Joy's header
does not say that in particular and stays as it is (the plan's section
4, point 9): it is still true. A tap on a source takes the member to
that page's site, as any link does. (Since 2026-11-25, the masterpod's
spec, section 36: or to one that OpenAI uses, when OpenAI's model
answers.)

What a wallet tab does that was loaded before this step's deploy (the
plan's section 4, point 11; tried by the masterpod's step, its spec
32.10, and again here, section 11). It keeps the wallet of before until
it is loaded again. It passes the `searching` line over and reads no
`sources`: it says "Joy is writing…" while a search runs, shows a
searched answer without its sources, and keeps such an answer as its
words alone. It ends with a reload, and the tab shows the Update button
by itself (8.1). This is why the wallet's step is deployed before the
masterpod's (the plan's section 4, point 10): an answer that used a
search has to show its sources. After the wallet's deploy nothing has
changed for anybody, and after the masterpod's deploy Joy looks things
up.

What this step's wallet does in front of a masterpod of before, which
is how things stand between the two deploys (tried, section 11): no
`searching` line comes and no last line has `sources`, so nothing new
shows and nothing fails.

Decided while building, each a small thing the plan had not named:

- The thread follows the grey line. The page's effect that keeps a
  reader at the thread's end also reads `searching` (8.2, Joy).
  Without that, a searching line that reaches the page alone, some
  time after Joy's last words, stands under the thread's lower edge,
  out of sight (tried with that line taken out, section 11).
- A list with no entry left is not kept: the message then has no
  `sources` field, and the page draws the word "Sources" only over a
  list with an entry.
- The rows stand between the bubble and the grey line of an answer
  that stopped early.
- The check also asks that the browser can read the address, since the
  site that is shown comes from that reading. An address with a space
  in its site passes the masterpod's own check; Chrome reads the space
  as `%20` and keeps the entry, and a browser that cannot read such an
  address passes it over.
- Sources that a kept chat holds on a member's own message are
  dropped when the chat is opened.
- The two numbers of the check, ten pages and 200 characters, are
  constants in joy.service.ts beside the check, not in constants.ts:
  the plan names this step's files, and constants.ts is not one.

Left as it is (the plan's section 6): opening a link that a member
pastes; marks inside an answer that point to a source; Joy reading the
pages again in a later message; telling a searched answer from one in
which Joy named a source from memory; choosing the sites; showing the
member what Joy searched for; a page that shows the searches. And of
this build: a site whose name has letters outside ASCII shows in the
form the browser gives it (`xn--…`); a title is drawn as it came, in
whatever letters, cut where the row ends; and a member cannot tell
from the rows which of Joy's sentences came from which page.

The proxy forwards the call as before (section 2): it hands the stream
on and reads no line of it. Nothing in server/ and nothing under
deploy/ changed. The wallet's side is the Joy page (8.2, Joy),
joy.service and masterpod-api.service (8.3) and the words (8.8).

### 4.21 Joy has pictures made

Added 2026-11-25 (forclaude/joy-pictures-plan-1.md, FINAL on the user's
word, its steps 1 and 2; section 11): a member asks Joy, the wallet's AI
of 4.18, for a picture, and gets one in her answer. Joy does not draw.
She writes a description, and a model of the company OpenAI makes the
picture from it. The user: "I suppose my server can just route image
creation request to chat gpt." And: "People could download the images/
photos they make." The masterpod's side is its own spec's section 33,
which holds the rules, Joy's third tool (`make_picture`), the one
request to OpenAI, the stream, the column that counts the pictures, what
Joy is told and what it costs. The masterpod gained there: one column on
`joy_usage` (`pictures`), six env variables, one file of code and new
words in its shared memory file. No table, no route and no npm package.
The wallet gained no package, no env variable and no route.

    POST /ask-joy (setup), the request as before (4.18), two additions to its answer
    body: { messages: [ { role, text } ], memory }, as before: of each message the wallet sends its role
          and its text and nothing else; no picture is ever sent back
    answer: the stream of 4.18 and 4.20, with two kinds of line more:
            { "drawing": true }                              Joy starts a call of her picture tool. One
                                                             line for each call that she starts, written
                                                             before OpenAI is asked, also for a call that
                                                             brings no picture: a refused one, a failed
                                                             one, a second call in one message, a
                                                             description that is empty or too long, an
                                                             answer cut off in the middle of the call
            { "picture": { "type": "image/jpeg" | "image/png" | "image/webp", "data": "<base64>",
                           "description": "<Joy's description>" } }
                                                             a picture that OpenAI made: ONE line, one in
                                                             an answer at most, before Joy's sentence
            data: the picture's bytes as plain base64. A picture at the masterpod's own settings is
                 about 160 to 220 KB, so the line is 210,000 to 290,000 characters long. The masterpod
                 sets no ceiling
            description: the description as it went to OpenAI, 1 to 1,000 characters
            the last line is the one of 4.20, unchanged. An answer can fail after the picture came (its
            last line is then { "error": ... }), and it can end with a picture and no word
    a masterpod of before, one that has no key for OpenAI, one with pictures switched off, and an anoPod
    past its 30 pictures of the day: no `drawing` line and no `picture` line. The answer is an ordinary
    one, and Joy says herself that she cannot make a picture

What the wallet does with it (8.2, Joy; 8.3).

- While a picture is made. A line `{ "drawing": true }` sets
  joy.service's `drawing`, and the page says "Joy is making a picture…".
  While no word of the answer has come, that stands in the waiting
  bubble, where "Joy is writing…" stands. When Joy wrote some words
  before the call, the bubble holds those words and the words on a
  picture stand under it as the small grey line. Three things take them
  away: the picture's line, the answer's next piece, and the answer's
  end, however it ends. The second is there because the line says that
  Joy asked, not that a picture comes: after a call that brought none,
  her own words follow. While a search and a picture are both under way,
  the page says making a picture. In the planning's real call (the
  plan's section 7) Joy called her tool at once, with no word before it,
  and a picture took 8 to 9 seconds, so a member mostly sees the waiting
  bubble.
- The picture's line. It takes the words on a picture away, and the
  words on a search with them. The picture then stands in the answer
  that is being written, with the button Download under it, and under
  them the waiting bubble says "Joy is writing…" until her first word.
- The check. The wallet checks the line itself (joy.service's
  `pictureOf`). `type` is one of the wallet's own three picture types,
  JPEG, PNG and WebP (`IMAGE_CONTENT_TYPES` of src/app/images.ts).
  `description` is a text of 1 to 1,000 characters once the spaces
  around it are taken off. `data` is base64 that the browser opens, to
  at least one byte and at most 4 MB (4,194,304 bytes), the wallet's own
  ceiling. A line that does not pass is passed over: no picture shows,
  Joy's words are kept as an answer without one, and nothing is written.
  A second picture's line in one answer is passed over too. The
  masterpod sends none of these (its spec, 33.3 and 33.4). The wallet
  checks all the same, since what passes is kept in the browser, drawn
  on the page and handed out as a file. The wallet does not look into
  the bytes: whether they are a picture is the browser's to say when it
  draws them, and the type is never one that a browser opens as a page.
- Where a picture is. In the page's memory: its bytes, for Download, and
  an address of them for the page to draw (an object URL, from
  `imageObjectUrl` of images.ts). In the browser's database: an entry of
  its own (below). In the chat's message:
  `picture: { id, description }`, an id that the wallet makes up, 16
  random bytes as hex, and Joy's description. The bytes are in no
  message.
- The picture in the answer. Above Joy's words, also above words that
  she wrote before it, with Download directly under the picture (8.2,
  Joy). A tap on the picture does nothing.
- Download. On an iPhone or an iPad the button opens the phone's own
  share sheet (`navigator.share` with the picture as one file), where
  Apple's "Save Image" puts the picture into Photos. Everywhere else it
  is a plain download, as the CSV download of the noted transactions is:
  a temporary link with `download`. The file is the whole picture as it
  came, not the small one of the page. Its name is `joy-`, the date and
  the time of the tap by the device's own clock, and `.jpg`, `.png` or
  `.webp`: `joy-2026-11-25-21-03-07.jpg`. Why two ways (tried on phones
  before the plan was written, the plan's section 4, point 1, and in the
  wallet itself, section 11): on an iPhone a plain download lands in the
  Files app from Safari and saves nothing at all from the Home Screen,
  and the share sheet of an Android phone has nothing that saves. It is
  a workaround. No browser has a call that saves into Photos, so the
  wallet tells an iPhone and an iPad by the browser's user agent, as
  alerts.service tells them: an iPad may call itself a Macintosh, and
  has a touch screen. The file is made inside the tap, from bytes that
  the page holds, since a share sheet opens only then. Closing the sheet
  rejects the call. That is no failure, and nothing shows. An iPhone
  whose browser has no share call, or says that it cannot share a file
  (`navigator.canShare`), gets the plain download.
- What is sent. The request does not change: of each message the wallet
  sends its role and its text (`conversationOf`). For an earlier answer
  that had a picture, the text is a note of the wallet's, an empty line
  and her words, or the note alone when the answer has no word:

      [Note from the wallet: a picture stood here. You made it with make_picture from this description: <Joy's description>]

  The note is the plan's, letter for letter (its 3.6), and the
  masterpod's shared memory file tells Joy what the line is (its spec,
  33.6). Why: Joy gets no picture back, so without the note "Make the
  hat red." would find her with no trace that she made one. In the
  planning's real call she called her tool again in four of four tries
  with the note in front of her earlier answer. The note stands only in
  what is sent. The chat on the screen shows her words as she wrote
  them. An answer whose picture is no longer kept still goes back with
  its note: the description is in the chat.
- Which answers keep a picture. Every answer in which one came. One that
  ended, whatever its `stop`. One that ended with a picture and no word:
  it is no cut-off answer, and shows the picture and its button alone.
  And one that failed after the picture came: it keeps the picture, with
  the grey line of a cut-off answer under it and no red line, and the
  member's message stays in the chat.
- Past the 30 pictures of a day, on a masterpod with no key for OpenAI
  and with pictures switched off there, nothing tells the wallet. The
  message is answered like any other, and Joy says so herself (the
  plan's section 4, point 6). The wallet shows no red line for it. A
  picture that OpenAI refuses, and one that fails, are answers in Joy's
  own words as well.

The kept chat and the pictures' place (4.18, "The chat survives a
reload"), as they are since this step:

    database    anopod-wallet, version 2 (version 1 until this step)
    place       joy-chat, as before: one entry for each pod, under the anoPod's id
    value       the blob as bytes: iv || ciphertext || tag of the JSON
                { v: 1, messages: [ { role: "user" | "assistant", text, at, end?, sources?, picture? } ] }
                picture: only on an answer of Joy's for which a picture was made: { id, description }
                id: 32 hex characters, made up by the wallet
                description: Joy's description, 1 to 1,000 characters
    place       joy-pictures, new: one entry for each picture
    key         the anoPod's id, hex, one space, the picture's id
    value       the blob as bytes: iv || ciphertext || tag (the wallet's `encrypt`, section 7) of
                one byte, the length of the type's name || the type's name in ASCII ("image/jpeg") ||
                the picture's bytes as they came, with no base64 in between

A browser that has the database of before keeps its first place, and the
chats in it, through the change of version: the wallet makes the second
place and touches nothing else (tried, section 11). A picture's bytes
are not in the chat's blob because that blob is written whole after
every message. An entry is the picture's bytes and 39 bytes more for a
JPEG: one, ten for "image/jpeg", and twelve and sixteen for the
encryption. The type is inside the ciphertext, so nothing can be read in
an entry. A picture is written when its line comes, in the same row of
writes as the chat, so it is there before the chat that names it. There
is no ceiling on how many pictures a chat keeps (the plan's section 4,
point 4).

When a kept chat is opened, the wallet checks each kept `picture` as it
checks the sources (`keptPictureOf`: only on an answer of Joy's, an id
of that form, a description of 1 to 1,000 characters), reads each
picture's entry, opens it under the anoPod encryption key and makes an
address for the page. Only then does the chat show, so no picture is
drawn as gone while its bytes are still being read. A picture whose
entry is not there, does not open under this key, or names another type
than the wallet's three shows a grey line in its place: "This picture is
no longer kept in this browser." Her words stay. Where the browser
refuses the write of a picture (no room, a private window), the picture
stays on the page until a reload, and the grey line stands in its place
after that.

New chat takes the pod's chat and every picture of the pod out of the
database, in one transaction, and gives the pictures' addresses back to
the browser. Another pod's entries in the same browser are not touched.
The box of New chat says one sentence more when the chat holds a picture
that can still be downloaded (8.9).

What leaves the wallet. Nothing that the wallet sends changes but the
note above. One thing is new behind the masterpod: for a picture, the
description that Joy wrote from the chat goes to OpenAI, with a hash of
the anoPod's id and nothing else of the chat (the masterpod's spec,
33.3). The one line under Joy's header does not say that in particular
and stays as it is (the plan's section 4, point 9): it is still true.
(Since 2026-11-25, the masterpod's spec, section 36: "nothing else of
the chat" holds for the request that makes the picture. When OpenAI's
model writes Joy's answers, the chat goes to OpenAI too, in the request
for her answer, as it went to Anthropic.)

What a wallet tab does that was loaded before this step's deploy (the
plan's section 4, point 11; tried by the masterpod's step, its spec
33.11). It passes both lines over: it says "Joy is writing…" while a
picture is made, and shows Joy's words about a picture and no picture,
until it is loaded again. The tab shows the Update button by itself
(8.1). This is why OpenAI's key goes into the masterpod's servers last,
after both deploys (the plan's section 4, point 10): without the key no
picture is made.

A wallet of before in a browser whose database this step's wallet has
opened. The database's version went up, and a wallet of before asks for
version 1, which the browser refuses. Such a wallet finds no kept chat,
shows an empty one with no red line, and keeps what is written to Joy in
the page's memory alone. It changes nothing in the database (tried,
section 11). That happens in two cases: a tab that was loaded before
this step's deploy and is still open while a newer tab of the same
browser has opened Joy, until it is loaded again; and a wallet server
that is taken back to a commit of before this step. In both, the chat
that this step's wallet kept is there again, with its pictures, as soon
as this step's wallet runs in that browser. It follows from the plan's
own choice (its section 7): the pictures' place is a second one in Joy's
database, and a place cannot be added without a new version.

What this step's wallet does in front of a masterpod of before, which is
how things stand between the two deploys, and in front of one with no
key for OpenAI (both tried, section 11): no `drawing` line and no
picture's line come, so nothing new shows and nothing fails. In a
browser that opens Joy the database goes to version 2, with an empty
second place.

Decided while building, each a small thing the plan had not named:

- A piece of the answer takes the words on a picture away, beside the
  two things that the plan names, the picture's line and the answer's
  end. The masterpod writes a `drawing` line for a call that brings no
  picture too, and her words would otherwise stand under "Joy is making
  a picture…" to the answer's end (tried with that line taken out,
  section 11).
- The picture's line takes the words on a search away. A search that ran
  before her call is over when the picture comes, and without this the
  page said "Joy is searching the web…" under the picture while she
  wrote her sentence (tried). What it costs: a search that Anthropic
  holds back behind her call (the masterpod's spec, 33.2) runs after the
  picture with no words on it.
- While both signals are on, the page says making a picture, in the
  waiting bubble and in the grey line alike.
- The ceiling is 4 MB of picture: 25 times a picture of the masterpod's
  own settings, and a PNG of 1024 by 1024 pixels still fits (the trial's
  was 1.5 MB). It is looked at twice: the text's length before the text
  is opened, and the bytes after.
- A description is taken as it is or not at all. One of more than 1,000
  characters, which the masterpod never sends, makes the line no
  picture. It is not cut, since it goes back to Joy as words.
- One picture for one answer: a second line is passed over.
- The id is 16 random bytes as hex. A picture's entry stands under the
  anoPod's id, a space and that id, so that New chat takes a pod's
  pictures out as one range of keys.
- The type's name is inside the ciphertext, in front of the picture.
- A kept chat shows when its pictures are opened, not before.
- The picture's box is a square until the browser has opened the bytes,
  and has the picture's own shape then (`aspect-ratio: auto 1 / 1`): the
  masterpod's size is a setting, so a picture need not be a square. When
  the browser has opened a picture, the thread follows once more (8.2,
  Joy).
- The file's name is the moment of the tap on the device's own clock, to
  the second.
- A browser that says it cannot share a file gets the plain download,

- The sentence in the box of New chat stands only when a picture can

- The two numbers of the check (4 MB, 1,000 characters) are constants in

Left as it is (the plan's section 6): changing the old picture itself;

showing the member the description; a larger view of the picture inside
the wallet; sending a picture from Joy into a chat room; a see-through
background, a drawing as SVG, a moving picture; a mark that says the
picture was made by an AI. And of this build: nothing tells a member

The proxy forwards the call as before (section 2): it hands the stream
