Since 2026-11-24 (section 11; 4.17) they are as fresh as the
conversation's own 3-second read: when the conversation opens, that read
brings the position of every member who has seen anything, and
afterwards only the positions that changed, so "Seen" follows within 3
seconds where it was 5. Against a masterpod of before, which hands the
positions out with the whole room list alone, it is 5 as it was. The
room is marked seen (Unread, below) when it opens and when
new messages show (since 2026-11-25, in a room that opens from its copy:
when the read that follows the copy is answered). While the conversation
is on the screen the page also
tells the masterpod how far this pod has read (/mark-messages-seen,
4.10; 2026-11-19, section 11): the newest position shown, after the
thread opens, after each 3-second poll and after a send, and only when
it is above what the page told before. It tells only while the page is
visible (the browser's document.visibilityState is "visible"): a chat
left open in a hidden tab reports nothing, so the others do not read
"Seen" for it. The call is quiet and shows nothing. One that fails is
made again at the next poll. After a 404, the answer of a masterpod of
before, the page tells nothing more for as long as it lives: on a phone
until the person goes back to the list of chats, and on a computer,
where a click on another chat keeps the same page, until the person
opens another page of the wallet or loads it again. "You are
not in this chat." for a room that is not in
the list.

Room picture (2026-11-22, section 11; 4.15), an entry of the
conversation's menu, under Members, in a public room and for its creator
alone: a member who is not the creator has no such entry, and a room
that is not public has none for anyone. The entry opens a panel under
the header, where the panel of Invite someone opens, and closes it
again. The panel shows the room's round mark at 72 px (8.6: the picture,
or the grey disc with the globe while the room has none), the sentence
"This picture stands beside the room's name. Everyone who looks for
public rooms sees it. Pick a photo to set it, or to put another in its
place.", and a file box that takes pictures. A picked file is sent at
once; there is no second button. The wallet redraws it first as it
redraws the public selfie (`redrawSquare` in images.ts): the middle of
the picture as a square of at most 320 pixels (`ROOM_PICTURE_SIDE`),
never made bigger, a fresh JPEG at 0.8 (`ROOM_PICTURE_JPEG`), so only
pixels go out. It is sent with /set-chat-room-picture. When the
masterpod has taken it, the wallet keeps the picture under the
`pictureAt` of the answer (room-picture-cache.service, 8.3), so it is
not read back, and reads the room list again: the picture then stands
at the conversation's top, in the panel and in the chat list. A file the
browser cannot read as a picture is refused with the camera's sentence,
"The browser cannot read this file as a picture. Pick another photo.",
in the conversation's red line, and nothing is sent. A refusal of the
masterpod shows in the same red line, and the picture of before stays.
The file box is switched off while an action of the page runs. The
panel closes when the page goes on to another conversation. The creator
puts another picture in its place the same way, at any time, and cannot
take the picture away. The other members see a new picture within about
5 seconds, by the shell's read of the room list, and a person on Find
public rooms at the next read of that list.

Stickers (2026-11-23, section 11; 4.16; the plan is
forclaude/stickers-database-plan-1.md, whose section 1 is the look in
eight points). Stickers work in every chat. What a person sees:
- A sticker in the conversation. A message whose whole text is a
  sticker's code, "[sticker:<set>/<number>]" (the spaces around it
  aside), shows as that sticker's picture with no bubble around it: 148
  by 128 pixels, the picture whole inside that box, at the left for
  someone else's and at the right for this pod's own, with the tick or
  "Sending" beside it and the words Sent and Seen under it as under any
  message. The picture's address, /stickers/<set>/<number>, is made of
  the code alone (`stickerSrc` in stickers.ts), so the page needs no
  list of the sets to draw it, and a wallet that has no list draws a
  sticker all the same. A moving sticker moves.
- A picture that cannot be fetched. Where the picture does not load (the
  masterpod has no such sticker, the masterpod cannot be reached, the
  answer is no picture), the word "Sticker" stands in its place, in an
  ordinary bubble. Nobody sees a code. The word stands in every message
  that is that sticker, until the conversation is opened again: then
  the picture is tried again.
- The chat list. A newest message that is a sticker reads "Sticker" in
  the row's line, "You: Sticker" for this pod's own. That is worked out
  from the message's text alone, whether or not the picture can be
  fetched; the chat list asks for no list of the sets.
- The smiling face. While this login's list holds at least one set
  (stickers.service, 8.3), a round button with a smiling face (the icon
  `mood`) stands to the left of the message box, which is 48 pixels
  narrower for it. A tap opens the stickers under the message box, and
  a second tap closes them. While the list has not arrived, and while
  the masterpod has no set, there is no button, no panel and no strip,
  and the conversation is, part for part, the page of before.
- The stickers under the message box. A panel under the message box, at
  most 284 pixels high, and 202 on a screen that is 640 pixels high or
  less; it gives way when the frame is shorter still. At its top a row of small
  pictures, one for each set in the order of the masterpod's row: the
  set's first sticker. Six and a half fit, so a seventh shows that the
  row slides. Under the row stand the stickers of the set that is
  picked, in the set's order, in columns of at least 64 pixels; a set
  that does not fit scrolls inside the panel. A tap on another set
  shows that set from its first row. No other set's pictures are on the
  page, so a picture travels only when it is about to be shown.
  Opening the panel takes the cursor out of the message box, so a
  phone's keyboard goes away and the panel stands where it was. A tap
  into the message box closes the panel. The panel is closed when the
  page goes on to another conversation.
- One tap sends. A tap on a sticker sends it at once: the message is the
  sticker's code, sent as any message is. The panel stays open and the
  message box keeps what it holds. A send that fails takes the sticker
  out of the conversation again and shows the refusal in the
  conversation's red line.
- The clock. Once a sticker was sent from this phone, a clock stands
  first in the row of sets. It shows the stickers sent lately, the
  newest first, at most 24, as the phone keeps them (its own storage,
  the entry `anopod-wallet.stickers-sent`; for the phone, not for one
  pod), and of those only the ones the list has. The first opening of
  the panel shows the clock's stickers when there are some and the
  first set when there are none; a later opening shows the part that
  was left. A sticker sent while the panel is open joins the clock at
  the next opening, so nothing moves under a finger.
- The suggestions. While a person types and the panel is closed, a strip
  above the message box shows up to four stickers whose tags fit what
  was typed (`suggestedStickers` in stickers.ts), in every chat but for
  the two traders of a marketplace chat (the last point). A sticker
  fits when
  the text ends with one of its tags, whole, of two characters or more
  and not in the middle of an English word, or when the last word, of
  three characters or more, is the beginning of one of its tags.
  Nothing while the box is empty or the text ends in a space. The
  order: the stickers sent lately first; then the ones a whole tag
  fits, before the ones only a tag's beginning fits; and within each of
  those two, one from every set in turn, in the order of the sets. Four
  stand side by side, so the strip does not slide. A tap on one sends
  it and takes the word that brought it up out of the message box;
  whatever stood before that word stays. The cursor stays in the
  message box through that tap, so a phone's keyboard stays up and the
  person can go on typing. The matching is done on the phone, from the
  tags of the list: what a person types never reaches the masterpod
  for it. A reader at the conversation's end stays there when the strip
  comes up.
- A marketplace chat. While the panel is open, the pinned card of the
  room's two traders is out of sight, so that the messages keep their
  room; it is back, as it was, when the panel closes. The two traders
  get no strip of suggestions (2026-11-23, later the same day, section
  11, the note after "Stickers"): the card does not give way to a
  strip, and on a short phone the strip pushed their message box under
  the conversation's lower edge. No suggestion is worked out for them
  (the page's `suggested` is empty while its `trader()` is true), so
  while they type no strip is in the page, no picture is fetched for
  one, and the thread stays where it is. They send a sticker from the
  panel. A guest in such a chat, who has no card, has the strip like
  everybody else.

Edit and delete (2026-11-24, section 11; 4.19; the plan is
forclaude/chat-edit-delete-plan-1.md, whose section 1 is what a person
sees). A person edits and deletes their own messages. What a person
sees:
- The menu. A tap on a message of your own, a click on a computer,
  opens a small menu right under the bubble, its right edge at the
  bubble's: Edit, with a pencil, and Delete, with a bin. A tap beside
  it, and the Escape key, close it. A long press stays what it was, the
  browser marking text. A tap on the copy button of an account id opens
  no menu. Neither does a click that ends a marking of text on a
  computer; a click on marked text takes the marking away, and the
  click after it opens the menu.
- Who has no menu. Somebody else's message has none, in any chat. No
  message has one in a chat about a listing, in an old marketplace
  room and in a chat about an attestor case: those chats can be
  evidence, and the masterpod refuses an edit and a delete there (4.19).
  A message that is still being sent has none, and a deleted one has
  none: a tap there does nothing, as before.
- Edit. It is in the menu for 15 minutes after the message was sent,
  by the phone's clock, and never for a sticker. A tap on it puts the
  message's text into the message box, with the cursor, so a phone's
  keyboard comes up, and a line stands above the box: a pencil, the
  words "Editing a message" and a cross that stops the edit. While it
  stands, the stickers button and the suggested stickers are away. Send
  saves, and so does the Enter key: the bubble keeps its place, shows
  the new text and carries the small grey word "edited" after the
  text, where the tick stands. Send with an unchanged text sends
  nothing and ends the edit; with an empty box Send is off. When the
  edit ends, by Send or by the cross, the box holds again what it held
  before Edit was tapped. A message can be edited more than once, each
  time within the 15 minutes of when it was first sent.
- Too late. The masterpod decides about the 15 minutes by its own
  clock. A person who typed past them, or whose phone's clock is off,
  reads "This message can no longer be edited." in red above the
  message box; the line "Editing a message" goes and the text stays in
  the box.
- Delete. It is in the menu at any time, for a sticker too. The wallet
  asks once, with the confirmation box (8.9): the title "Delete this
  message?", the sentence "Everyone in this chat will see that a
  message was deleted. This cannot be undone.", Cancel and a red
  Delete. After Delete a grey line stands in the message's place, in
  the middle of the thread, with no name and no time: "This message was
  deleted". The person who deleted reads the same line. Cancel, and a
  step back in the browser, delete nothing.
- The others in the chat see the same within 3 seconds, by their
  conversation's own read: the new text with "edited", or the grey
  line. In a room that is not a direct chat the sender's name stands
  over an edited message as over any. Whoever opens the chat later
  gets only the new text, or the grey line: the masterpod hands the old
  text to nobody any more.
- Seen. Under an edited message of your own, "Seen" is counted from the
  edit: an edited newest message reads "Sent" again until the other
  person's wallet has read the edit ("One conversation", above).
- The chat list. The row of a chat whose newest message was edited
  shows the new text, and one whose newest message was deleted reads
  "Message deleted". No dot is lit, nothing rings, and no row moves.
- Deleted meanwhile. An edit or a delete of a message that was deleted
  a moment ago from another phone or computer of the same person reads
  "This message was already deleted." in red, and the grey line then
  stands in the message's place.

A room keeps its messages in the browser (2026-11-25, section 11; 8.3,
room-copies.service; the plan is forclaude/chat-rooms-kept-plan-1.md,
whose section 1 is what a person sees). Until that day every opening of
a conversation emptied the thread and read the room's newest 50 rows
again. Going from one room to another loaded everything again, and the
thread said "No messages yet." meanwhile, also in a room full of
messages. Since then the wallet keeps a copy of the thread of every
room a person has opened: in the page's memory and, encrypted, in the
browser's own database (8.3 has where and how). The masterpod is as it
was: no route, no field and no table changed. What a person sees:
- Back into a room. The room's messages are there at once. What was
  written since comes a moment later, with the masterpod's answer.
- After a load of the page: a reload, a new login, Lock, a phone that
  dropped the page. A room that was opened before has its messages at
  once, from the browser's database: the newest 200 of them at most.
  Older ones load on scrolling up, as before. Messages that were loaded
  by scrolling up stay for as long as the page lives.
- A room this browser has never shown. The thread says "Loading the
  chat." until the messages have come. "No messages yet." stays for a
  room that has none.
- No connection. The room's kept messages, and the red line with the
  reason. When the connection is back, what is new comes within 3
  seconds and the red line goes.
- An edit or a delete that was made while the person was away. The
  message shows as it was for a moment, until the masterpod's answer
  has come. Then it changes.
- A room opens at the end of its thread, as before. Everything else of
  a conversation is as it was: the 3-second read, "Sent" and "Seen",
  the unread dot, sending, editing, deleting, stickers, the pinned
  card.

How a room opens. The page looks for the room's copy: in the page's
memory first, which answers at once, and then in the browser's
database, where it is one read and one decryption. With a copy the page
draws it, through the code that draws an answer of the masterpod, and
is ready from that moment: the 3-second read and a send work before the
masterpod has answered. Then it sends the request of the 3-second read,
with the copy's highest position and a named limit:

    POST /list-messages   { chatRoomId, afterPosition, limit: 100, seenSince: 0 }

The masterpod answers the room's rows after that position, oldest
first: the new messages, and the edits and the deletes written since,
which are rows with a position of their own. With `seenSince` 0 it also
answers how far every member has read, as at an opening before. 100 is
the number the masterpod uses when a request names none, so the answer
is the same (`NEW_ROWS_LIMIT` in chat-room.page.ts); the wallet names it
to know what a full answer is. The answer goes into the thread as a
3-second read's does. Then the room is marked seen up to the highest
position and the masterpod is told (/mark-messages-seen), also when the
answer held no row. Without a copy the room opens with the request of
before, { chatRoomId, beforePosition: lastPosition + 1, limit: 50,
seenSince: 0 }, and the thread it reads becomes the room's copy. It is
one signed request for each opening, before and after: what got better
is what a person sees, not the bytes.

When a copy is dropped. The room then opens as before.
- The room moved on too far. The answer holds 100 rows, so there may be
  more. The copy is dropped, the page stops being ready, and the room's
  newest 50 are read with the request of before. The old thread stays
  on the screen until they have come, and then gives way to them.
- The person is no longer in the room. When a whole chat list arrives
  and a room is not in it, that room's copy is deleted. This covers
  Leave, on this phone and on another.
- The copy is ahead of the masterpod, whose database was put back from
  a backup: a copy from the browser's database whose highest position
  is above the room's `lastPosition` in the chat list.
- The copy cannot be used: an entry that does not open under the anoPod
  encryption key or does not hold a copy, a browser that refuses its
  database, a browser that has cleared it.

The red line of a read of the messages that failed. Since 2026-11-25 it
goes when a later read of the messages succeeds, and only while the red
line is still that line. Until then it stayed until the person's next
action in the room. Two reads put such a line up: a conversation's
opening and Load older messages. Every read of the messages that
succeeds takes it away, the 3-second read first of all. So with a copy
on the screen a failed opening mends itself: the page is ready, the
3-second read asks again, and the line goes with its first answer. A
room that the browser has no copy of and whose opening read fails stays
empty under its red line until it is opened again, as before. Its
thread then says neither "Loading the chat." nor "No messages yet.",
since neither is known; until 2026-11-25 it said "No messages yet.".

The order of the thread. Since 2026-11-25 the thread is kept in the
order of the positions, and a row that comes a second time changes
nothing. Until then such a message moved to the thread's end, also when
newer messages stood there already. With a copy on the screen the page
is ready before its opening read is answered, so the 3-second read or
the read after a send can overtake that answer, which then brings rows
the thread already holds.

What it does not do, by the plan's section 6. The requests going up are
as they were: one signed request for each opening, about 9.6 KB, and
the 3-second read is not touched. The chat list and the faces are read
again after a load of the page. A room's new messages are fetched when
the room is opened, not before. The pinned card of a marketplace chat
still reads the whole chat at each opening. A copy is this browser's: a
second phone has its own. A message that was missed by the gap of the
after-production line "chat: of two changes written at the same
instant, a phone can miss one" stays missing in that browser until the
copy is dropped, where until 2026-11-25 it showed when the chat was
opened again. The fault of the line "chat: a message of your own can
show twice" still goes away when the chat is opened again, since a copy
holds each message once. And a text that was typed and not sent stays
in the message box on a computer when another chat is opened, and is
lost on a phone on the way back to the chat list, both as before.

The pinned card (2026-11-06, section 11), in a private room about a
listing, under the header and its panels and above the thread, drawn for
the room's two traders only (2026-11-12, section 11: the person who made
the room by pressing Connect, and the listing's owner; anyone else in
the room is a guest and gets no card, and "the other person" in this
paragraph and the two after it is the other trader, never a guest; 8.7,
and the paragraph on the attestor in a marketplace chat, below): two
lines (2026-11-19, section 11; until then the listing in one line,
"Selling 100 anos · 35.50 THB each · 3,550 THB", with the other person's
avatar). The first line is the trade in one sentence from the reader's
own side, with the other person's username and no avatar: "You are
selling 500 anos to mai" for the seller, "You are buying 500 anos from
somchai" for the buyer, and Closed when the listing is closed. The line
under it, smaller and grey, is the listing's price and who pays whom how
much: "2.00 THB each · mai pays you 1,000 THB" for the seller, "2.00 THB
each · you pay somchai 1,000 THB" for the buyer. The roles come from the
listing (the owner of a sell listing and the
other person of a buy listing are the seller). Under those lines the card
is the trade guide (rewritten 2026-11-17, section 11; the plan is
forclaude/wallet-trade-guide-plan-1.md): it walks both sides through the
four steps of a trade, the same list for both, one button at a time. The
steps: the buyer sends an account, the seller puts the anos in escrow,
the buyer pays the seller, the seller releases the anos. First the
status box (`app-escrow-strip`, 8.7), the box of the escrow trade page,
here with the other person's username in its sentences: whether the anos
are in escrow, "Step 2 of 4", and the one thing to do and the one thing
not to do. With no trade it reads "Not in escrow", amber to the buyer
and grey to the seller. Step 1, while no account is in the chat (for the
buyer none of this pod's own, for the seller none that the other person
posted): to the buyer "Send somchai the account the anos should go to.
Do not pay yet.", to the seller "Ask somchai to send the account the
anos should go to." Step 2, once one is there: to the buyer "Wait for
somchai to put the anos in escrow. Do not pay until this box says In
escrow. A message in the chat is not proof.", to the seller "Put the
anos in escrow for somchai. You release them after you have been paid."
What the box and the card say once there is a trade is in the next
paragraph. Under the box stands a row of buttons. At its right end the
text button "How a trade works" opens and closes a panel in the card,
under the buttons: the four steps as a numbered list, the step the box
is at in bold, and four lines, "Buyer: do not pay until the anos are in
escrow.", "Seller: do not release the anos until the money is in your
own bank account.", "Buyer: if you paid and the seller does not release
the anos, dispute the trade. Do not cancel." and "Seller: if the buyer
does not pay, ask them to cancel, or dispute the trade." The button is
there whenever the box shows, but for two states: once the trade is
released, and while the seller's form is open. The panel is drawn only
where its button is drawn, so it is not drawn in those two states
either (the plan's decision 27, the same day); a panel that was open
when the seller's form opened is there again when the form closes, and
the button closes it. The buyer's button, with no trade: "Send my
account" (filled), which reads "Send another account" (a text button)
once one of this pod's accounts is in the chat; until 2026-11-17 it was
"Share an account". It opens a menu of this pod's accounts (the id
shortened, the type); one tap posts "Please send the anos to this
account: <the account id>" into the chat, encrypted like any message, so
the thread shows the id in code font with its copy button (8.5); since
2026-11-19 (section 11) the two traders read a grey line in its place,
"You sent your account for this trade." or "mai sent their account for
this trade.", and a guest reads the message as it is. The
seller's button, with no trade: "Put the anos in escrow" (filled), shown
once the other person has posted an account id; until 2026-11-17 it was
"Start the escrow trade", shown from the first and disabled with the
hint "Ask them to share an account first", which the box says now. It
opens a small form in the card, From
(this pod's spending accounts; one is fixed, more is a select), To (the
other person's account ids in the chat, newest first; one is fixed),
Amount in anos (the listing's quantity at first), the total at the
listing's price, Start and Cancel. Start opens the confirmation box
(8.9) with the Start box (`startBox` of src/app/escrow-boxes.ts;
2026-11-19, section 11). The box's title is "Put the anos in escrow",
the words of the card's button. Its first note is the question, "Put
100 anos into escrow for somchai? You release them once you have been
paid. Only the buyer can cancel; either side can dispute.", for the
amount as the form has it when Start is pressed. Its second note is the
passkey line, "To confirm, this phone or computer will ask for your
passkey, the one you log in with." Its buttons are Back and Yes. Back
sends nothing and leaves the form as it was, and so does a box closed
by a step back in the browser's history. Since 2026-11-20 (section 11;
the plan is forclaude/second-key-and-signing-passkey-plan-1.md) the
Start box waits for the same read as the account page's Send box. From
the moment the box opens the card reads pair one from the account's
keyBlob and the account's latest transaction id from /get-account, and
until that read is back Yes is grey and a thin moving bar shows under
the notes (the box's `ready`, 8.9). A read that fails says "No latest
transaction on the ledger yet" in red in the box, Yes stays grey, and
Back closes the box. Once the read is back, Yes builds the
escrowTransfer as the account page's Send does
(buildAnosTransferTransaction with type escrowTransfer) and asks the
device for the
passkey that opened the session, for exactly that transfer (the passkey
check, 8.9; the box's `approve`), straight from
its click: a check that does not pass shows its sentence in red in the
box, the box stays open, and nothing is sent. The
accounts and the amount are taken when Start is pressed, so what is
sent is what the box asked about. Start does nothing while a box is
open or a send is on its way. Until 2026-11-19 Start asked once in
place: the question stood in the card, under the form, with Yes or
Back. The build of that day first put the passkey line under it, small
and grey. With that line a phone screen less than 600 to 620 pixels
high no longer showed Yes and Back, and the card cannot be scrolled, so
the question went into the box before that build was committed (section
11). Once the check has passed and the box has closed, the card
makes its fresh check for an earlier trade (the next paragraph) and then
sends the escrowTransfer the box's Yes built: /api/sign/<n>, with the
passkey's answer sent along (section 3), and /anos-transfer. Until
2026-11-20 the card read the latest transaction id and built the
transfer here, after the box. What follows the answer
(rewritten 2026-11-10, section 11, from
forclaude/wallet-trade-message-plan-1.md): an answer with a 4xx status is
a refusal and shows the validator's reason as the account page shows it,
with plain words when the account already has something waiting on the
validators ("This account already has an escrow trade or a transfer
waiting on the validators. Finish that first, or use another account.").
After any other answer the card checks the chat's trade once more
(below), and that check posts the message "Escrow trade started: 100 anos
from <my account id> to <their account id>. Transaction <id>."; Yes does
not post it. Since 2026-11-19 (section 11) the two traders read a grey
line in its place, "Trade update. Look at the box at the top of this
chat.", and a guest reads the message as it is. The validator stores a trade before it answers, so an answer
lost on the way (no network, the proxy's 502, the doorman's 502 or 504)
may hide a trade that started: found open, it has started and no error
shows; otherwise the card says "The validators did not answer. If the
trade started, it will show here in a moment. If it does not, try again."
and the form stays for another try. A trade the check finds, open or
released, closes the form, so the form does not come back by itself
once that trade is cancelled. A Start box that is open at that moment
stays open; its Yes then meets the fresh check of the next paragraph,
which sends nothing.

The chat's trade (rewritten 2026-11-10, section 11, from
forclaude/wallet-finished-trade-plan-1.md): the card reads it from the
validators when the conversation opens, every 5 seconds while it is open,
once more when the seller says Yes to Start and, since 2026-11-17, once
after the Yes of the card's Release (below). Until the first check
ends the box reads "Checking for a trade…", grey, and the row under it
has "How a trade works" only (2026-11-17, section 11; until then the
card said it in a line of its own where its two buttons go). The
chat's account ids: the page holds the room's newest 50 messages only
(since 2026-11-25, section 11, what the browser kept of the room, which
can be more and is still not the whole chat), so
the card reads every message of the room itself, once (/list-messages
from the first position, 200 at a time, CARD_MESSAGES_PAGE, decrypted
with the room key), and adds the ids the page feeds it, which carry what
arrived since; the form's To list and the step the box is at with no
trade (step 1 until an account is in the chat, then step 2) follow all
of them. The accounts it reads: this pod's usable
spending accounts when it is the seller, and this pod's usable accounts
named in the chat (an id in the messages that is one of
session.accounts), pair one from each keyBlob; with no account id in the
chat nothing is read. A trade is the chat's when it is between one of
those accounts and an account named in the chat, whoever posted the id.
First /list-escrows on each account: the newest open trade of the chat
shows as the box (2026-11-17, section 11; until then as the line "Escrow
trade: 100 anos · Waiting for the seller to release the anos"), by the
trade's stage and this pod's side in it, the seller being the pod whose
account sent the trade. Its words are those of the escrow trade page's
box (the Escrow trade paragraph, above), with the other person's
username where that page says "the seller" or "the buyer": waiting, "Not
in escrow yet", step 2; held, "In escrow: 100 anos", step 3, green to
the buyer ("The anos are held for you. The seller cannot take them back.
Pay somchai now and keep your payment slip.") and amber to the seller;
releasing, "Being released", step 4; cancelling, "Being cancelled";
disputed, "In dispute"; a stage word the wallet does not know, "Open".
While the anos are held the card adds, under the box, "At the listing's
price that is 3,550 THB.", the trade's amount at the listing's price,
and for the buyer, when the trade holds fewer anos than the listing's
quantity, "The listing says 100 anos, but only 40 are in escrow. Pay
only for those." Then the row of buttons. For the seller of a held
trade, "I have been paid: release the anos" (filled): it opens the
Release box of the escrow trade page (8.9; `releaseBox` of
src/app/escrow-boxes.ts) with the buyer's account id and the passkey
line (2026-11-19, section 11; until then the username was typed in the
box), Back sends nothing, and Yes asks for the passkey in the box,
since 2026-11-20 (section 11) for the release itself, which that Yes
builds first (escrow-actions.service's approve; the box's `approve`,
8.9), and,
when that passes, the card sends the release through
escrow-actions.service (8.3), with the passkey's answer. The card then
checks the chat's trade
once. An answer that failed shows in the card's error line, as the
refusal in plain words of the Escrow trade paragraph, only when after
that check the card still shows this trade as held: an answer lost on
the way whose release landed shows no error, as at Start. The button
does nothing while the box is open or a send is on its way. Then, for
both sides, a link to /wallet/<my account>/escrow/<transactionId>, a
text button that reads "Something wrong?" while the anos are held and
"See the trade" in any other stage; then "How a trade works". Cancel and
Dispute stay on that page; until 2026-11-17 Release was there only. An
open trade shows this way whatever the listing's status. With none open, /list-transactions on each account
with `from` the room's createdAt, 200 rows at a time
(CARD_TRANSACTIONS_PAGE), paging back with beforePosition while a page
comes back full: an escrowTransfer of the chat is its released trade, the
newest when there are several. The open list is read first because the
validators write the link before the trade leaves /list-escrows
(anossoftware src/accounts/accounts.service.js, writeApproved), so a
released trade is never missing from both reads. A released trade ends
the chat's trading: both sides read the box's "Released: 100 anos",
green, step 4 (to the buyer "The anos are in your account.", to the
seller, the pod whose account sent the trade, "The anos went to
somchai."; until 2026-11-17 the line "Released: 100 anos went to the
buyer.") and "This trade is finished. To trade again, start a new chat.",
the guide's buttons do not come back in this chat, on this visit or a later
one, and the owner of an open listing gets "Close the listing", which
asks once and calls /close-listing; the card reads Closed once the room
list is refreshed. A new trade between the same two people needs a new
chat, and so another listing, since the masterpod allows one chat per
person per listing. A trade seen open here and then gone with nothing
released reads "Cancelled: the seller kept the anos.", from the card's
memory of this visit, in a line above the box, and the guide is back at
step 2 with its buttons. A read that fails,
on the validators or the masterpod, is never taken as "no trade": the
card keeps the trade or the Released box it shows, and with neither the
box reads "Cannot check right now" until a check has read everything,
with "How a trade works" as the row's only button: to the buyer, amber,
"The wallet could not reach the validators. It is trying again. Do not
pay until this box says In escrow.", to the seller, grey, the first two
of those sentences (until 2026-11-17 the card said "Could not check for
a trade. Trying again." where its two buttons go). The Yes of the Start
box runs one fresh check, after the passkey check has passed in the box
(2026-11-19, section 11) and
before
anything is sent to a signing server. Since 2026-11-20 (section 11) the
order of the guards is: the read of the account's latest transaction id
when the box opens; the build and the passkey at the box's Yes; then
this fresh check; then the signing server. The transfer has to exist
before the passkey can answer for it, so it is built before the check
and no longer after it. The reason given on 2026-11-19 for asking the
passkey first, that Safari opens the passkey sheet only for a tap, is
out of date for every device that can use the wallet (the note of
2026-11-20 in section 11). When the check cannot be read, nothing is sent and
the card says "Could not check for an earlier trade, so nothing was sent.
Try again."; when it finds a trade open or released, nothing is sent,
what was built is dropped, and
the card says "Nothing was sent. This chat already has an escrow trade."
and shows that trade. Three limits: the buyer's card can match a trade
only when the seller's account id is in the chat, which the chat's
message about the trade (the next paragraph) puts there the first time
the seller has the chat open after the trade started; two chats at once
between the same two people on the same accounts both read Released after
one release; a seller who recovered the account after a lost passkey
cannot read the old account, so a release sent from it is not seen. "Send
my account", "Send another account" and "Put the anos in escrow" show
until a trade has started, and again after a cancelled
one; a closed listing's card shows the box and what goes with it only
for a trade, open or released, and with no trade neither the box nor a
button. A room whose listing the masterpod does not give shows no card.

The chat's message about its trade (2026-11-10, section 11, from
forclaude/wallet-trade-message-plan-1.md): whenever the check finds the
chat's trade, open or released, the account it was read on sent it, and
no message in the chat carries its transaction id (64 hex characters, so
it is among the ids named in the chat), the card posts the message
itself, in the seller's name, encrypted with the room key like any other:
"Escrow trade started: 100 anos from <my account id> to <their account
id>. Transaction <id>." for an open trade, "Escrow trade released: 100
anos from <my account id> to <their account id>. Transaction <id>." for
one already released. Since 2026-11-19 (section 11) the two traders read
a grey line in the place of either, "Trade update. Look at the box at
the top of this chat.", and a guest reads the message as it is. This is the only place the message is posted. So a
lost answer to the transfer, a /send-message that failed, a tab closed in
between and a trade started from the account page's Send (escrow kind) to
an account named in the chat all end with the chat told, the next time
the seller has the chat open; the message puts the seller's account id
into the chat, and the buyer's card then finds the trade. The card keeps
the transaction ids it posted about, per room (`told`), so a check that
runs before the thread shows the message does not post it again; a post
that fails is tried again by the next check; two devices of the seller in
the same chat at the same moment can post it twice. The buyer's card
never posts about a trade.

The attestor in a marketplace chat (2026-11-12, section 11; the plan is
forclaude/wallet-case-chats-plan-1.md, its decisions 9, 26 and 27; the
masterpod's part is its spec's section 18): an attestor on an escrow
dispute can be brought into the marketplace chat of the trade, and then
reads everything said there, since a room has one key and a member gets
every message from the first. Either trader can do it, without the other
agreeing, with the menu's "Invite an attestor". The entry shows for the
room's two traders only, and only while the chat's trade is in dispute
and an attestor has a case open on it: the pinned card finds that case
(8.7: /list-my-cases, and of its disputes the one on the trade's
transaction that is open or in review) and tells the page its id. Before
the dispute, before an attestor opens the case, and once the trade is no
longer in dispute there is no entry. Opening it reads /list-my-cases
again, quiet, and takes the dispute with that case id. When that case is
no longer open or in review the entry goes. Otherwise a panel shows
under the header, like the invite panel: the muted line "An attestor you
invite can read this whole chat.", then the attestors on the case, each
with avatar (8.6), username and Invite. The attestors on the case are
the ones the masterpod names on the dispute (`attestors`, masterpod
13.4.5 and 18: every attestor who acted on the case, the one who opened
it first) and, with them, the attestors who have a chat with this pod
about the case (chat.service's `caseAttestors`, 8.3), each once, without
those who are a member of this room or invited to it. So the attestor
who opened the case is on the list from the start, and no other chat
with that attestor is needed first. Invite wraps the room's key to the
attestor's chat keys (`wrapFor`), calls /invite-to-chat-room and
refreshes the room list; the attestor then shows as invited and leaves
the list, and with nobody left to invite the panel reads "The attestors
on this case are already in this chat." A refusal shows in the page's
error line as the masterpod says it; the masterpod lets a member of a
listing chat who did not start it invite an appointed attestor and
nobody else. A second click on the entry closes the panel. The attestor
gets the request on the Requests page (below) and, once in, is a guest:
no pinned card, the two traders' card keeps going by the two traders,
and the attestor's menu has Members and Leave. Nothing takes the
attestor out when the case closes. "Invite someone" stays as it was, for
the room's creator.

Requests, at /chat/requests: the invites to this pod (the inviter's
username, then `invited you to "<the public room's name>"`, `invited you
to a private chat` or, for a room about one of this pod's listings,
`wants to chat about your listing Selling 100 anos for THB`; 2026-11-06;
for a room about someone else's listing, `invited you to the chat about
the listing Selling 100 anos for THB`, which is what an attestor reads
whom a trader brings into a marketplace chat; 2026-11-12, section 11,
step 6;
for a room about an attestor case, by the case's kind, `is an attestor
and wants to chat about your assisted transfer`, `is an attestor and
wants to chat about your escrow dispute` or `is an attestor and wants to
chat about your recovery`, and in the wallet of a pod that is itself an
attestor (its role, 4.3) `invited you to a chat about a case`;
2026-11-12, section 11),
Accept (the room opens) and Decline; the join
requests on the rooms this pod created (`<username> asks to join
<title>`), Approve (the room key wrapped to the requester) and Decline;
each with the person's avatar; "No requests." when both lists are empty.

New chat, at /chat/new, three tabs, since 2026-11-22 (section 11; 4.14)
in the order Message someone, Find public rooms, New public room; until
then New public room stood second and Find public rooms third. Message
someone: a username, Find (/search-usernames), the person's name,
username and selfie, Start chat: the private chat with exactly the two
of you opens when it exists, else a private room is created with a new
room key wrapped to this pod's chat keys, the person is invited with it
wrapped to theirs (their chat public keys are read first, so someone
without them makes no room) and the room opens; finding yourself reads
"That is you.". Since 2026-11-24 (section 11) a chat about a listing
and a chat about an attestor case do not count as that private chat:
Start chat passes a marketplace chat or a case chat with the person
over, and creates a room when the two of you have no other.

Find public rooms, since 2026-11-22: a box "Search public rooms", and
under it the public rooms with the most members first, 50 at a time
(`PUBLIC_ROOMS_PAGE`), read with /list-public-chat-rooms when the tab
opens, until a read has come back: a first read that was refused is
tried again when the tab is opened anew, and after a read that came
back the tab does not read by itself again. Each room has its name, "by
<username> · N members" and
Open (this pod is in it), Requested (asked from this tab) or Request to
join; in front of the name stands the room's round mark at 40 px (8.6;
since the picture's step of 2026-11-22, section 11 and 4.15): the
room's picture when it has one, else the grey disc with the globe, which
every row had until then. Typing into the box reads the list again 400
milliseconds after
the last key (`ROOM_SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_MS`), for the rooms whose name holds
the word; that read is quiet, as a poll is. Under the list stands "Show
more" while the last read came back full: it reads the next 50 for the
word the list was read for and adds them under the rooms shown, leaving
out a room that is already there, since the order goes by the number of
members and can move between two reads. Refresh reads the list again
for the word in the box. A read that comes back empty shows "No public
rooms yet." when the box held no word and "No public rooms match." when
it held one; neither shows before a read has come back, so not while
the first read runs and not after a first read that was refused. A
refused read is said in red in the tab, and what stood there before
stays: the rooms, or the line for an empty list. An answer that a later
read overtook is dropped. Until 2026-11-22 the tab read
/list-public-chat-rooms with an empty body when it first opened and on
Refresh, and showed the 50 newest rooms and no others.

New public room: a name, Create, the room opens. Since 2026-11-22 the
tab also shows a hint: 400 milliseconds after the last key in the name
box the wallet reads, quietly, the five public rooms with the most
members whose name holds what was typed (`LIKE_NAMED_ROOMS`), and shows
them under the box, each with Open, Requested or Request to join, under
the sentence "These public rooms already have a name like this. You can
ask to join one, or create yours.". The hint's rows are the rows of
Find public rooms, so each shows the room's picture when it has one
(4.15). The hint never stops a creation:
Create stays pressable, and Enter in the name box still creates. A hint
read that fails shows nothing, and an emptied box takes the hint away at
once.

Unread: the last message position seen in each room is kept on this
device, in localStorage under `anopod-wallet.chat-seen.<anopodId>`, read
when the session opens and raised by the conversation when it opens,
when new messages show and after a send (`markSeen`). A room is unread
when its newest message is by someone else and above that position (0
when the room was never opened here); the count of unread rooms shows at
the right of the Chat entry in the side navigation, and the room's row
shows a dot and a bold title. The count is per device: a new phone shows
every room with messages as unread until each is opened once. A count of
messages is not possible, since positions count across all rooms
(2026-11-05, section 11). The unread dot is still this device's own
list: what the masterpod keeps since 2026-11-19 (4.10) is what the other
members of a room see, the words "Sent" and "Seen" of the paragraph "One
conversation", above.

Joy (2026-11-24, section 11; 4.18): two screens. The chat, at /joy, in
the navigation and on Home once setup is complete, after Chat. One
frame as high as the screen leaves under the top bar, as the Chat page
is, at most 820 px wide and centred on a desktop. From its top: a
header with a round mark (the icon `auto_awesome`), the name "Joy",
the text link "Memory", which goes to /joy/memory, and the outlined
button "New chat"; one line on a grey ground that always stands there,
"Joy is an AI. What you write to her leaves your wallet to be
answered."; the thread; and the message box, "Message Joy", which grows
to five lines, with the round Send. Enter sends and Shift+Enter makes a
new line, as in a conversation with people. The member's messages stand
at the right, Joy's at the left, each in a bubble; a bubble of Joy's is
at most 88 percent of the frame wide, one of the member's 80. Joy's
words are drawn as she wrote them: line breaks kept (`white-space:
pre-wrap`) and nothing read as Markdown, so an asterisk shows as an
asterisk. While the chat is empty the thread says what Joy is for: "Ask
Joy anything: a question, something to write or to translate, a plan to
think through." After a send the member's message shows at once, the
box empties, Send and New chat are off, and "Joy is writing…" stands in
a bubble in grey letters until the answer's first piece has come; then
the answer shows as far as it has come and grows piece by piece. The
thread follows what is added at its end while the reader is within 120
px of the end; a reader who has gone up to read stays there. What the
page says when a message is refused, when an answer fails and when one
stops early is in 4.18: in red above the message box, with the text
back in the box, or as a grey line under the answer. New chat, off
while the chat is empty and while an answer is written, opens the
confirmation box (8.9) "Start a new chat?" with the note "This chat is
not saved anywhere. It will be gone, and it cannot be brought back."
and the buttons Cancel and New chat, and then empties the chat. The
chat is joy.service's (8.3), not the page's: leaving the page and
coming back shows the chat as it stands, an answer that is still being
written with it, and the message box keeps what was typed.
Since 2026-11-24 (section 11; 4.20) Joy can search the web, and the
chat shows two things more. While a search runs, "Joy is searching the
web…" stands in the waiting bubble, in the place of "Joy is writing…".
When Joy wrote some words before the search, the bubble holds those
words and the searching words stand under it as a small grey line, 12
px, as the line under an answer that stopped early is; the next piece
of the answer takes it away. Under a finished answer for which Joy
cited web pages stands the word "Sources", grey and 12 px, and under
it one row for each page, ten at most. A row is 32 px high: the page's
title in the primary colour, 13 px, cut with an ellipsis where the row
ends, and after it the page's site in grey, 12 px, which keeps up to
45 percent of the row. A page that gave no title shows its site in the
title's place, in the primary colour. The rows are as wide as their
longest row needs, and at most as wide as a bubble of Joy's may be,
less 8 px at each side. That does not hang on the answer's own bubble:
under an answer of one word a long title still gets that room. A row
is a link that opens the page in a new tab
(`target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener"`), so the wallet's own tab stays
as it is. Under an answer that stopped early the rows stand between
the bubble and its grey line. The thread follows the grey line and the
rows as it follows the answer, and leaves a reader who has gone up
where they are. An answer without a search looks as it did.
Since 2026-11-25 (section 11; 4.21) Joy can have a picture made, and the
chat shows three things more. While a picture is made, "Joy is making a
picture…" stands in the waiting bubble, in the place of "Joy is
writing…". When Joy wrote some words before it, the bubble holds those
words and the words on a picture stand under it as the small grey line,
12 px. The picture stands in her answer, above all of her words: 280 px
wide, and less where a bubble of Joy's has less room (266 px on a phone
of 360), with corners rounded by 16 px, on a grey ground until the
browser has drawn it. Its box is a square until then and has the
picture's own shape after; a picture of the masterpod's own settings is
a square. Directly under it stands the button "Download": outlined, 40
px high, with the download icon. Under the button stands the bubble with
her words, when she wrote any, and then, as before, the rows of sources
and the grey line of an answer that stopped early. A tap on the picture
does nothing. Download hands the picture over as a file (4.21). In the
place of a picture that the browser no longer keeps stands a grey line,
12 px: "This picture is no longer kept in this browser." The thread
follows the grey line and the picture as it follows the answer, follows
once more when the browser has opened a picture and its box has taken
the picture's shape, and leaves a reader who has gone up where they are.
An answer without a picture looks as it did.
Joy's memory, at /joy/memory: one outlined card, as the Account pages
are. The title "Joy's memory of you"; a back link "Joy"; three
paragraphs: "This is what Joy remembers about you. She reads it with
every message you send her, and she adds a line when she learns
something worth keeping.", "It is yours: change it, add to it, or
delete it." and, in the muted colour, "The file is kept encrypted, and
nobody at anoPod can open the kept file. It leaves your wallet, as your
messages do, each time you write to Joy."; the file's text in a box
"What Joy remembers", 6 to 18 lines high; under it how full the file
would be with the box's text, "12% full", in percent of the 10,240
bytes, rounded up, or in red "This is more than Joy can keep. Take some
lines out." when the box holds more; then Save, off until the box
differs from the stored file and while the text is too long, and
Delete all, outlined in red, off while the file is empty. Save stores
the box's text as the file, and "Saved." shows. Delete all opens the
confirmation box "Delete everything Joy remembers about you?" with the
note "In your next chat Joy will know nothing about you. It cannot be
undone." and a red Delete all, which stores an empty file. While an
answer of Joy's is being written both buttons are off and a line says
"Joy is answering. You can change this when she is done.": the answer's
last line may bring a file that Joy changed. A store that is refused
shows its reason in red, as every refusal does.

Marketplace (rebuilt for the phone 2026-11-06, section 11; the plan is
forclaude/wallet-marketplace-plan-1.md): four screens. Browse, at
/marketplace: one row of chips on top, scrolling sideways on a phone: All,
Selling, Buying (one chosen, All at first); Country and Currency, each
showing the chosen name or its own word and opening the picker sheet
(8.7); Sort, a menu of Newest, Price low to high and Price high to low;
Filters, with the number of ranges set, opening the filters sheet (8.7). A
chip change reads the listings again: /list-listings with the side, the
currency, the country, the sort and limit 200, open listings only. Under
the chips a "Your listings" row with a storefront icon and the line "N
open · M waiting", shown while this pod has listings or someone waits on
one (the open count from one /list-listings with mine when the page
opens, the waiting count the invites to this pod that carry a listing),
to /marketplace/mine. Then the cards (8.7) in a grid, one column on a
phone and two or three on a desktop; the quantity and price ranges are
applied on the phone over the listings loaded, the price range only once
a currency is picked; "No listings match." when nothing is left; a
refused read in red. Since 2026-11-20 (4.12; section 11) a Show more
button stands under the cards while the last read came back full, with
200 listings. A press reads the next 200 for the same chips, by offset,
and adds them under the listings shown. A listing already shown is left
out: one posted between two reads moves every row down by one. The two
ranges still apply on the phone, over the listings loaded, so with a
range set a press may add nothing that shows, and "No listings match."
can then stand with Show more under it. A chip change starts over, with
the first 200 in place of the listings shown, and the answer of a read
that a later one overtook is dropped. A refused Show more shows its line
in red beside the button, which stays.
A round + at the bottom right to /marketplace/new on
a phone, a New listing button in the chip row on a desktop. The country
and the currency picked last are remembered on the device (localStorage,
`anopod-wallet.marketplace-filters`); Browse opens with them and the
new-listing form starts from them.

Listing, at /marketplace/:listingId: /get-listing when the page opens and
after Connect, Accept, Decline and Close ("Loading" meanwhile, "This
listing does not exist." on a 404); a back arrow to /marketplace; the
price in large bold text ("35.50 THB per anos"), then "Selling 100
anos", "Total 3,550 THB", the country's name, when it was posted, and the
owner with their avatar (8.6, 56 px), username and name; a Closed banner
when closed. Someone else's listing, by this pod's own room about it
(8.3, marketplace.service): no room, a big Connect that opens the
first-message box, a textarea with "Hi, is this still available?" on a
Selling listing or "Hi, I can sell you anos. Are you still buying?" on a
Buying one, which can be changed, Send and Cancel; Send makes a private
room about the listing with a new room key, invites the owner with the
key wrapped to theirs and sends the message, and the state becomes
waiting; the owner invited, the big button disabled reading "Waiting for
somchai to accept"; the owner in, a big Open chat to the conversation; the
owner neither, "somchai did not accept." and Connect again, the box
again, the invite and the message into the same room. A closed listing
shows "This listing is closed." instead of Connect and keeps Open chat
when a room exists. The error line in red under the button; without chat
keys "No chat keys in this tab: unlock again." and Connect disabled. This
pod's own listing: the people who connected (8.7) and, for an open
listing, Close listing, which asks once in place ("Close this listing?
People can no longer connect; your chats stay.", Yes or Back) and calls
/close-listing; a closed one has nothing to do.

New listing, at /marketplace/new: a back arrow; two large toggle buttons,
"I am selling anos" and "I am buying anos" (selling at first); the
quantity in anos (up to six decimals); the price per anos (a decimal, up
to eight decimals, two usual); Currency and Country as buttons that open
the picker sheet (8.7) and show the chosen name, the remembered ones at
first; a live "Total 3,550 THB" once the three are in; Create listing,
which calls /create-listing (side, quantity in millionths, currency,
country, price; no room and no key work) and opens the listing's page; the
refusal in red. At the masterpod's 403 listing limit reached (4.12, since
2026-11-20) the line is one sentence: "You have reached the limit of open
listings. Close one of your listings to create a new one."

Your listings, at /marketplace/mine: a back arrow; /list-listings with
mine and status any when the page opens and after a Close: the open
listings first, newest first, then the closed ones; each a card (8.7)
with, under it, the people who connected (8.7) and, for an open listing,
Close, asking once as on the listing page. "You have no listings yet."
with a New listing button when there are none.

The prices (src/app/prices.ts): a price shows with at least two decimals,
the whole part grouped by the browser's locale and the currency code after
the number, never a symbol ("35.50 THB"); a total is the quantity times
the price rounded to two decimals on the digits (BigInt, as amounts.ts
does amounts), shown without decimals when whole ("3,550 THB", else
"3,554.38 THB"); the currencies and their names come from
Intl.supportedValuesOf and Intl.DisplayNames, the countries' names from
Intl.DisplayNames (src/app/countries.ts, countryName). Nobody types a
currency or country code, an anopod id or an account id: the pickers show
names, people are found by username and selfie. The old group room per
listing is not made any more; old marketplace rooms stay in Chat for the
people in them, and Request to join stays for public rooms (Chat, New
chat).

DAO (2026-11-08, section 11; the plan is forclaude/dao-voting-plan-1.md,
the masterpod's routes its spec's section 15): three screens, two of them
step 4 and the third step 5. The wallet reads and writes the ledger
through the masterpod alone; it never asks a validator for DAO stake. One
staked anos of the daoVote purpose is one DAO vote; a pod's weight in a
proposal is fixed by the masterpod's snapshot when the proposal is posted
and again when it goes to a vote, so stake added later counts from the
next proposal.

DAO, at /dao: a header "DAO" with a Refresh icon button and, on a
desktop, a New proposal button (a round + at the bottom right on a
phone, as Browse); then the notice, an info icon and one paragraph in the
plain muted style on a surface-container background with 12 px corners,
never the error container: "DAO proposals come from people who staked
anos for daoVote. One staked anos is one vote. Anyone with votes can post
a proposal. It goes to a vote once 15 percent of all DAO votes support
it, and then everyone votes for or against for 14 days. An accepted
proposal records what the community decided. It moves no money and
changes nothing by itself.", the two numbers from the `settings` the
masterpod answers with every list (the minutes turned into days by
Math.round(minutes / 1440)), shown once the first list answered; then,
since 2026-11-08 (section 11; the Guardians plan,
forclaude/wallet-guardians-plan-1.md), one outlined card the width of the
page, for everyone: a shield icon, "Guardians" in bold with "The fund's
proposals and the guardians' votes" under it and a chevron at the right,
the whole card a link to /dao/guardians (the Guardians paragraphs below);
it says nothing about the caller, since the Guardians page reads the
caller's accounts itself; then three tabs, Open votes, Pending and
Decided. A tab reads
/list-dao-proposals for its status (open, pending, decided: accepted and
rejected together) when it is first shown and on Refresh, 20 at a time,
newest first, and Show more reads 20 more by offset while the last page
came back full (the list has no more flag); Refresh forgets every tab and
reads the one on screen again, the others when they are shown next. The
Decided tab has a date range above its cards, as the history page: both
days picked, or both cleared, read again, with from at the start of the
first day and to at the start of the day after the last (the masterpod
takes from inclusive and to exclusive, on decidedAt). The cards, one
column on a phone and two on a desktop: the title in bold; "by somchai ·
posted Nov 8, 2026" (the date without the time); then the state line.
Pending: "25 of 180 votes in support" with a progress bar of the support
over the support needed and "5 days left" (the whole days to
pendingUntil, or the hours, rounded up, under a day). Open: "For 120 ·
Against 40" and "closes Nov 22, 2026, 3:50:12 PM". Decided: Accepted or
Rejected as a small label, green or red, the for and against, and
"decided Nov 22, 2026, 3:50:12 PM". Under it, when the caller acted: "You
supported this" with a green thumb_up on a pending card; "You voted for"
or "You voted against" with the green thumb_up or the red thumb_down on
an open or decided one (a support is not a vote, everyone votes fresh).
The green is #2e7d32 and the red var(--mat-sys-error), Material's icons,
never emojis. A card opens /dao/<id>. The tab's empty line when nothing
came back: "No proposal is open for votes.", "No proposal is collecting
support.", "No proposal has been decided yet."; a refused read in red
under the tab ("/list-dao-proposals: HTTP 404: Not Found" against a
masterpod without the routes), and the rest of the wallet works.

New proposal, at /dao/new (step 4): a back arrow to /dao; Title (100
characters at most, a counter "12/100" under it); Your proposal, a
textarea of 10 rows (5,000 at most, its counter); under them the rule
once the settings came, read quietly with /list-dao-proposals { status:
'open', limit: 1 } when the page opens: "Your proposal needs support from
15 percent of all DAO votes within 7 days to go to a vote. Posting it
counts as your own support. You need at least 1 DAO vote(s) to post.";
Post proposal, disabled until both fields have text and while busy. Post
calls /create-dao-proposal with the trimmed fields; a 201 opens
/dao/<proposalId> (the masterpod answers status pending, or open when the
proposer's own weight alone reaches the support needed). The refusals in
words: not enough DAO votes, "You need at least 1 DAO votes to post a
proposal. Stake anos for daoVote from a spending account."; a pending
proposal is already open, "You already have a pending proposal. Wait
until it goes to a vote or expires."; validators unreachable, "The
validators did not answer. Try again in a moment."; the rest
"/create-dao-proposal: HTTP 400: invalid title" and the like.

Proposal, at /dao/:proposalId (step 5, 2026-11-08, section 11), in the
frame of the listing page: a back arrow to /dao and a Refresh icon
button; /get-dao-proposal when the page opens, after each action and on
Refresh, "Loading" until the first answer, "This proposal does not
exist." on a 404, any other refusal in red ("/get-dao-proposal: HTTP
404: Not Found" against a masterpod without the routes). Top to bottom:
the status as a small bordered label ("Pending", "Open for votes",
"Accepted" in green, "Rejected" in red, "Expired" muted); the title as
the heading; the proposer's avatar (8.6, 40 px) with "by somchai ·
posted Nov 8, 2026" (the date without the time); the text in a
paragraph with white-space pre-wrap, shown as typed, line breaks kept
and nothing rendered; the numbers: pending, and expired, "25 of 180
votes in support" with the progress bar and "until Nov 15, 2026,
12:00:00 PM"; open, "For 120 · Against 40" in large type and "closes
Nov 22, 2026, 3:50:12 PM"; decided, "For 120 · Against 40" and "decided
Nov 22, 2026, 3:50:12 PM" (the label at the top is the result); then
"1200 DAO votes in this proposal's snapshot". Your part: "Your votes in
this proposal: 12", or at 0 "You have no votes in this proposal's
snapshot. Anos staked after it was posted count from the next
proposal." Then the action, one per pod per stage, no undo, asked in
place: pending, with votes and not yet supported, one big outlined
button with the green thumb_up, "Support with 12 votes", which asks
"Add your 12 votes in support of this proposal? It cannot be undone."
with "Yes, support" and Back; Yes calls /support-dao-proposal, shows
"Your support is recorded." in green and reads the proposal again (it
may now be open). Open, with votes and not yet voted, two big outlined
buttons side by side, the green thumb_up "For" and the red thumb_down
"Against"; either asks "Vote for this proposal with 12 votes? It cannot
be undone." with "Yes, vote for" and Back; Yes calls /vote-dao-proposal,
shows "Your vote for is recorded." in green and reads again. After the
caller acted: "You supported this" on a pending proposal, "You voted
for" or "You voted against" on an open or decided one, with the icon
and no button; without votes in the snapshot, no button. The refusals
in words: already supported and already voted, "You already acted on
this proposal."; no DAO votes in this proposal, the no-votes sentence;
proposal not pending, proposal not open, proposal expired and voting
closed, "This proposal is no longer taking votes." with the proposal
read again; validators unreachable, "The validators did not answer. Try
again in a moment."; the rest "/vote-dao-proposal: HTTP 400: invalid
vote" and the like. Below, the public lists from /list-dao-votes, 50
rows at a time, newest first, Show more by offset while a page came
back full: once the proposal has opened, a heading "Votes" with the
official-stage rows; then a heading "Supported by" with the
pending-stage rows. A row: the username ("unknown pod" when the pod's
row is gone) with a small "you" tag on the caller's own row (the row's
anopodId against the session's), the time under it, and at the right
the colored thumb icon with "12 votes". "No votes yet." under an empty
heading once its list answered; a refused list in red under its heading.
The Home line "2 proposals open for your vote" is in the Home paragraph
above.

Guardians (2026-11-08, section 11; the plan is
forclaude/wallet-guardians-plan-1.md, the validator's reads anossoftware
spec 25, the doorman's lines doormansoftware spec 7): where the fund's
proposals and the guardians' votes are seen and acted on, three screens
under the DAO page, two of them step 3 and the third step 4. The guts are
the validator's as they were (the fundProposal transaction, the
guardianVote follow-up, the tally in the leader round: one vote per
GUARDIAN_VOTE_ANOS staked for guardian, the vote open for
GUARDIAN_VOTE_MINUTES, passed at GUARDIAN_VOTE_PERCENT of the votes for);
what is new is the reading side, two public reads built like
/list-dao-stakes, /list-fund-proposals and /get-fund-proposal (5.4), and
the two stake fields of /get-account. The data comes from the session's
validator (8.3; the wallet's defaultValidator until 2026-11-10) through
its doorman and the proxy, never from the
masterpod. Everyone signed in may look; an account with at least one
guardian vote acts, and every guardian account of the pod acts on its own
with its own weight, since the validators count guardian stake per
account and never per pod (a pod with two staked spending accounts votes
from each). Guardians and recipients are shown by account id in short
form, "a1b2c3d4…e5f6", with a copy button, as the history and the Home
lines show accounts: the validators know account ids only, and a username
lookup by account id is a later step. Every number in the words
(1,000 anos per vote, 70 percent, 60 minutes on the testnet and a week in
production, the 1,000 anos least stake) comes from the `settings` the
validator answers with every read, never from the wallet.

Guardians, at /dao/guardians (step 3), in the frame of the DAO page: a
header with a back arrow to /dao, "Guardians", a Refresh icon button and,
on a desktop, a New proposal button (a round + at the bottom right on a
phone); the notice, an info icon and one paragraph in the plain muted
style on a surface-container background with 12 px corners, never the
error container, once the first list answered: "Fund proposals come from
guardians, people who staked anos for guardian. One vote per 1000 anos
staked. A guardian proposes payments from the fund, and the guardians
vote for or against for 1 hour. The proposal passes when at least 70
percent of the votes are for, and the next round moves the money." (the
time through the dictionary's `minutes`, so 10080 reads "7 days"); then
"Your guardian accounts": when the page opens and on Refresh, /get-account
for each of the pod's accounts, quietly, signed by pair one opened from
the keyBlob and dropped (guardian-accounts.service, 8.3), "Reading…"
meanwhile; the accounts whose guardianVotes is at least 1, as the short
id with a copy button and "3 votes" ("1 vote" at one), the one with the
most votes first; with none, "None of your accounts has guardian votes. To
become a guardian, stake 1000 anos or more for guardian from a spending
account, on its page in the Wallet." with the least stake from the
settings and a Wallet button to /wallet (nothing under the heading while
the settings are unknown: the refusal under the tab says why). New
proposal is enabled with a guardian account and no proposal in the Open
vote tab; a refused list leaves it enabled, since the validator refuses
with words. Two tabs. Open vote reads /list-fund-proposals { status:
'open' } when the page opens and on Refresh: one card at most (the fund
holds one proposal), or "No fund proposal is open.". Decided reads {
status: 'decided', limit: 20, offset } when it is first shown and on
Refresh, newest first, Show more reads 20 more by offset while the last
page came back full, and has a date range above its cards as the DAO's
Decided tab (both days picked, or both cleared, read again; from at the
start of the first day, to at the start of the day after the last, on
the decision's moment); "No fund proposal has been decided yet." when
nothing came back. Refresh forgets both tabs, reads the one on screen
again and the accounts again. The cards, one column on a phone and two on
a desktop: "Fund proposal" and the short id in bold; "proposed by
a1b2c3d4…e5f6 · Nov 8, 2026" (the date without the time); "2 payouts ·
1500 anos" ("1 payout" at one), the count and the sum the validator
answers; then the state line: open, "For 5 · Against 2", a progress bar
of for over for plus against, "needs 70 percent for · closes Nov 8, 2026,
4:50:12 PM"; waiting, "Waiting for the validators"; closing, "Vote closed,
waiting for the next round"; decided, the status as a small label,
"Passed, the money moved" in green or "Failed" in red (a status the
wallet does not know shows its own word, neither colour), "For 5 ·
Against 2" and "decided Nov 8, 2026, 5:00:00 PM". Under it, "You proposed
this" with the green thumb_up when the proposer is one of the caller's
guardian accounts, or "You voted for" / "You voted against" with the
green thumb_up or the red thumb_down when one of them is in the votes
(the biggest account's vote when they differ). The green is #2e7d32 and
the red var(--mat-sys-error), as on the DAO page. A card opens
/dao/guardians/<id>. A refused read in red under the tab
("/list-fund-proposals: HTTP 404: Not Found" against a validator or a
doorman without the route), and the rest of the wallet works.

New fund proposal, at /dao/guardians/new (step 3), in the frame of the
DAO's New proposal page: a back arrow to /dao/guardians; "Proposing as", a
select of the caller's guardian accounts read as the Guardians page reads
them, each option the short id and "3 votes", the biggest first and
selected (a proposal is one transaction signed by one account; with one
guardian account the select has one option; without one, the
become-a-guardian sentence and Post stays disabled); the payout rows, the
form that left the account page, each in an outlined box: Recipient
account id (64 hex characters, with the paste button Send has, which
takes the run of 64 hex characters on the clipboard and says under the
box when the browser refused or nothing there looks like an id), Amount
(anos), Reason, Returns stake (no, or one of the six purposes) and a
remove button, disabled on the last row; Add payout; the rule once the
settings came, read quietly with /list-fund-proposals { status: 'open' }
when the page opens, which also tells whether a proposal is open: "The
guardians vote for 1 hour. The proposal passes when at least 70 percent
of the votes are for; your own votes count as the first votes for. One
fund proposal can be open at a time."; Post proposal, disabled while
busy, without a guardian account, or while a proposal is open, "A fund
proposal is already open. Wait until it is decided." shown as the reason
(a refused quiet read shows in red instead, and Post stays enabled: the
validator refuses with words). Over the button, above the red error
line, stands the passkey line in the page's muted grey since 2026-11-19
(section 11): "To confirm, this phone or computer will ask for your
passkey, the one you log in with." Post checks each row ("Payout 2: the
recipient must be an account id of 64 hex characters", "Payout 2: the
amount must be anos with up to six decimals"; the recipient lower-cased,
the amount as millionths, the reason trimmed, stakeFor only when picked),
so a row that is wrong is said before any passkey is asked; then it
opens pair one of the chosen account for the signature and drops it,
builds the fundProposal (crypto.buildFundProposal: the fund as accountId,
the chosen account as guardianId, no previousTransactionId), and
then asks the device for the passkey that opened the session, for
exactly that proposal (the
passkey check, 8.9; the check since 2026-11-19, and since 2026-11-20,
section 11, after the build and for what was built), and a check that
does not pass shows its sentence
in the error line with nothing sent; then it has /api/sign/<n>
add the wallet pair, with the passkey's answer sent along (section 3),
and posts /fund-proposal; a 202 opens
/dao/guardians/<transactionId>. The refusals in words: "a fund proposal is
already open" (the validator's held check), the sentence above; "the
proposer has no guardian vote", "This account has no guardian votes.";
the rest "/fund-proposal: HTTP 400: payload.payouts[0].reason must be a
string" and the like.

Fund proposal, at /dao/guardians/:transactionId (step 4, 2026-11-08,
section 11), in the frame of the DAO's Proposal page: a back arrow to
/dao/guardians and a Refresh icon button; /get-fund-proposal when the
page opens, after each action and on Refresh, "Loading" until the first
answer, "This proposal does not exist." on the validator's 404 unknown
proposal, any other refusal in red ("/get-fund-proposal: HTTP 404: Not
Found" against a validator or a doorman without the route). Top to
bottom: the status as a small bordered label, the five words of the
Guardians page's cards, "Passed, the money moved" in green and "Failed"
in red (a word the wallet does not know as it is, no colour); "Fund
proposal a1b2c3d4…e5f6" as the heading with a copy button for the id;
"proposed by a1b2c3d4…e5f6 · Nov 8, 2026" (the date without the time);
the payouts, one row each in the validator's index order: "1500 anos to
a1b2c3d4…e5f6" with a copy button for the recipient, the reason under
it when there is one, and "returns guardian stake" (the purpose's wire
word, as the notice says "for guardian") when the payout returns stake;
then the total line, "2 payouts · 1500 anos" ("1 payout" at one); the
numbers: "For 5 · Against 2", in large type while the vote is open, with
the progress bar of for over for plus against and "needs 70 percent for
· closes Nov 8, 2026, 4:50:12 PM" on an open proposal; the tally and the
needs and closes line on a waiting one (the label at the top says it
waits for the validators); the tally alone on a closing one; the tally
and "decided Nov 8, 2026, 5:00:00 PM" on a decided one (the label at the
top is the result). Your part (the plan's decision 8: every guardian
account of the pod votes, one at a time): "Reading…" while the pod's
guardian accounts are read (guardian-accounts.service, 8.3, as the
Guardians page reads them); with none, the become-a-guardian sentence of
the Guardians page with the least stake from the settings and no select;
else "Voting as", a select of the guardian accounts, each option the
short id, "3 votes" and its state, "You proposed this", "You voted for"
/ "You voted against" or, while the vote is open, "can vote" (nothing
for an account that neither proposed nor voted on a proposal that is
not open); the first account that can still vote is selected when the
page opens, the first in the list when none can (with one guardian
account the select has one option). Under the select the selected
account's state: "You proposed this" with the green thumb_up, "You voted
for" / "You voted against" with the colored thumb, or, while the status
is open and the account is neither the proposer nor in the votes, two
big outlined buttons side by side, the green thumb_up "For" and the red
thumb_down "Against", the DAO page's pair; either asks in place, "Vote
for with 3 votes from a1b2c3d4…e5f6? It cannot be undone.", with the
passkey line under it, small and grey, since 2026-11-19 (section 11),
"To confirm, this phone or computer will ask for your passkey, the one
you log in with.", and with "Yes,
vote for" and Back (a new pick in the select closes the question, which
named the account). Yes opens pair one of the selected account from its
keyBlob for the signature and drops it, builds the guardianVote
follow-up (crypto.buildFollowUp: type guardianVote, the proposal's
transactionId, the account as guardianId, the vote), and then asks the
device for the passkey that
opened the session, for exactly that vote (the passkey check, 8.9; the
check since 2026-11-19, and since 2026-11-20, section 11, after the
build and for what was built): a build or a check that
does not pass shows its sentence in the red error line and leaves the
question open, so Yes can be pressed again, where every later failure
closes the question. Then Yes has /api/sign/<n> add
the wallet pair, with the passkey's answer sent along (section 3), and
posts /guardian-vote; a 202 shows "Your vote for is
sent to the validators." in green (the thumb green, #2e7d32) and reads
the proposal again, where the vote shows as waiting for approval until
every validator accepted it, and the select moves to the next account
that can still vote, so the next vote is one pick away (it stays when
none can). The refusals in words, matched on the validator's own text
(anossoftware src/fund/guardian-vote.js): "the vote on this proposal has
closed", "The vote on this proposal has closed." with the proposal read
again; "this guardian has already voted on this proposal", "This account
