already voted."; "the guardian has no guardian vote", "This account has
no guardian votes."; "payload.guardianId is the proposer, whose vote for
is already counted", "You proposed this"; the rest with the path,
"/guardian-vote: HTTP 400: payload.vote must be …" and the like. Below,
a heading "Votes": the first row the proposer, the short id with a copy
button (tagged "you" when it is one of the pod's accounts), the time the
proposal was made under it, and at the right the green thumb_up with
"proposer · 3 votes for" (proposerWeight, the proposer's votes when the
proposal was stored); then one row per vote in the validator's order
(guardian id order): the short id with a copy button and the "you" tag
on the pod's own, "approved" or "waiting for approval" and the time
under it, and at the right the colored thumb with "3 votes"; "No votes
yet." under the proposer alone. Refresh reads the proposal and the
guardian accounts again and clears the two messages. The green is
#2e7d32 and the red var(--mat-sys-error), as on the DAO pages. The Home
line "A fund proposal is open for your vote" is in the Home paragraph
above.

Notifications: the list, newest first, mark read (since 2026-11-25 with
a new look and no button: the paragraphs "Since 2026-11-25" below); the
5-second poll runs while a session is open and updates the status (vouched, counts),
and the chat rooms with them once setup is complete. Since 2026-11-24
(section 11; 4.17) the poll's read of the chat rooms asks only for what
is new: about 100 bytes come back while nothing is new, where the whole
list came before. Its two other reads are as they were. Since 2026-11-25
(section 11; 4.22) the poll's read of the notifications asks only for
what is new too: 54 bytes come back while nothing is new, where the
newest 100 notifications came whole. Since 2026-11-19
(section 11) the poll also rings the wallet's sound when its read of the
chat rooms holds a new message from someone else or a new chat request
(8.1). A notification by itself rings nothing: a chat request rings
because it is in the answer of /list-chat-rooms. Since 2026-11-22
(section 11) the poll's status read also tells the end of a login (8.1),
and the poll runs at once when the page comes back to the front. The
chat kinds
link: chatInvite and joinRequest to /chat/requests; inviteAccepted,
inviteDeclined and joinApproved to the room, /chat/:chatRoomId
(2026-11-05, section 11). The kind recoveryCaseScheduled (2026-11-12,
section 11; masterpod 14.7), which the masterpod writes to the person
when an attestor sets up the video call of their recovery case, reads "A
video call was scheduled for your recovery" and links to the person's
recovery case page, /cases/recovery/:caseId (13.3): its reference id is
the case id. The kind passkeyAdded (2026-11-18, section 11; masterpod
19.4), which the masterpod writes to the anoPod when a passkey is added
to it, reads "A passkey was added to your anoPod" and links to the
Passkeys page, /account/passkeys; its reference id is the new passkey's
id, which the link does not use.
The four kinds of the security alerts (2026-11-21, section 11; masterpod
25.5), which the masterpod writes to the pod whether or not it has an
email or a phone on its list. transferWaiting reads "A transfer is
waiting to leave one of your accounts" and links to that account's page,
/wallet/:accountId: its reference id is the account's id.
recoveryMoveWaiting reads "A recovery is moving anos out of one of your
accounts" and recoveryCaseOpened "A recovery was started for your
anoPod"; neither links anywhere. alertSettingsChanged, one kind for
every change of the pod's alert list, reads "Your security alerts were
changed" and links to the Security alerts page, /account/alerts; its
reference id is the pod's own id, which the link does not use.

Since 2026-11-25 (section 11; 4.22; the plan is
forclaude/notifications-page-plan-1.md) the Notifications page has a new
look. It is a frame of at most 720 pixels, in the middle of its room on
a wide screen, where the card was as wide as the page. Top to bottom:
the title "Notifications"; a row of five filters, chips, All, Security,
Chat, Cases and Vouching, which scrolls sideways inside its strip on a
phone; the rows; and "Show older" under them while older rows are left.
A row is a round disc of 40 px with the icon of the row's group, the
kind's sentence whole, on as many lines as it needs, and under it the
time in small grey letters. The four groups, which are the wallet's own
list: Security is passkeyAdded, transferWaiting, recoveryMoveWaiting,
recoveryCaseOpened and alertSettingsChanged, a shield with a lock
(shield_lock) on a red disc; Chat is chatInvite, inviteAccepted,
inviteDeclined, joinRequest, joinApproved and joinDeclined; Cases is
tradeCaseOpened, disputeCaseOpened, caseScheduled, caseDecided,
caseDismissed and recoveryCaseScheduled; Vouching is vouchRequest,
vouchApproved, vouchDeclined and vouched. Chat, Cases and Vouching have
a grey disc with the icon of the menu's Chat, Cases and Vouch requests
entries (chat, folder_shared, verified_user). The time reads "Just now"
in the first minute, then "5 min ago", then "3 h ago" up to 24 hours,
and after that as the chat list words a day: "Yesterday", the weekday
within six days, else the date ("Nov 18"), with the year when it is
another year. The whole row is the link, where it was the sentence
alone: for the fourteen kinds that were links before, which lead where
they led (above), and for vouchRequest, "Someone asked you to vouch for
them", which leads to the Vouch requests page, /seed. The other six
kinds are rows like the others and no link: vouchApproved,
vouchDeclined, vouched, joinDeclined, recoveryMoveWaiting and
recoveryCaseOpened. A kind that the wallet does not know shows its name
as its sentence, as before, with a bell on a grey disc; it is no link
and shows under All only. Gone are the subtitle "Newest first; refreshed
every 5 seconds", the envelope, the date with seconds, the 16 characters
of the reference id, and the two buttons under the list, "Mark N read"
and "Refresh".

Since the same day the page marks by itself (4.22). The rows that are
unread when the page opens stand first, under the heading "New", each
with a bold sentence and a blue dot at its right; the rest stand under
"Earlier". With no unread row the page has neither heading. Opening the
page marks everything read with one request, so the number in the menu
and on Home goes to zero, and the rows keep their dot for as long as the
page is open: after a tap on a row and the way back, no row has one. A
new notification comes onto the open page by itself within 5 seconds,
on top under "New" with its dot, and is marked read at once. A tap on a
filter shows the rows of its group, the newest 30; a row keeps its dot
under a filter; a tap on the filter that is on takes it off, which is
All. "Show older" brings 30 more rows with each tap and is off while
its read is on its way; an older row that was still unread comes
without a dot, since it was marked with the rest when the page opened.
A list with no row says "No notifications yet.", a filter with none "No
notifications of this kind.", and the page says "Loading" while a read
of its own is on its way and no row is there to show. A read of the
page that fails shows a red line with the path and the reason. The page
draws the list in memory, which the shell's poll keeps, and asks the
masterpod for no rows when it opens, except in the first seconds after
a login; until this step it read the whole list again at its opening
and after "Mark N read".

Seed: the Vouch requests page, for a seed or super seed (2026-11-08,
section 11). One small call, /list-vouch-requests, answers the open
requests without pictures, so the seed sees every card at once; until
that first answer the list's place shows a spinner and "Fetching…",
never again after it. Each card shows the requester's avatar (8.6), the
picture read through the profile cache (8.3) five at a time, the letter
disc until it arrives. Approve and Decline disable only their own card's
two buttons, so several can be approved back to back; on success, or on
a 404 (the request was handled from another device), the card goes and
nothing is fetched again; any other refusal stays on the card as its
reason. A quiet 5-second poll (VOUCH_REQUESTS_POLL_MS) re-reads the list
while the page is open, skipped while a read is in flight, and its
answer never brings back a request handled on this page since it opened.
Refresh is the manual retry after a page-level error.

Log: the test apps' call log, newest 40, path, status and answer, polls
excepted, with the keyholder and anos calls included.

                            and getFundProposal(transactionId, quiet), each a plain unsigned post with the

                            FundProposalItem, FundProposal and FundListFilters; AccountAnswer carries the
                            optional stakes and guardianVotes of /get-account (5.4);
                            the session's validator (2026-11-10, section 11): the wallet talks to one validator
                            per session, a session being one load of the wallet in a tab, so a reload picks
                            again; the first call picks it at random (Math.random) from 1 to the validators of
                            /api/config, and every call goes to it, since the wallet reads an account and then
                            builds a transfer on what it read and a balance refresh makes several reads at the
                            same moment; validator() answers it, picking it when none is set, for the attestor
                            case pages (13.3); no answer is status 0 (the network failed, or a read ran into
                            its time limit), 502 (the proxy's "validator n unavailable", a doorman's "worker
                            unavailable"), 503 (a just booted validator's "not counted yet") or 504 (a
                            doorman's "worker timeout"), and every other status is an answer, a refusal and a
                            500 included; with no answer the session moves to the next validator in the list,
                            the first after the last, and stays there, by one place however many calls got no
                            answer from that validator at the same moment; the nine reads (read: /get-account,
                            /list-transactions, /list-escrows, /get-assisted-transfer, /get-locked-transfer,
                            /list-assisted-transfers, /list-disputed-escrows, /list-fund-proposals,
                            /get-fund-proposal) wait at most VALIDATOR_READ_TIMEOUT_MS, 10 seconds
                            (constants.ts), and with no answer are asked again on the next validator, each
                            validator at most once per call, the last failure returned when none answers; the
                            nine submissions (write: /create-account, /anos-transfer, /transfer-to-fund,

                            ROOM_PICTURE_RETRY_MS (30 seconds) later, and not at once: the disc stands meanwhile,

                            after-production item "faces: a failed read is asked again at once, over and over");

    room-copies.service     the chat rooms' copies (2026-11-25, section 11; 8.2, Chat; the plan is
                            forclaude/chat-rooms-kept-plan-1.md, section 7): for every room a person has opened,
                            a copy of the room's thread as the conversation page last had it. The page stays the
                            one place that holds the open room's thread; this service holds the copies. A copy
                            (RoomCopy) is { messages, changes, lowest, highest, olderLeft }. messages: each
                            message once, by its id, oldest first, a KeptMessage { messageId, position,
                            senderAnopodId, createdAt, own }, where own is the message's own decrypted text as a
                            KeptText, { opened: true, text } or, for a text that did not open under the room
                            key, { opened: false }, never the sentence the thread shows for it, which the page
                            makes when it draws, in the language of that moment; own is null when the row came
                            without its ciphertext, and when an edit or a delete names the message, so the text
                            of before is not kept. changes: for each message that an edit or a delete names, the
                            newest such row, { target, change }, target the named message's id and change a
                            KeptChange, { kind: 'delete', position } or { kind: 'edit', position, text }, text a
                            KeptText. lowest and highest: the lowest and the highest position the page's reads
                            have covered, 0 and 0 for a room with no row; highest is never the position of a
                            message the person has just sent, nor of their own edit or delete, since the read
                            that follows brings those rows. olderLeft: whether the masterpod has rows below
                            lowest. A copy holds nothing that the page works out from a text (the pieces, the
                            sticker, a trade's grey line), no message that is still being sent, nothing of a
                            read that was made without the room's key, and not how far the other members have
                            read, which is in the chat list in memory. A copy is in two places. In the page's
                            memory, by the room's id: everything the page has read of the room, never cut,
                            until the page is loaded again, which Lock does too, or until another pod is in the
                            tab (an effect on session.anopodId, and every call looks again). In the browser's
                            own database (IndexedDB): the database `anopod-wallet-chat`, version 1, with one
                            place, the object store `chat-messages`; one entry for each room, its key the
                            anoPod's id, one space, the room's id; its value the bytes of wrapJson (7) of
                            { v: 1 } and the copy, under the anoPod encryption key. No key is stored with it, so
                            an entry opens only after a passkey login of the same pod, and another pod in the
                            same browser has entries of its own. It stays after Lock. The database is the rooms'
                            own, and the seven small functions that name its entries and read and write it stand
                            at the end of the file (entryKey, openDb, inStore, readEntry, writeEntry,
                            deleteEntry, entriesOf); the chat with Joy
                            is in the database `anopod-wallet`, which nothing of this file opens, and
                            joy.service is not changed. The cut for the browser's database (cut): the newest
                            KEPT_MESSAGES (200) messages, and fewer when their texts are over KEPT_TEXT_BYTES
                            (1,000,000) bytes of UTF-8 together, a message's texts being its own and that of the
                            edit kept for it; the newest message is always kept; a copy that was cut has the
                            position of its oldest kept message as lowest and olderLeft true, and keeps of the
                            edits and the deletes those whose own position is above that lowest position, also
                            when the message one names is not kept: that message comes without its ciphertext
                            with a later read of older rows and is drawn by this row. Both constants stand in
                            the file. Five methods. held(chatRoomId): the copy in memory, or null, at once.
                            stored(chatRoomId, lastPosition): the copy from the browser's database, opened, one
                            read and one decryption, after the writes that are still on their way; null when
                            there is none, when the entry does not open under this anoPod encryption key, when
                            what it holds is not a copy (another version, or a part that has not the form this
                            file writes: copyOf checks every part and takes nothing else over), and when the
                            browser refuses its database; a copy whose highest position is above lastPosition,
                            the room's in the chat list, is ahead of the masterpod and is dropped; a copy that
                            is found is in memory from then on. keep(chatRoomId, copy), the page's call each
                            time an answer of the masterpod changed the thread: the copy into memory, and its
                            cut into the browser's database; nothing for a room that is not in the chat list in
                            memory, so an answer that was on its way while the person left brings no deleted
                            copy back; without the anoPod encryption key the copy stays in memory alone; when a
                            copy of the room already waits to be written, the new one takes its place.
                            drop(chatRoomId), the page's call after a full answer: the copy out of memory and
                            out of the browser's database. keepOnly(chatRoomIds), chat.service's call for every
                            whole chat list: the copy of every other room is deleted, in memory and, for this
                            pod's entries, in the browser's database, where another pod's entries are not
                            touched; this look makes the database when it is not there yet, so a browser has
                            it, empty, from a login's first chat list on. The writes to the browser's database
                            go one after the other, and one that fails is passed over (private mode, blocked
                            storage, no room): the copy then stays in the page's memory
    stickers.service        the stickers' list (2026-11-23, section 11; 4.16): sets, a signal, every set of this

    signing.service         the signing servers through the proxy (2026-11-13, section 11; until then
                            /api/sign/public-keys and /api/sign on one server): publicKeys(), GET
                            /api/sign/<n>/public-keys, and sign(transaction, signerAccountId), POST /api/sign/<n>, n
                            being the session's signing server; the wallet uses one signing server per session, a

                            answers one of its wallet pairs, picked at random, and the session keeps none; a

                            approve(action, accountId, transactionId), which the Yes of the page's confirmation
                            box runs (the box's `approve`, 8.9), opens pair one and builds the follow-up as
                            send did, asks the passkey for exactly that follow-up (askSigningPasskey) and
                            resolves with an ApprovedEscrowAction, the account, the follow-up and the passkey's
                            answer; and send(approved), which the page runs after the box, has /api/sign/<n>
                            add the wallet pair, with the passkey's answer sent along, posts the follow-up to
                            /escrow-signature and resolves to that answer
    sound.service           the wallet's one sound and its switch (2026-11-19, section 11; 8.1): on, a signal, true
                            while the sound is on, on this device, read once, when the wallet loads, from
                            localStorage under `anopod-wallet.sound`: 'off' there means off, anything else, or
                            nothing, means on, and a browser that refuses the read gives on; the key is the
                            device's and not a pod's, so it holds no anoPod id and a Lock leaves it;
                            setOn(value), the switch of the Account page (8.2, Account): it sets the signal,
                            removes the key for on and writes 'off' for off, and for on it calls chime();
                            chime(), the sound: two sine notes, 880 Hz for 0.12 seconds and 1174.66 Hz for 0.22
                            seconds, the second starting 0.14 seconds after the first, each coming in within
                            0.01 seconds to a gain of 0.2 and fading out; it plays nothing while the switch is
                            off, while there is no engine yet, or while the engine's state is not "running";
                            the engine is the browser's AudioContext, made at the first click, touchend or
                            keydown of the tab, which the service listens for on the document in the capture
                            phase, since a browser lets a page make sound only after the person has touched it;
                            the engine is resumed at each such event while it is not running, and when the
                            page becomes visible again (visibilitychange); a browser without an AudioContext,
                            or one that refuses, leaves the wallet silent, and nothing is shown; the shell
                            calls chime() from its poll (app.ts, ring; 8.1)
    alerts.service          the security alerts of the pod (2026-11-21, section 11; 8.2, Security alerts; 4.13):
                            settings, a signal, the pod's list as /list-alert-settings last answered it, null until
                            read; an effect sets it back to null whenever the session's anoPod changes, so that one
                            anoPod never sees another's list in the same tab (a change alone does it: the effect's
                            first run leaves the list as it is); nothingSet, true when the list is read and holds
                            no confirmed email and no phone, which the account page asks (8.2, Account);
                            load(quiet), the read: a
                            good answer goes into the signal, and the answer is returned; ensureLoaded(), a quiet
                            load when the signal is null; then the phone's part, which is this browser on this
                            device: device(), `tab` when the wallet was not opened from the Home Screen (neither the
                            display mode standalone nor an iPhone's own navigator.standalone says so), else
                            `unsupported` when the browser lacks a service worker, the push manager or
                            notifications, else `ready`; label(), the kind of device from the user agent, in this
                            order: iphone when it holds "iPhone"; ipad when it holds "iPad", or "Macintosh" with
                            more than one touch point; android when it holds "Android"; computer when it holds
                            "Windows", "Macintosh", "Linux" or "CrOS"; else other; permission(), the browser's
                            Notification.permission, or denied where the browser has no notifications;
                            thisEndpointHash(), the SHA-256 of this browser's delivery address as 64 hex characters,
                            what the list names a phone by, from the worker's registration for "/" and its
                            subscription, null when there is neither or when anything throws; turnOn(key), called
                            straight from the button's tap, in this order: Notification.requestPermission(), first,
                            since an iPhone asks only inside a tap (anything but granted throws "denied");
                            navigator.serviceWorker.register('/alerts-worker.js', { scope: '/' }) and the wait until
                            it is ready; the masterpod's public key for the phones, 65 bytes from base64url; the
                            registration's subscription, which is taken back and made anew when it was made with
                            another server key, and made when there is none (userVisibleOnly, with that key); it
                            answers { endpoint, p256dh, auth, label }, the delivery address, the browser's public
                            key and its secret as the browser hands them over (base64url), and label(); nothing in
                            the wallet ever calls unsubscribe() for a phone that is taken off: the masterpod stops
                            sending when the month is over, and until then the phone gets every alert; the one
                            unsubscribe() in turnOn is for a subscription that was made with another server key,
                            which no message of ours can reach; the worker is switched on in a browser only by
                            turnOn, when a person turns the phone's alerts on, and the delivery address is the
                            browser's own: it gets it from its maker's delivery service
    alerts-worker.js        not a service: the file public/alerts-worker.js, the wallet's notification worker
                            (2026-11-21, section 11), a plain file of public/ and no part of the Angular build, so
                            it keeps its name through every build, and the browser asks the wallet's servers for it
                            again by itself; the browser starts it when the masterpod sends this phone a security
                            alert, also while the wallet is closed; it does two things: it shows the alert as a
                            notification, titled "Security alert", with the wallet's logo (/icon-192.png), and when
                            the notification is tapped it brings the open wallet to the front, or opens the wallet
                            at "/"; it has no fetch handler and keeps no copy of the wallet, so every page load
                            still comes from the wallet's servers; the masterpod sends facts, not sentences ({ kind,
                            ... }, masterpod 25.7), and the sentence is made here: the file's sentences are its own,
                            in two languages, and not the dictionary's (8.8), Thai when the browser's language is
                            Thai and English otherwise; an amount is written from its millionths with commas
                            ("5,000", "1.5"), and a day in the phone's own time ("Dec 21, 2026"); a message it
                            cannot read (a kind it does not know, an empty message, one that is not JSON) still
                            shows a notification, "Open the wallet to see your security alerts.", because a browser
                            takes the permission away from a site whose message shows nothing; a new version of the
                            file takes over at once (skipWaiting, clients.claim), since it holds nothing an open
                            page depends on
    update.service          the update check and the refresh (2026-11-22, section 11; 8.1): available, a signal,
                            true once the wallet's server named another script file than the one this page runs,
                            until the page is loaded again; refreshing, a signal, true from the start of a refresh
                            until the page is gone, or until the server did not answer; refresh(before?), which
                            asks the server for the page, waits REFRESH_WAIT_MS (5 seconds) at most, runs `before`
                            when one is given and then loads the page again (location.reload()), and with no
                            answer does nothing but turn refreshing false again; the check looks at three moments:
                            when the wallet starts, every UPDATE_CHECK_MS (5 minutes) while the page is on the
                            screen, and each time the page comes back to the front; it never looks while the page
                            is hidden, and no more once a newer build was seen; in a development build, whose
                            script has no content name, the check is off; both constants are in constants.ts
    joy.service             Joy, the wallet's AI (2026-11-24, section 11; 4.18): the one chat with her and the
                            member's memory file, kept here and not in a page, so that an answer goes on while
                            another page is on the screen. Signals: messages (the chat, oldest first: a
                            JoyChatMessage is { role, text, at, end? }), answer (the answer that is being written,
                            as far as it has come; null while none is), writing (true from a send until its
                            answer has ended or failed), draft (what the message box holds), error (the page's
                            red line), memory (the opened memory file; null until it was read in this login) and
                            ready (true once the browser's database was looked into for the pod). open(), which
                            both Joy pages call when they open: the first time in a login it reads the pod's
                            entry of the browser's database and opens it under the encryption key; every time it
                            reads the memory file (loadMemory), unless an answer is under way. send(): the
                            draft's text becomes the member's message; nothing is sent without the encryption
                            key, before the memory file is known, for a text over JOY_MAX_CONVERSATION_BYTES or
                            with a memory file over JOY_MEMORY_MAX_BYTES; then masterpod-api.service's askJoy
                            with the conversation cut to the limits (conversationOf, a function beside the
                            class) and the memory file; each { text } line is added to answer; at the last line
                            the answer becomes a message, a changed memory file is taken and stored
                            (/set-joy-memory, the text wrapped as { v: 1, text }), and writing ends; what happens
                            to a refused message and to a failed answer is in 4.18. newChat() empties the chat.
                            loadMemory() reads /get-joy-memory, quiet, and opens the blob; an answer that comes
                            after the file was set from this page is dropped. saveMemory(text), for the memory
                            page: the text stored as the file, refused while an answer is under way and for a
                            text over the limit; it answers null or the reason. After every change of messages
                            the chat goes into the browser's database, encrypted, one write after the other
                            (keep); the five functions that read and write that database (openDb, inStore,
                            readKept, writeKept, dropKept) stand beside the class, and a browser that refuses
                            leaves the chat in the page's memory. A login's end, and another pod in the tab,
                            empty everything here (an effect on session.anopodId), and an answer that began under
                            the login before is dropped. utf8Length(text), exported, counts a text as the
                            masterpod does. The four constants are in constants.ts: JOY_MAX_MESSAGES (200),
                            JOY_MAX_CONVERSATION_BYTES (120,000), JOY_MEMORY_MAX_BYTES (10,240) and
                            JOY_SILENCE_MS (60 seconds).
                            Web search (2026-11-24, section 11; 4.20): one signal more, searching (true while Joy
                            searches the web for the answer that is being written: a line { searching: true }
                            sets it; the next { text } line, the answer's end and a login's end clear it). A
                            JoyChatMessage can carry sources (a list of JoySource, one to ten, only on an answer
                            of Joy's for which she cited web pages): send() takes them from the last line's
                            `sources` through sourcesOf(value), exported, and the reading of a kept chat puts
                            every message's sources through it again and drops them from a member's own
                            message. sourcesOf answers an empty list for a value that is no list, and takes of
                            a list each entry whose title is a text and whose address is a text that begins
                            with https:// or http:// and that the browser reads as an address: each address
                            once, the first MAX_SOURCES (10), a title without the spaces around it and cut at
                            SOURCE_TITLE_MAX_CHARS (200); both constants stand beside it in joy.service.ts.
                            siteOf(url), exported: the address's host without a leading "www.", empty for a
                            text that is no such address; the Joy page shows it beside a title. What is sent
                            to /ask-joy is as before: conversationOf takes each message's role and text
                            Pictures (2026-11-25, section 11; 4.21): three signals more, drawing (true while a
                            picture is made for the answer that is being written: a line { drawing: true } sets
                            it; the picture's line, the next { text } line, the answer's end and a login's end
                            clear it), answerPicture (the picture of the answer that is being written, once it
                            has come) and pictureUrls (for each picture that the page can draw, by its id, an
                            address of its bytes in the page's memory). A JoyChatMessage can carry picture (a
                            JoyPicture, { id, description }, only on an answer of Joy's for which a picture was
                            made). In send() a picture's line goes to takePicture, which clears drawing and
                            searching, puts the line through pictureOf(value), exported, makes the id and the
                            address, shows the picture in the answer and has its entry written (keepPicture),
                            and passes a second picture of one answer over; an answer that ended, and one that
                            failed after a picture came, keeps it. pictureOf answers null for anything but a
                            type of the wallet's three, a description of 1 to PICTURE_DESCRIPTION_MAX_CHARS
                            (1,000) characters and base64 that opens to between one byte and PICTURE_MAX_BYTES
                            (4 MB); both constants stand beside it in joy.service.ts. open() opens the pictures
                            of the kept chat (openPictures) before it shows the chat, and the reading of a kept
                            chat puts every message's picture through keptPictureOf and drops it from a member's
                            own message. download(id) hands a picture over as a file: the share sheet on an
                            iPhone or an iPad (onIphoneOrIpad, by the user agent), a plain download elsewhere,
                            the file's name from fileStamp. hasPictures() says whether the chat holds a picture
                            that can still be drawn, for the box of New chat. newChat() and a login's end give
                            the pictures' addresses back to the browser (forgetPictures). conversationOf puts
                            pictureNote(description), exported, an empty line and the answer's words in the
                            place of the text of an answer that had a picture. The database is version 2 with a
                            second place, joy-pictures: openDb makes each place that is not there, inStore takes
                            the place's name, dropKept takes the pod's chat and the pod's pictures out in one
                            transaction, pictureKey, readPicture and writePicture are the pictures' own, and
                            packPicture and unpackPicture put the type's name in front of a picture's bytes and
                            take it off again
    log.service             the activity log; since 2026-11-24 (section 11; 4.18) also postLines(path, body,
                            onLine, silenceMs), for an answer that a backend writes as a stream of lines, each
                            one JSON object (/ask-joy): it posts through the browser's own fetch, where every
                            other call goes through HttpClient, which hands an answer over only when it has
                            ended; reads the answer as it arrives and hands each whole line to `onLine`, an
                            empty line and a line that is no JSON passed over; and resolves, when the answer has
                            ended, to { ok: true, status: 200, body: { lines, whole } } (a LinesRead: how many
                            lines came, and whether the answer was read to its end). Another status than 200 is
                            a refusal, as for post(): the status and the backend's body. When nothing arrives
                            for `silenceMs` the call is given up: before the answer began that is status 0 with
                            api.noAnswer as its reason, and in the middle of an answer `whole` is false, as it is
                            when the connection breaks. The Log's entry for such a call holds the status and
                            the two numbers, and none of the lines' text

Keys are regenerated from blobs at each unlock; nothing secret touches
localStorage, sessionStorage or IndexedDB. (Since 2026-11-24, section
11 and 4.18, IndexedDB holds one thing: the chat with Joy that is under
way, as ciphertext under the anoPod encryption key. The key is never
written there, so the sentence still holds for everything that can be
read.) (Since 2026-11-25, section 11, it holds a second thing, in a
database of its own, `anopod-wallet-chat`: for each chat room the person
has opened, the room's newest messages, as ciphertext under the same
key, which is not written there either; room-copies.service, above.
What the browser keeps of a pod is then, in all: in localStorage the
five small things that are no secret; in IndexedDB the chat with Joy
and the rooms' copies, both as ciphertext; and, on a phone where the
security alerts were turned on, the notification worker and that
phone's delivery address.)
(Since 2026-11-25, section 11 and 4.21, IndexedDB holds a third thing,
in the database of Joy's chat: the pictures that Joy had made for that
chat, each as ciphertext under the same key.)

### 8.4 The camera component

One component for the selfie, the recovery photos and any photo: when
getUserMedia is available it shows the live camera (facingMode from a
facing input, user by default or environment for the back camera, which
the ID steps use; width and height ideal from a quality input: normal
1280 by 720, high 1920 by 1080), a Take photo button, the frame drawn to
a canvas and encoded as JPEG (quality 0.92 normal, 0.95 high), preview,
Retake. Below it always a file input, accept image/*, with capture set to
the same facing so a phone offers that camera, as the fallback when the
camera is refused or absent. The output is { contentType, bytes } for the
caller to encrypt or send. Since 2026-11-08 (section 11) a chosen file
whose longer side exceeds the quality's width (1280 normal, 1920 high) is
scaled so that side is the width, the aspect kept, and encoded as JPEG at
the quality's factor (0.92, 0.95), the size and quality a photo from the
live camera has, before anything else is done with it. Since 2026-11-12
(section 11) a smaller file is redrawn too, at its own size, as a JPEG at
the same factor, so every chosen file goes out as its pixels and nothing
else, with the type `image/jpeg`; a file the browser cannot read as a
picture is refused with a line under the file input, and nothing is
emitted. Since 2026-11-21 (section 11) a third quality, `publicSelfie`,
which the Create page uses for the public selfie: the camera is asked
for 1280 by 720 as for normal, and what goes out is the middle of the
picture as a square, the largest square that fits, made smaller to 320
by 320 pixels when it is larger and never made larger, as JPEG at 0.8.
That holds for the live camera's frame and for a chosen file alike. The
live camera is shown as that square, 320 pixels wide at most, and the
photo taken is shown at 160 pixels, the largest any page draws a public
selfie. The other two qualities are as they were.

### 8.5 The copy button

One small component, src/app/components/copy-button.component.ts
(`<app-copy-button>`), for every account id a person may want to share
or paste (2026-11-05, section 11): an icon button that copies the text
it is given (navigator.clipboard.writeText) and shows "copied" next to
the icon for two seconds, or "could not copy" when the browser refuses.
It sits after the account id in the Account title, in the footer of each
account card on the Wallet page (2026-11-06, section 11), after an
account id in a chat message, but not for the two traders of a
marketplace chat (2026-11-19, section 11), and in a history row's
details beside the other side's id and the transaction id (2026-11-06).
The case pages of
sections 12 and 13 keep their own copy code.

### 8.6 The avatar, and the room's round mark

One small component, src/app/components/avatar.component.ts
(`<app-avatar>`, inputs `anopodId`, `username` and `size`, 40 by default;
2026-11-05, section 11): a round selfie when the pod's profile has one,
else a round disc in the primary-container colour with the first letter
of the username. The profile comes from profile-cache.service (8.3), one
/get-anopod-profile per pod per tab (until the page is loaded again,
which a Lock does too since 2026-11-22; 8.3). In the chat list, the conversation
header, the members panel and the chat requests; since 2026-11-06 also on
the listing cards (24 px), the listing page (56 px) and the people who
connected (8.7; the pinned listing card drew one too until 2026-11-19,
section 11), and on Home beside the
greeting (56 px); since 2026-11-08 on the cards of the Vouch requests
page (72 px) and beside the proposer on the DAO proposal page (40 px);
since 2026-11-12 (section 11) in the person's chats about an attestor
case on My case and My recovery case (8.7), and beside each attestor in
the conversation's "Invite an attestor" panel (8.2, Chat; 40 px).

The room's round mark (2026-11-22, section 11; 4.15), a second small
component, src/app/components/room-picture.component.ts
(`<app-room-picture>`): the picture of a public room when it has one,
round, else a round grey disc with the icon of the room's kind, as the
chat pages drew it themselves until then. Four inputs: `chatRoomId`, the
room; `pictureAt`, when the room's picture was last set, as the room
lists give it, null or absent for a room without one; `icon`, the
disc's icon (public, group or storefront, chat.service's `icon`),
`public` by default; and `size`, the width and height in pixels, 40 by
default. With a `pictureAt` it asks room-picture-cache.service (8.3),
one /get-chat-room-picture per room and `pictureAt` per tab (until the
page is loaded again, which a Lock does too since 2026-11-22; 8.3);
without one it asks nothing. The disc stands while the picture loads, when the
read fails and when the picture cannot be shown. The picture has an
empty `alt`: the room's name stands beside it in every place. It is
drawn in the chat list (48 px), at the conversation's top (40 px) and in
its Room picture panel (72 px), and in the rows of Find public rooms and
of the hint of New public room (40 px; 8.2, Chat). A private chat with
one other person still shows that person's avatar. The row "Requests" of
the chat list, the chat requests, the notifications and the pinned
listing card are as they were.

### 8.7 The marketplace components, the case chat components and the escrow trade's status box

Five small components (2026-11-06, section 11), under
src/app/components/:

- listing-card.component.ts (`<app-listing-card [listing]>`): the card of
  Browse and Your listings, a link to the listing's page. Line 1 in bold,
  "35.50 THB per anos"; line 2, "Selling 100 anos · 3,550 THB"; line 3,
  the owner's avatar (24 px), username, country name and the short time
  of the chat list (shortWhen). Small labels when so: Yours, Closed,
  Waiting (this pod's room about it, the owner not yet in), Chat open
  (the owner in).
- listing-people.component.ts (`<app-listing-people [listing]
  (changed)>`): the owner's block of the listing page and Your listings:
  the people waiting (the invites to this pod about the listing: avatar,
  "somchai wants to chat", Accept, which calls /accept-invite and
  refreshes the rooms, and Decline), then the chats (the rooms about it:
  avatar, username, Open chat to /chat/:chatRoomId); "Nobody has
  connected yet." when both are empty. Live from session.chatRooms;
  `changed` fires after an answer so the listing page reads its listing
  again.
- picker-sheet.component.ts (`PickerSheetComponent`), opened with
  MatBottomSheet for a country or a currency, on Browse and on the
  new-listing form: a title, a search box, "Any" on top when the sheet
  allows it, the options `{ code, name }` whose code or name contains the
  typed letters; tapping one closes the sheet with the code. Without any
  option (a browser that does not know the currencies) a typed
  three-letter code can be used as it is.
- filters-sheet.component.ts (`FiltersSheetComponent`): the quantity
  range (least and most anos) and the price range (least and most,
  disabled with the hint "Pick a currency first" while Browse has no
  currency), Apply and Clear.
- pinned-listing.component.ts (`<app-pinned-listing [room]
  [accountIds] (disputeCase)>`): the pinned card of a private room about a
  listing (8.2, Chat), drawn by chat-room.page.ts under its header, above
  the thread.
  `accountIds` is the page's computed of the account ids found in the
  decrypted messages (the 64-hex pieces of `piecesOf`), each with its
  sender and position, newest first; the page changes only to draw the
  card and feed it. The card posts its own messages (the buyer's account
  id, from "Send my account" and "Send another account", which were
  "Share an account" until 2026-11-17; Escrow trade started and, since
  2026-11-10, Escrow trade released, the last two from its check)
  encrypted with the room key, and the thread's
  poll shows them: since 2026-11-19 (section 11) to the two traders as
  short grey lines with no account id, and to a guest as they are. The
  conversation page and the chat list know the three messages by their
  words, in every language of the wallet, through `tradeMessageKind` of
  src/app/trade-messages.ts: it makes its patterns from the three
  dictionary sentences (`pinned.shareMessage`, `pinned.startedMessage`
  and `pinned.releasedMessage`, 8.8) and answers `account`, `trade` or
  null for a whole text, so a change of those words needs the old words
  kept in that file. What the card reads from the chat is as it was: it
  finds the account ids in every message, the ones drawn as a grey line
  too. It exports `FoundAccountId`. Since 2026-11-10 the card
  also reads the room's messages itself for their account ids (8.2,
  Chat): the page's computed holds the ids of the newest 50 messages and
  of what arrived since, which is not the whole chat (since 2026-11-25,
  section 11: of the messages the page holds, which in a room that
  opened from its copy can be more than the newest 50, and is still not
  the whole chat). Since 2026-11-12
  (section 11, step 6) the card is drawn for the room's two traders only
  (chat.service's `isTrader`, 8.3) and goes by the other trader: `other`,
  whose username the card shows (until 2026-11-19 the avatar too), is
  `otherTrader(room)`, the
  other of the room's creator and the listing's owner, and the form's To
  list takes the account ids that trader posted, so a guest's messages
  never feed the trade form. Only when the other trader is neither a
  member nor invited any more does the list take the ids anyone else
  posted, as before. The card also finds the dispute case of its trade,
  as the escrow trade page does: on a check that shows the chat's trade
  in the stage `disputed` while no case is known, /list-my-cases, quiet,
  and of its disputes the one with the trade's transaction id whose
  status is open or inReview. The output `disputeCase` gives the page
  that case's id, for "Invite an attestor" (8.2, Chat), and null when the
  chat has no open trade, when the trade is not disputed and when no such
  case is there; it fires when the value changes. A case found stays
  until the trade is no longer disputed. Since 2026-11-17 (section 11;
  the plan is forclaude/wallet-trade-guide-plan-1.md) the card is the
  trade guide (8.2, Chat): it draws the status box (`app-escrow-strip`,
  below) from `escrowGuide` (src/app/escrow-stage.ts), for the seller of
  a held trade it opens the Release box (`releaseBox` of
  src/app/escrow-boxes.ts, with `askConfirm`, 8.9) and sends the release
  through `EscrowActionsService` (8.3), and it calls `escrowStageWords`
  no more. Since 2026-11-19 (section 11) the Start of the seller's form
  opens the Start box of the same file (`startBox`, with `askConfirm`),
  and the card holds no question of its own for it: its signal
  `confirmStart` is gone, and one field, `boxOpen`, keeps Start and the
  Release button from opening a second box.

Two more small components, for the chat on an attestor case (2026-11-12,
section 11; the plan is forclaude/wallet-case-chats-plan-1.md), under
src/app/components/ too:

- case-chat-start.component.ts (`<app-case-chat-start [caseId] [person]
  [open]>`): the attestor's button on the three attestor case pages
  (13.3), under the person's facts. `person` is the profile the case page
  has (its `anopodId` and `username`), or null, which draws nothing;
  `open` is false on a closed case. It goes by chat.service's
  `caseRoomWith` (8.3), live from session.chatRooms. No room: a stroked
  Start chat, shown while `open`, which runs `startCaseChat`. A room with
  the person invited: Open chat, a link to /chat/:chatRoomId, and the
  muted line "somchai has not accepted the chat yet." A room with the
  person a member: Open chat. A room the person is not in: the muted line
  "somchai did not accept the chat." and, while `open`, Invite again,
  which runs `inviteAgain`. Start chat and Invite again are off while one
  of them runs and without chat keys, and then "No chat keys in this tab:
  unlock again." shows. A refusal shows in red under the button: the
  masterpod's `403 not an attestor` as "This anoPod is not an attestor.",

  and username of the room's creator, who is the attestor, and Open chat.

  both are empty. Live from session.chatRooms.

- escrow-strip.component.ts (`<app-escrow-strip [guide]>`): the status
  box, drawn by the escrow trade page first under its Back link while
  the trade is open (8.2, Escrow trade) and by the pinned card of a
  marketplace chat under the listing's two lines, with and without a trade
  (8.2, Chat). `guide` is an `EscrowGuide`
  `{ tone, icon, headline, text, step }` and the box draws what it is
  given: a Material icon (hidden from screen readers), the headline at
  16 px, "Step 3 of 4" at the right of the headline's line when `step`
  is a number, and the sentence under them at 14 px when `text` is not
  empty. `tone` gives the colour: `ok` a light green (#e8f5e9) with dark
  green words (#1b5e20), `warn` a light amber (#fff8e1) with dark amber
  words (#7a5200), `plain` the theme's surface-container-high with the
  on-surface colour. The box has `role="status"` and 12 px round
  corners. It reads the dictionary itself for the step label only
  (`escrowGuide.stepOf`).

The box's content comes from src/app/escrow-stage.ts, beside
`escrowStageWords`, and the boxes of an escrow trade from
src/app/escrow-boxes.ts: `stateOfStage(stage)` turns the validator's
stage word into the box's state (the word itself for waiting, held,
releasing, cancelling and disputed, `open` for any other word) and
`escrowGuide(state, side, name, anos, words)` answers the `EscrowGuide`
of a state for a side, one case per state, with its colour, its icon,
its step and the words of the dictionary's `escrowGuide` section (8.2,
Escrow trade, gives them for an open trade; the states checking,
unread, noAccount, noTrade and released are no stage of an open trade:
the escrow trade page never gives them, and the pinned card of a
marketplace chat gives all five, 8.2, Chat), while escrow-boxes.ts
holds the five boxes as five functions, `releaseBox`, `disputeBox`,
`paidQuestionBox`, `doNotCancelBox` and `cancelBox`, each answering the
`ConfirmData` that `askConfirm` takes (8.9), so every page that opens
one of them opens the same box. A sixth function stands with them since
2026-11-19 (section 11), `startBox(words, anos, name)`: the Start box of
the pinned card (8.2, Chat), which the escrow trade page does not open.

### 8.8 The languages

The app speaks two languages, English and Thai (2026-11-06, section 11;
the plan is forclaude/wallet-languages-plan-1.md). English is the
default: the language is Thai when the browser's first preferred
language (the first entry of navigator.languages, else
navigator.language) begins with "th", else English; nothing is stored.
One button, "Switch to English", always in those English words, under
the landing card while the app is in Thai: after it the app is English
for as long as the tab lives, like the unlock itself, and a new tab
follows the browser again. Since 2026-11-22 (section 11) the choice no
longer outlives a Lock: Lock, the Update button and the box "You are
logged out" load the page again (the refresh, 8.1), and a page that is
loaded again follows the browser, as it always did after a reload by
hand. On a phone whose language is Thai the wallet is then Thai again on
its first page, and the button is tapped once more. That is a line of
the after-production list, "Switch to English: the choice is gone after
a refresh". There is no button to Thai and no language
toggle anywhere else.

The words live in a dictionary, src/app/i18n/en.ts and th.ts, no
package: one section per page or component, `common` for the sentences
several pages share, `dates` for the day words, `material` for
Material's visible word "Optional". `Words` is the English object's
shape and th.ts must match it, so a sentence missing in Thai fails the
build. A sentence with a number, a name, an amount, a date or an id in
it is a function, so each language keeps its own grammar (English its
plurals, Thai none). language.service (8.3) holds the language in a
signal; a page reads `t = this.lang.words` and writes `t().page.key`,
a sentence with a variable as `t().page.sentence(n)`. The page's `lang`
attribute follows the language, so Chrome sees a Thai page as Thai and
does not offer to translate it; nothing is blocked and nothing is
marked untranslatable. Dates and times go through the service's
dateTime ("Nov 6, 2026, 3:50:12 PM"; "6 พ.ย. 2026 15:50:12") and time
("3:50:12 PM"; "15:50:12"), or pass its tag to the browser's own
formatting: en-US, and th-TH-u-ca-gregory for Thai, so a Thai date
reads with Thai month names and the Western year, never the Buddhist
one; "Today" and "Yesterday" come from the dictionary; the date
pickers' calendar and Material's "Optional" follow the language.

The English on screen does not change: every English sentence moves
into en.ts letter for letter, and this spec's descriptions quote it.
In both languages these stay as they are: the messages of the servers
(the validators, the doormen, the masterpod), shown inside the Thai
page as they come, and the wallet's pattern checks on them; every wire
word, id, code, path, field name and key ("Send guardedAnosTransfer",
"Fund proposal transactionId"); the product names, in Latin letters
(anoPod, anos, anoSphere, masterpod, seed, super seed, PRF); the
browser tab's titles; Material's screen-reader labels ("Open calendar"
and the like); the developer-worded errors of crypto.service.ts. Every edition
speaks both languages, the staff pages of the moderator and attestor
editions too. The Thai was written by the build chat from the plan's
style and glossary, for Thai readers to correct; a correction is an
edit of th.ts.
