### Two signing servers, and the signer's creation with every sign request (2026-11-13)

Built from `forclaude/signing-server-plan-1.md` (FINAL since 2026-11-10),
its step 1, the wallet's side: its section 1, points 1.1 to 1.13, one
commit, on top of f2b565f. Why, from the user's four items of 2026-11-09
(section 2 of the phase 3 build list): two signing servers, with the
wallet trying the second when the first is down, and a signing server
that checks a transaction itself before it signs. For that check the
wallet sends the creation of the signer's account with every sign
request (the plan's decision 2). A signing server also holds many wallet
pairs and answers one of them per call, so the wallet asks for the
public keys for every new account (decision 18). The signing server's
own software is step 2 of the plan, in its own folder; the two go out
together at the phase 3 launch (decision 33). Nothing changes on the
validators, the doormen, the masterpod or the keyholders. No new
package, no new word in either language, no change to a page's
template, no test code.

- `server/config.js`: `signingServerUrls`, the list from
  `SIGNING_SERVER_URLS`, default `http://localhost:3300`, in place of
  `signingServerUrl` from `SIGNING_SERVER_URL`, which is no longer read.
  An empty list is refused at boot, beside the `DEFAULT_VALIDATOR`
  check: `SIGNING_SERVER_URLS must list at least one signing server`.
  The comment at the top names the signing servers among the list
  variables.
- `server/app.js`: `/api/config` also answers `signingServers`, the
  length of the list. The two forwards became a loop over the list, as
  the validators' loop is. For entry n, counted from 1,
  `GET /api/sign/<n>/public-keys` goes to that server's `/public-keys`
  and `POST /api/sign/<n>` to its `/sign`; a server that does not answer
  is `502 { error: "signing server <n> unavailable" }`. After the loop,
  `unknownNumber('sign', 'signing server', count)`: a number the list
  does not have is `404 { error: "unknown signing server" }`.
  `/api/sign` and `/api/sign/public-keys` are gone and fall to the
  `/api` catch-all, `404 { error: "Not Found", path }`, so a tab loaded
  before the change cannot sign until it is reloaded (decision 30).
- `server/index.js`: the boot line reads `signing servers` and prints
  the list.
- `network/wallet.env`: `SIGNING_SERVER_URLS` in place of
  `SIGNING_SERVER_URL`, with a comment that says what the list is: the
  signing servers in order, the two Google Cloud machines. The one entry
  is still signing1's address, because the two machines do not exist
  yet; the user puts their two addresses in before the wallet goes out
  (stage 4 of the how-to,
  `test_net_phase_3_production/signing-server-go-live.md`). Until then
  the comment is ahead of the value under it.
- `src/app/constants.ts`: `SIGNING_TIMEOUT_MS`, 15 000 (decision 18).
- `src/app/services/log.service.ts`: `get(path, quiet, timeoutMs)` takes
  the time limit the way `post` does.
- `src/app/services/config.service.ts`: `signingServers?: number` in
  `WalletConfig`; a proxy that does not send it has one.
- `src/app/services/anos-api.service.ts`: `noAnswer` is exported.
  Nothing else changed in that file.
- `src/app/services/signing.service.ts`, written anew (8.3 has it
  whole). The private field `sessionServer`. `ask`, private: it makes a
  call on the session's signing server and, with no answer, moves the
  session on and makes the call again, each server at most once.
  `publicKeys()`, which keeps nothing. `sign(transaction,
  signerAccountId?)`, which sends the creation payload of the signer's
  account along. `ConfigService` is injected for the count. The comment
  of the class says all this.
- `src/app/services/session.service.ts`: the `walletKeys` signal is
  gone, with its line in `close()` and the `WalletPublicKeys` import,
  which it alone used.
- The eleven calls that pass the signer's account id as the second
  argument. `pages/account.page.ts`, the two in `send()` and the one in
  `askCancelLocked()`: `this.accountId()`.
  `components/pinned-listing.component.ts`: `from`.
  `pages/escrow-trade.page.ts` and `pages/assisted-transfer.page.ts`:
  `this.accountId()`. `pages/guardian-new.page.ts`: `proposer`.
  `pages/guardian-proposal.page.ts`: `account.accountId`.
  `pages/attesting-trade-case.page.ts`,
  `pages/attesting-recovery-case.page.ts` and
  `pages/attesting-dispute-case.page.ts`: `account.accountId`. The
  twelfth call, the creation's in
  `services/account-creation.service.ts`, passes none. Each of the
  eleven opens pair one from the same account in the session's list
  just before it signs, so the account is in the list when
  `signing.sign` looks for it.
- Readings where the plan left a detail open. Calls that get no answer
  from the same signing server at the same moment move the session on
  by one place, not by one each, as the validator service does it:
  `ask` changes the session's server only while it is still the one
  that did not answer. With two servers, a second call would otherwise
  put the session back on the dead one and give up without asking the
  other. A repeated call goes to the server the session is on at that
  moment. The time limit holds for each try, so a call waits at most 15
  seconds per listed server before it fails. A refusal, a 400, is an
  answer and is shown; the other server is not asked. A 503, `kms
  unavailable`, is no answer, so the other server is asked, though both
  ask the same Google service. An id that is not in the session's list
  throws before anything is sent. `ask` takes the call as a function of
  the server's number, so `publicKeys` and `sign` share the loop.
  `signingServers` stands after `keyholders` in the answer of
  `/api/config` and in `WalletConfig`. Every try is a line of the Log,
  with the server's number in the path.
- The signing server of before, the stand-in at c614b21, reads only
  `transaction` from the body and ignores the `creation` sent along.
  So this wallet also works with the one old entry that
  `network/wallet.env` still holds, and on this machine with the old
  server on 3300.
- Put right on the user's word of 2026-11-13 ("Yes, fix them"), after
  the first report of this build listed them as left because the plan
  does not name them. Words only, no line of code. The comments that
  said `/api/sign` for the signing step say `/api/sign/<n>`: in
  `pinned-listing.component.ts`, `account.page.ts` (four),
  `assisted-transfer.page.ts`, the three attestor case pages,
  `escrow-trade.page.ts`, `guardian-new.page.ts` (two),
  `guardian-proposal.page.ts` (two), `account-creation.service.ts` and
  `crypto.service.ts` (seven, one of them the path of the public
  keys). The class comment of `log.service.ts` names `/api/sign/<n>`
  and says that a post or a get may carry a time limit. The comment
  over `noAnswer` in `anos-api.service.ts` says that the signing
  service takes the same four for no answer. The comment over
  `WalletConfig` says "the three counts". In `server/app.js` the top

  In `README.md`: the signing servers among what `/api/config` counts,

- Left as they are. The dated notes of earlier builds, in section 11

### The launch show in the closed page (2026-11-14)

Built by `forclaude/launch-show-plan-1.md` beside the repos, its three
steps in one chat on the user's word. This spec does not describe the
closed page (`deploy/nginx/closed.html`): the plan does, and the README's
point "The closed page" names the show. Changed: `closed.html`,
`deploy/nginx/wallet.conf` (the block `location /launch/` in each of the
three server blocks, and its header comment), the README's point, this
note. The photos are in no repo. Step 4, the music, came the same day;
its part is at the end of this note, and it changed the show's times.

What the build chose where the plan was silent:

- The river is three tenths of the screen's height (`30svh`). Its top
  seventh is haze over the far bank, and the water begins under that.
  The far bank has one light for every 60 pixels of width or so, between
  6 and 14. There are seven candle lights.
- The first words fade in over 1.2 seconds once the white is gone, and
  take their place as the title over one second.
- The words become the small title when the first photo is on screen.
  That is the 258th second before the hour (the 272nd before the music
  came) unless the first photo is late, and when no photo ever arrives
  the words stay large, as with `PHOTOS` at 0.
- A photo that has not come within 20 seconds is given up and not asked
  for again. At most two travel at a time, so two stuck ones would hold
  back all the others.
- A person who has just arrived, with no photo on screen yet, gets the
  photo of the moment as soon as it is there, not at the next turn.
- When the quiet begins, what is left of the fireworks is taken off the
  sky. On a slow phone the fireworks run slow, and their last stars
  would stand over the river. It happens under the white.
- The 20 seconds at the hour hold back the first look for the wallet
  only on a page that was counting down when the hour came. A page
  opened after the hour looks at once, within those 20 seconds too. So
  does a hidden page that is shown again: `check()` and the page's
  `visibilitychange` lines did not change.
- A page opened more than 20 seconds after the hour has the slow
  fireworks only. Before, every page opened after the hour began with
  12 seconds of dense ones.
- Safari gives its word to keep the screen on only at a tap: WebKit
  lists `navigator.wakeLock.request()` among the calls that need a
  user's gesture. So in the show's time the page asks at every
  `touchend` and `mousedown` as well. After a no it asks by itself
  again 30 seconds later. It asks from 360 seconds on, whether or not
  the show has photos.
- A file that is the copy of another, byte for byte, counts once: the
  59 files gave 57 photos. Their order is Finder's order of the file
  names.

Checked, steps 1 to 3, with the times the show had before the music
(the fireworks until 285, the white from 285 to 281, the words at 281,
the photos from 272):

- `node --check` on the page's script: clean. nginx is not on the Mac,
  so `wallet.conf` was read, not run: the three new blocks are equal,
  one in each wallet name's server block, and the braces balance.
  `nginx -t` on the server is its test.
- Seen through a small server in the build's scratchpad that answers as
  nginx does on a closed wallet: every address with a copy of the page
  and the status 503, `/launch/` from the folder of the 57 photos. The
  copy differs from the real file in one line, the launch hour, which
  is so many seconds after the page is opened. In the Browser pane at
  375 by 812 and at 320 by 568:
  - opened 304 seconds before the hour: photos 001 to 006 fetched two
    at a time, then one more with every turn; the fireworks from 300;
    the white from 285, the river scene under it at 283.5; the words at
    281; photo 001 at 272 and each next one at its turn;
  - opened at 150 seconds: the river at once, photo 026 as soon as it
    was there, 027 at its turn;
  - photo 045 answered with 404: 044 stayed through that turn and 046
    came at its own. Nothing on screen said so;
  - the end: photo 057 went at 2 seconds, the last words and the footer
    stood above the river at the hour. The server had answered as an
    open wallet since 13 seconds before the hour: the page asked for
    `/` 20 seconds after the hour and loaded the wallet then;
  - opened 30 seconds after the hour: the last scene, `/` asked in the
    same second, the wallet loaded at the next look 15 seconds later;
  - `PHOTOS` at 0, in a copy: the words stayed large and no photo was
    asked for;
  - less motion, in a copy: no white, no fade, the sky's canvas never
    set up, the river drawn once;
  - made to throw at 270 seconds, in a copy: the show left the page,
    the countdown and the fireworks went on, the console had no error;
  - no sideways scroll at either size. At 320 pixels the first words
    are on one line, in Kanit and in the Mac's own Thai font (271 of
    284 pixels).
- The Browser pane draws about 1.5 frames a second while the app is not

  - the sound is put back on the clock when it is more than 1.2 seconds
    behind it or 0.8 ahead, at most once in six seconds, and once when

### The escrow trade page: the status box, the red Dispute, the boxes with the username (2026-11-17)

Built from `forclaude/wallet-trade-guide-plan-1.md` (FINAL, 2026-11-17),
its step 1 of two, its sections 1 to 8, one commit, on top of b2d5717.
The plan is about people losing money or anos in a marketplace trade.
Nothing on the screens stopped a buyer from paying before the anos were
in escrow, or a seller from releasing before the money had come. The
user: "do not send the money until the coins are in escrow", "It also
needs to be ever clear to the buyer whether the coins are currently in
escrow or not in escrow." And on this page the buyer's "Cancel trade"
was the filled red button, the one a worried person presses: a buyer
who has paid and cancels loses the money, and a cancelled trade cannot
be disputed any more. The user: "the dispute button should be the red
one, maybe more bold. It looks like the button you press if shit is
wrong." Step 1 is this page and the pieces the marketplace chat's card
will share with it. Step 2, the card (the plan's sections 10 to 14), is
not built here, and `src/app/components/pinned-listing.component.ts` is
not touched. Wallet only: no route, no env variable and no npm package;
the validators, the doormen, the masterpod, the keyholders and the
proxy (`server/`) are not touched.

- `src/app/escrow-stage.ts`: `escrowStageWords` is as it was, comment
  and body. Under it, new: the types `EscrowGuideState` (eleven states:
  checking, unread, noAccount, noTrade, waiting, held, releasing,
  cancelling, disputed, released, open), `EscrowGuideTone` (`ok` green,

### More than one passkey (2026-11-18)

Built from `forclaude/add-passkey-plan-1.md` (FINAL, 2026-11-18), its
step 2 of three, its section 2, one commit, on main at 8145540, the
working tree clean. Step 1 was the masterpod (its spec's section 19,
commit cc2bd44, merged and deployed the same day); step 3 is the record
folders. Why: an anoPod had one passkey. A moderator or an attestor who
unlocks with a YubiKey had no spare, so a lost key meant the long
recovery. A person who made their anoPod with a Google passkey and uses
Apple devices could not log in in Safari with Face ID. Now a person can
add passkeys to their anoPod, and every passkey unlocks the same anoPod
and opens the same accounts. Nothing a person has already encrypted
changes: the first passkey stays the main one, and an added passkey
carries its own locked copies of the encryption key and of the key blob
key (4.8, section 7). Wallet only: no route of the proxy (`server/`), no
line of `network/wallet.env` and no npm package; the validators, the
doormen, the keyholders and the signing servers are not touched.

The plan's section 2 and the masterpod as built do not disagree
anywhere. The bodies, the answers and the refusal words this step reads
(`/challenge` for addPasskey, `/add-passkey`, `/list-passkeys` and
`/unlock`) were read in the masterpod's section 19 and in its code at
cc2bd44, and they are the plan's. The two lookups the masterpod gained
the same day outside the plan (`/create-anopod` and
`/open-recovery-case` answer 409 key already registered when the new
passkey's credential id stands in another passkey table) change nothing
here: both routes had those words before, the create page shows them as
they come, and the locked-out page reads every 409 of
`/open-recovery-case` as "already open", as it did. A real passkey never
meets those checks.

- `src/app/services/passkey.service.ts`: `Registration` gains `rawId`
  and `transports`, and `Assertion` gains `rawId`. `register()` takes
  `exclude`, an empty list by default, and hands it to the browser as
  `excludeCredentials`. `assert()` takes `only`, and with it the
  browser's `allowCredentials` is that one credential. The class comment
  names both. The five callers of before (`unlock.ts`, the create page,
  the Recover page and the two calls of the locked-out page) pass
  neither.
- `src/app/services/crypto.service.ts`: `INFO.kekKeysWrap` and
  `deriveKekKeysWrap(prfOutput)`. The copies are made and opened with
  `encrypt` and `decrypt`, as blob1 is.
- `src/app/services/masterpod-api.service.ts`: `'addPasskey'` in
  `ChallengePurpose`; `wrappedKeyBlobKey` on `UnlockAnswer`; the types
  `AddedPasskeyItem`, `PasskeyList` and `AddPasskeyBody`; `listPasskeys`
  and `addPasskey` in a new group after the wallet settings group.
- `src/app/services/session.service.ts`: the signal
  `passkeyCredentialId`, null again at `close()`.
- `src/app/unlock.ts`: `addedPasskeys: true` in the payload; the
  credential id of the passkey that signed into the session, right after
  `session.open`; the key blob key by one of two ways, the wrapped copy
  when `/unlock` answers one and `deriveKekKeys` as before when it
  answers none; the error of a copy that does not open; the function's
  comment.
- `src/app/pages/create.page.ts`: the new passkey's credential id into
  the session, right after `session.open`.
- `src/app/services/settings.service.ts`: `passkeyNames` on
  `WalletSettings`; the interface's comment and the class comment.
- `src/app/pages/account-passkeys.page.ts`, new, and its route in
  `src/app/app.routes.ts` after `account/protect`: the page of 8.2,
  Passkeys.
- `src/app/pages/account-home.page.ts`: the third row; the class
  comment.
- `src/app/pages/notifications.page.ts`: `linkOf` sends `passkeyAdded`
  to `/account/passkeys`; its comment.
- `src/app/i18n/en.ts` and `th.ts`: `notifications.labels.passkeyAdded`,
  `accountHome.passkeysTitle` and `passkeysLine`, and the new section

- Tables typed `Record<string, string>` added to the dictionaries (the
  type cannot check their keys in Thai): none. `notifications.labels`
  is such a table and gains one key, in both files.
- Readings where the plan left a detail open, the services. BUILD-DATE
  is 2026-11-18. `excludeCredentials` is always among the options, an
  empty list for the callers of before, which is the browser's own
  default. `allowCredentials` is among the options only with `only`.
  `transports` is read from the hand-built JSON, where it is
  `getTransports()` of the browser, or an empty list in a browser
  without it. In `UnlockAnswer` the new field stands after `blob1`, as
  the masterpod answers it. In `unlock.ts` the order is `session.open`,
  the credential id, the PRF output, the key blob key. The wrapped copy
  is opened whenever the field holds text; hex that does not decode
  counts as a copy that does not open. When that error is thrown the tab
  already holds the session, as after any failure that follows
  `/unlock` (a blob1 that does not open, a refused status read): the
  landing card shows the sentence, the session has no key blob key, and
  every page that signs refuses without one. No key is made from the
  added passkey's PRF output in its place: that would be the second key
  of the old page guard.
- Readings, the Passkeys page. The back link's word is `nav.account`
  ("Account"), as the protect page's is `nav.home`. The rows are
  Material list items. A Material list item has a fixed height and cuts
  each line at the row's width, and the main passkey's line is 72
  letters, so two style lines let a row grow with its lines and let a
  line wrap. The Rename button stands beside the list item, the two in
  one row, and not in the item's trailing slot, which is made for a
  short text. "In use now" is a line of its own under the row's line. A
  row being renamed is drawn as a small form in the row's place,
  because a list item has no room for a text box: the box starts with
  the stored name, empty for "Passkey"; one row at a time; the rule's
  sentence and a save that failed show under the box. Rename and the
  add share one busy state, so a save and a step do not run together.
  The two name boxes take `maxlength="40"`, which counts UTF-16 units,
  so a name made of emoji stops before 40 characters; the rule itself
  counts whole characters. The step titles are "1. ", "2. " and "3. "
  in front of the dictionary's titles, in both languages. `nameRule`
  shows from Rename's Save, and in the add when the name in the box no
  longer keeps the rule after step 1: step 3 checks before it asks for
  the tap. Step 1's handler checks too, though its button is off then.
  The success line is a line of its own in the primary colour, with the
  red line under it; both go when a step starts and at Start again,
  which is on whenever nothing runs. On a 201 whose name save failed
  both lines show: the passkey was added, and the red line says what to
  do about the name. The display name of the new passkey is the first
  and last name joined by a space and trimmed, the username when that is
  empty. A refused `/list-passkeys` has a line of its own where the list
  would be, and the list on screen stays while it is read again. On a
  201 the order is: the name's save, the steps and the name box start
  over, the list is read, then the lines show. The name's save reads the
  settings first when they were not read, so the names already stored
  stay. No progress bar: the plan's list of Material parts has none, and
  while a step runs every button is off. The exclusion of step 2 is read
  from the browser's InvalidStateError alone; a browser that answers it
  another way shows that error's own words.
- Thai, written here by the glossary and style of the languages plan's
  1.6 and the Thai settled in the notes above; no Thai reader has read

  spare security key" คีย์ความปลอดภัยสำรอง, with คีย์ความปลอดภัย as the
  protect pane has it; "password manager" reads เครื่องมือจัดการรหัสผ่าน;
  "a place" that holds a passkey reads ที่เก็บ; "tap" reads แตะ, as the

  "Start again" เริ่มใหม่อีกครั้ง; "Check and finish"
  ตรวจสอบและเสร็จสิ้น. "You can add another one" reads
  คุณเพิ่มพาสคีย์ได้อีก (you can add more passkeys), since Thai has no
  "one" to stand for the noun. The numbers the English writes as words
  stay words (สามครั้ง, หนึ่งครั้ง, สองครั้ง, สิบนาที) and its digits
  stay digits (1 ถึง 40). A passkey counts with รายการ, a security key
  and a password manager with ตัว. The name in `added` keeps its

- Known and left as it is, three things the plan does not cover. One:

  The 8.8 text stands on lines of its own at the end of its paragraph,

  `a[mat-list-item] { height: auto; min-height: 64px; padding-bottom:

  that much closer. A row with a second line is 83.5 pixels high. A
  padding of up to 6.5 pixels moves nothing in a row that fits. The row

### The passkey check and the open case check at Open my case (2026-11-18)

Built from `forclaude/recovery-passkey-check-plan-1.md` (FINAL,
2026-11-18), its step 2 of three, its section 2, one commit, on main at
500e8f6, the working tree clean. Step 1 is the masterpod (its spec's
section 20); step 3 is the record folders. Why: in the first days of
production six people opened a recovery case without having lost their
passkey. The user, 2026-11-18: "they're just confused, didn't know how
to use their passkey and thought that account recovery was something
more like forgot password". "Open my case" makes a new passkey on the
device, with the anoPod id as its hidden user id, and a place that
stores passkeys keeps one passkey per user id and site. So where the
person's own passkey sat in that same place, the new passkey took its
place. That person was then truly locked out, and no screen warned of
it. Now the wallet hands the device the ids of the passkeys the anoPod
already has, so a device that still holds one of them makes no new
passkey. A person whose case is already open is told so at the birth
record step, before any passkey is made. And two lines say to try Log
in first. Wallet only: no route of the proxy (`server/`), no line of
`network/wallet.env` and no npm package; the validators, the doormen,
the keyholders and the signing servers are not touched. Either order of
the two deploys is safe: a masterpod of before ignores the lookup id
and sends no ids, and then both checks do nothing, as before this
build.

The masterpod's step 1 was not committed when this step was built. It
stood in the masterpod's folder as uncommitted changes, on 3de0522.
Its `challenge()` in `src/auth/auth.handlers.js` was read there: the
six checks in the order of the plan's 1.1, the words of the refusals
and the `credentialIds` line are the plan's, and they are what this
step reads. The user committed it the same day, as 68b80b5 of
masterpodsoftware, and the code lines of that commit are the ones that
were read.

- `src/app/services/masterpod-api.service.ts`: `credentialIds` on
  `ChallengeAnswer`, with its comment. `challenge()` takes a third
  argument, `lookupId`, and builds the body from `purpose`, with
  `anopodId` and `lookupId` when each is given; its comment names the
  lookup id, the 409 and the ids. The callers for the five other

### The Public ledger id page: the result stays on the screen (2026-11-18)

One small fix, built on the user's word in the chat of the note above
("Fix it now", to the question what should happen with the sentence that
lands under the screen's edge after Check; the other choice was a line
on the after-production list), with no plan file, one commit, on top of
the commit of the note above. Why: the note above measured that right
after the first press of Check, with the page at its end, the sentence
that says the same or different stood under the screen's bottom edge,
and Check with it. The plan expected the whole result on the screen (its
decision 5, and in its section 2 "After a tap on Check the result shows
without scrolling"). Now, once the three lines of a result are drawn,
the page scrolls just far enough that the row of Check is on the screen
again, with the lines above it. Wallet only: one file of code, and no
word of the dictionaries changes.

- `src/app/pages/account-ledger-id.page.ts`. The row that holds Check
  has a name in the template (`#actions`), and the class reads it with
  `viewChild`. In the constructor an `afterRenderEffect` reads `result`
  and, when there is one, calls `scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' })`
  on the row: it runs after the render that draws a result, and at no
  other time. The row's style has `scroll-margin-bottom: 33px`, with a
  comment. The import line names `ElementRef`, `afterRenderEffect` and
  `viewChild`, and the class comment has three lines more. `check()` is
  as the plan has it. From this commit on the file differs from the
  plan's 1.1 by these lines; the plan file is FINAL and was not edited.
- Why 33 pixels. Under the row stand the card's padding (16), the card's
  border (1) and the page's padding (16). With that margin the page
  stops at its end and Check stands where it was pressed: its top is 73
  pixels above the screen's bottom edge before the press and after it.
  Without the margin, tried by hand in the scratch page before any file
  was changed, the scroll stops with Check's lower edge on the screen's
  edge, 33 pixels lower than where it was pressed, and the card's end
  under it stays out of sight.
- Why `afterRenderEffect`. The chat page and the locked-out page wait
  for a render with `afterNextRender` and the page's injector, called
  from the method that made the change, and the fix was first built that
  way, in `check()`. When the page was left while a check ran, that call
  was made with the dead page's injector and threw "NG0911: View has
  already been destroyed" into `check()`'s own catch. Nothing showed and
  nothing was logged, but an effect made in the constructor belongs to
  the page's life, so nothing runs after the page is left: the same
  leave then gave no error. `afterRenderEffect` is new to the wallet.
- Spec: 8.2, three sentences at the end of the page's paragraph; this
  note. The note above stands as it was written: it is the record of the
  step.
- The look, where: the way of the note above. A development build in a
  scratch folder on this Mac, served by a plain file server on 127.0.0.1
  (port 8803, the temporary entry in `/Users/codex/.claude/launch.json`
  taken out again, the file byte for byte what it was), in the Claude
  app's browser pane, with the made-up session of the note above. Not on
  a phone and not on the live wallet. 360, 375, 390 and 430 pixels wide
  and 600 high, each in English and in Thai.

case. Like it should tell them various ways to find their passkey and
ask if they've checked these other methods." Now the page at
`/recover/open` opens with five screens, "Find your passkey first": a
real Log in on the device, the other places a passkey may be, and what
a recovery is. The form of before shows after them. Wallet only: no
route of the proxy (`server/`), no line of `network/wallet.env` and no
npm package; the masterpod, the validators, the doormen, the
keyholders and the signing servers are not touched, and the new
screens ask the masterpod only what the start page's Log in asks. The
wallet, the moderator edition and the attestor edition are one
codebase, so all three get the screens.

built once, by this build (the plan's "Not tried yet"). It compiled as
written, at the first build, with no warning. One word differs from
the plan's code, in each of two files: `block: 'nearest'` where the
plan has `block: 'start'`. It was changed on the user's word, after
the look found a fault in iPhone Safari (the bullet on iPhone Safari
below).

### Who buys and who sells, and the card's messages as grey lines (2026-11-19)

Built from `forclaude/wallet-chat-and-passkey-plan-1.md` (FINAL,
2026-11-19), its step 1 of six, its section 1, one commit, on main at
fc5ef0c, the merge of pull request 32, the working tree clean. Why, in
the user's words of 2026-11-19, on the marketplace chat of the
production wallet. The card "shows a picture of the other person and
then selling 500 anos for 2 thb each. It makes it seem to me like
they're doing the opposite what they're doing." And: Share account
"throws it into the chat with a copy button. This is confusing and
could lead to someone sending people coins from their wallet not in
escrow. Same when the other side sends to escrow, it throws a chunk of
lines into the chat." Of the sentence from the reader's own side: "I
like it." Of keeping the messages posted and no longer showing them as
they are: "B sounds like the much easier way." Wallet only: no route,
no line of `network/wallet.env` and no npm package; the masterpod, the
validators, the doormen, the keyholders, the signing servers and the
proxy (`server/`) are not touched. The card posts the same three
messages with the same words, and `share()`, `tell()`, `check()` and
every rule by which the card finds the chat's trade have the code they
had: they guard against a second send.

### The passkey wherever the wallet signs with an account's key (2026-11-19)

Built from `forclaude/wallet-chat-and-passkey-plan-1.md` (FINAL,
2026-11-19), its step 2 of six, its section 2, one commit, on main at
11196f5, which is step 1 of the same plan, the working tree clean. Why,
in the user's words of 2026-11-19: "Before releasing coins out of escrow
the user is prompted to type in their username. We might want to change
this instead to using their passkey to confirm? The username thing is
confusing people. And having a biometric lock is helpful anyway on that
step." Then: "Yes, passkey on all." Then: "And while we're at it, I
think each transaction send should require a passkey use. I think that
makes it more safe." And, asked which buttons: "Yeah, let's do the
passkey on each of those as well. Basically, we'll be replacing type
user name with the passkey prompt." And of a new anos account: "I want
them to both click ok, and also put in the passkey next. That way we
prevent accidental sign ups." Wallet only: no route, no line of
`network/wallet.env` and no npm package; the masterpod, the validators,
the doormen, the keyholders, the signing servers and the proxy
(`server/`) are not touched.

What it is. Wherever the wallet signs with an account's key, the button
first asks the device for the passkey that opened the session, and goes
on only when that passkey answers. It is a lock on the button, checked
by the wallet itself. It stops a slip of the finger and a second person
holding the unlocked phone. It is not a check by the validators or the
signing servers: the keys that sign also sign every read of a balance,
every few seconds, so the key that opens them stays in the tab after
Log in, and this step cannot take it away. Code that got into the
wallet's page could go around the check. Safari's rule, read on WebKit's
own page on 2026-11-19
(webkit.org/blog/11312/meet-face-id-and-touch-id-for-the-web): "Face ID
and Touch ID for the web require user gestures to function", and the
gesture is carried through XHR and fetch for 10 seconds. So the passkey
is asked straight from the click of the button that signs, before any
other wait. (Since 2026-11-20, the note "The first key blob, and the
passkey's answer to the signing servers": for every button of the table
below but two, "Create anos account" and the moderator's Sign, the thing
is built first, the passkey answers for exactly what was built, and a
signing server has the masterpod check that answer before it signs; and
Safari's rule is out of date for every device that can use the wallet,
so the passkey no longer has to come before every other wait.)

The fourteen buttons, the table of the plan's section 2, with its
seventh row as the build ended: the plan has that button, the Yes of
the chat card's Start, asking in the card, and it got a box of its own
before the commit, on the user's word (the plan's decision 12, added
that day; the bullet "The card's Start in the pop-up box", below). So
the first seven ask in the confirmation box. Six of them did so before,
and their box gained the passkey. The other seven asked in the page or
asked nothing, and there the passkey is the first thing the click does.

| The button that brings up the passkey sheet | Where it is | What is signed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Send, or Stake, in the box | the Send form of an account's page | every transfer and every stake |
| "Yes, cancel the transfer", in the box | "Cancel transfer" under the Locked transfer row of an account's page | the cancel of a guarded or vault transfer |
| "Create anos account", in the box | "Create anos account", and Retry, on the Wallet page | a new anos account |
| "Yes, release the anos", in the box | the escrow trade page, and "I have been paid: release the anos" in the chat's card | the release |
| "Yes, dispute", in the box | the escrow trade page | the dispute |
| "Yes, cancel the trade", in the box | the escrow trade page | the buyer's cancel |
| Yes, in the box | Start, in the form of "Put the anos in escrow" in the chat's card | the escrow transfer |
| "Yes, cancel the transfer" | the assisted transfer page | the cancel of an assisted transfer |
| "Post proposal" | the New fund proposal page | a guardian's fund proposal |
| "Yes, vote for", "Yes, vote against" | the Fund proposal page | a guardian's vote |
| "Sign the attestation" | the attestor's trade case page | one attestation |
| "Sign the verdict" | the attestor's dispute case page | one verdict |
| "Sign all attestations" | the attestor's recovery case page | one attestation for each move |
| Sign | the moderator's recovery case page | the sign-off |

One click asks once, however many signatures it makes. What asks for no
passkey is in 8.9.

### Sent and Seen (2026-11-19)

Built from `forclaude/wallet-chat-and-passkey-plan-1.md` (FINAL,
2026-11-19), its step 4 of six, its section 4, one commit, on main at
9298884, the working tree clean. Why, in the user's words of 2026-11-19,
on the chat of the production wallet: "It's unclear as to whether or not
there is a read notification." Asked which of two things was meant:
"Yes, we want to know if the other person has seen the message." And of
the two words, as the planning chat had put them: "I like your
sugesstions". The masterpod's part is step 3 of the plan, built the same
day (masterpodsoftware 45fb549, its spec's section 21): it keeps how far
each member of a chat has read. This step is the wallet's part: the
words "Sent" and "Seen" under a person's own messages, and the report to
the masterpod while a chat is on the screen. One new call to the
masterpod; no line of `network/wallet.env` and no npm package; the
validators, the doormen, the keyholders, the signing servers and the
proxy (`server/`) are not touched. The tick in a bubble, "Sending", the
unread dot and `session.markSeen` are as they were. Either order of the
two deploys is safe (the plan's section 7).

- `src/app/services/masterpod-api.service.ts`, as the plan's 4.1 gives
  it: `RoomMember` gains the optional `seenPosition`, and
  `markMessagesSeen(chatRoomId, position)` stands after `sendMessage()`.
  It posts `/mark-messages-seen` and is always quiet, so it writes no
  line into the Log page.
- `src/app/pages/chat-room.page.ts`, as the plan's 4.2 gives it: the
  constant `SEEN_NAMES` (3) after `FOLLOW_PX`; the two fields `toldSeen`
  and `seenOff` after `newest`; `toldSeen = 0` in `open()`, and
  `void this.tellSeen();` as its last line; the timer, which calls
  `tellSeen()` after each poll; the same line in `send()` after its
  poll; the method `tellSeen()` after `poll()`; the computed `marks`
  after `accountIds`; in the template, after a bubble's closing tag, the
  word in a `span` of the class `mark`; the style line `.mark`; and the
  class comment.
- `src/app/i18n/en.ts` and `th.ts`: four entries in `chatRoom` after
  `sending`: `sent`, `seen`, and the functions `seenBy` and
  `seenByCount`. The English is the plan's 4.3, letter for letter.
- The four Thai lines, the build chat's, in full. No Thai reader has
  read them; "Thai read by a Thai reader" stands on the after-production
  list.
  `chatRoom.sent`: "ส่งแล้ว".
  `chatRoom.seen`: "เห็นแล้ว".
  `chatRoom.seenBy`: "เห็นแล้วโดย ${names}".
  `chatRoom.seenByCount`: "เห็นแล้ว ${count} คน".
  How they were made, from the glossary and style of
  `forclaude/wallet-languages-plan-1.md` 1.6 and from the Thai the file
  had: "Sent" is "ส่งแล้ว", as the file's own "Sent." has it
  (`assisted.sentCancel`, the three sentences of `escrow.sent`). "Seen" is
  "เห็นแล้ว", with the verb the file uses for what a person sees on a
  page (`vouching.what4`). It is not "อ่านแล้ว", read: the word says
  that the chat was open on a visible page, not that the person read
  the message (the plan's known limits). "By" a person is "โดย", as
  `chatNew.byAndMembers` has it, and a number of people is "${count}
  คน", as that entry and `myRecoveryCase.signed` count them. All three
  "Seen" lines begin with the same word. No line ends in a full stop,
  and a Latin word or a number has a space on each side.
- README: nothing, as the plan says. Spec: 4.10, new; 8.2, Chat (the
  paragraph "One conversation": the two words and the telling; the
  paragraph "Unread": one sentence); 8.3 (the line of
  `masterpod-api.service`); 8.8; and this note.
- What follows from the plan's code, written here so that it is not
  taken for a fault. Every opening of a conversation reports once, also
  when nothing is new: the page keeps what it told only for as long as
  it lives, and the masterpod changes nothing for a position at or
  below the one it holds. A person's own send is reported too. The word
  stands under a bubble: a message drawn as a grey line carries none,
  and when this pod's newest message is one, the word stands under its
  newest bubble. In a room with more than one other member the "Seen
  by" line names those who have seen the newest of this pod's messages
  that anyone has seen; the others are not named, and no "Sent" stands
  under that message. A message that is on its way moves no word. The
  words are as fresh as two polls: the reader's page reports within 3
  seconds of a message showing, and the writer's wallet reads the room
  list every 5 seconds. After a 404 the page tells nothing more for as
  long as it lives. On a phone that is until the person goes back to
  the list of chats. On a computer the list and the conversation stand
  side by side, and a click on another chat keeps the same page: only
  the route's parameter changes. So there nothing is told from any chat
  until the person opens another page of the wallet or loads it again.
  And while the three masterpod servers are updated one after the
  other, an answer of /list-chat-rooms from a server that is not
  updated yet carries no seen position: the words go away until the
  next answer that carries them, so for that time they can come and go.
- Readings where the plan left a detail open. BUILD-DATE is 2026-11-19.
  The two fields stand right after `newest`, and the style line `.mark`
  after `.tick`. The class comment's new sentences stand at its end,
  and the last of them tells the two things apart that are both called
  seen: the mark of the room on this device, for the unread dot, and
  the report to the masterpod. In 8.2 the plan puts the two words after
  "the bubble turns normal with a small tick", which is the middle of a
  sentence: they stand after that sentence, so that it is not cut in
  two. The plan's section 7 says that after a 404 a wallet "reports
  nothing more until that chat is opened again"; by the plan's code that
  holds on a phone, and 8.2 says what holds on a computer (the point
  above). The plan file is as it was. In 4.10 the route's block has the
  checks in the masterpod's order, from its spec's 21.3.
- The look, where. A development build of a scratch copy of the working
  tree, served by a plain file server on 127.0.0.1 (a temporary entry
  in `/Users/codex/.claude/launch.json`, taken out again; the file is
  byte for byte what it was), in the Claude app's browser pane. The
  sizes: 360, 375, 390 and 430 pixels wide at 600 high, in English and
  in Thai; the short screens 360x560 and 375x553; 360x640; 360x740 for
  the pictures of a chat with a card; 1024x600 once. A made-up session
  was set through the `ng` debug tools, the way of the note "Who buys

### The sound (2026-11-19)

2026-11-19), its step 5 of six, its section 5, one commit, on main at
3821a49, the working tree clean. Why, in the user's words of 2026-11-19,

marketplace sound notifications?" The planning chat offered the small

notifications. And of how it rings, as the planning chat had put it: "I

reads are as they were.

- What a browser lets a page do, as the plan has it from the makers' own
  pages, read by the planning chats on 2026-11-19; this build read none
  of them again. Which events let a page start sound: the HTML standard
  (html.spec.whatwg.org, "activation triggering input event") lists
  `keydown`, `mousedown`, `pointerdown` only when it comes from a mouse,
  `pointerup` when it does not, and `touchend`. WebKit's page for the
  iPhone (webkit.org/blog/6784/new-video-policies-for-ios, 2016) asks
  for "a handler for a touchend, click, doubleclick, or keydown event".
  Chrome's page (developer.chrome.com/blog/autoplay) says an engine made
  before the person touched the page starts suspended and has to be
  resumed afterwards, and advises to "stick to "click" for the time
  being". So the service listens for `click`, `touchend` and `keydown`,
  and not for `pointerdown`: under a finger that event comes before the
  touch counts. When a page stops running: a frozen page's "JavaScript
  timers and fetch callbacks don't run"
  (developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/page-lifecycle-api), and a
  hidden tab's timers are checked once a second, and once a minute after
  five minutes hidden
  (developer.chrome.com/blog/timer-throttling-in-chrome-88). Push
  notifications on an iPhone are for "Home Screen web apps", since iOS
  16.4 (webkit.org/blog/13878). That Safari pauses a page's sound engine
  when it leaves the screen was found in WebKit's bug tracker, in its
  engineers' words, not on a policy page.
- What follows from the plan's code, written here so that it is not
  taken for a fault. Log in is silent whatever waits: the first answer
  of a session only tells the shell what is there. A room that is new to
  the list is silent too: its invite rang when it came. This pod's own
  message is silent, also one written on another device. The chat on the
  screen is silent only while its page is visible; the same chat in a
  hidden tab rings. One answer rings once, however much is new in it,
  so the sound comes at most once in 5 seconds. A read of the room list
  that fails changes nothing: what is new rings with the next read that
  works. But something new that comes while the sound cannot play is not
  rung for later: the shell counts it as rung. That holds while the
  switch is off, before the first tap of the tab, and while the phone's
  browser has stopped the engine. The messages the pinned card posts
  into a marketplace chat (8.2, Chat) are messages, so a buyer's "Send
  my account" and a started or released trade ring on the other side. A
  chat about an attestor case rings like any other, and all three
  editions have the sound. The switch is the device's: two anoPods on
  one phone share it, and one anoPod on two phones has two.

### The proxy sends its own headers (2026-11-19)

Built from `forclaude/wallet-headers-plan-1.md` (FINAL, 2026-11-19), its
step 1 of four, its section 1, one commit, on main at f58c65c, the
working tree clean. Why, in the user's words of 2026-11-19: "Let's start
looking at low hanging fruit security upgrades. I believe are content
headers are a great starting point. Are the current headers set
correctly?" The look of that day found two things in the proxy. It
handed a backend's answer headers to the browser as they came. And it
sent every header of the person's browser out to each backend it calls.
A validator's doorman is a machine the project does not own. Whoever
runs one, or breaks into one, could answer
`https://wallet.anocloud.com/api/anos/<n>/<anything>` with a web page.
A person who opened that link saw the wallet's real address, the page's
script ran as the wallet, and the phone offered the wallet's passkey to
it. The keyholders sit behind the same doormen and the same proxy.
Honest backends answer only JSON, so nothing was wrong unless a doorman
turned bad. This step closes it, in the proxy only. There is no route,
no line of `network/wallet.env`, no npm package and no change under
`src/` or `deploy/`. The validators, the doormen, the masterpod, the
keyholders and the signing servers are not touched, and no validator
has to pull. The page's own safety headers and its content security
policy are the plan's steps 2 to 4 and are not in this build.

- `server/app.js`, as the plan's 1.1 gives it. In front of the comment
  of `unavailable`: the constants `API_HEADERS`, `KEPT_REQUEST_HEADERS`
  and `KEPT_ANSWER_HEADERS` and the function `ownAnswerHeaders`, each
  with its comment. In `forward` the `on` option gains
  `proxyRes: ownAnswerHeaders`; nothing else in `forward` changed, and
  its `headers: { connection: 'keep-alive' }` stays. In `createApp` two
  small pieces of middleware on `/api`. The first, right after
  `app.disable('x-powered-by')`, sets `API_HEADERS` on the answer. The
  second, after the route `/api/health` and in front of the validators'
  two agents, takes every header off a call but the four of
  `KEPT_REQUEST_HEADERS`. The comment at the top of the file says what
  goes out, what comes back, and that Connection is the proxy library's
  own; the comment of `forward` gains one sentence.
- What goes out (the plan's decision 3). A backend gets three of the
  browser's headers: Content-Type, Content-Length and Origin. Every
  other one stops at the proxy. Until now each backend got them all:
  the cookies, the Referer (the address of the wallet page the person
  is on, which holds account, chat room, case and listing ids), the
  browser's name and the person's languages. Each doorman's nginx
  writes the Referer and the browser's name of a call into its log;
  from the wallet it now gets neither. No backend's own code reads a
  header of a call; their middleware reads the three that are kept.
- What comes back (decisions 4, 5 and 6). The status and the body, not
  touched, and Content-Length. Every other header of the backend is
  dropped, and the proxy writes Content-Type itself: JSON when the
  backend said `application/json`, plain text for anything else. Every
  answer under `/api`, the proxy's own too, carries the three headers
  of `API_HEADERS`. A redirect comes back with its status and without
  its target. The wallet's code reads only the status and the body of
  an answer (`src/app/services/log.service.ts`), so nothing changes
  under `src/`.
- How. http-proxy sends its `proxyRes` event before it copies the
  answer's headers to the browser, so the function takes them off the
  backend's answer and the library copies what is left. On the way out
  the library copies `req.headers` onto the outgoing call, so taking
  them off `req.headers` in front of the forwards is enough. The two
  routes the proxy answers itself stand in front of that middleware.
- Connection (decision 7) is set as before. The proxy library writes it
  itself: `close` to the masterpod, a keyholder and a signing server,
  `keep-alive` to a validator. That is why it stays on the call, as
  the fourth name in `KEPT_REQUEST_HEADERS`, and the kept connections
  of 2026-11-11 do not change. One thing changes on the side of nginx.
  After a call to a validator the proxy now answers nginx `close`, as
  after every other call, where it handed on the doorman's
  `keep-alive`, and it closes that connection itself. nginx closed it
  either way.
- Accepted by the plan. Its decision 8: a backend's ETag no longer
  reaches the browser, so the two small GET answers that had one,
  `/api/sign/<n>/public-keys` and the health answers, are always sent
  in full. Its decision 9: a page under another address can no longer
  read an answer through the wallet's `/api`, because the backends'
  CORS headers are dropped with the rest. No page does: each of the
  three wallet names calls its own `/api`.
- What follows from the plan's code, written here so that it is not
  taken for a fault. What the proxy does in each case was seen in the
  run below. A body sent in pieces has no length, so the backend sees
  `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` in its place, written by Node in the
  proxy; an answer in pieces comes back in pieces the same way. The
  Date of an answer is the proxy's own. The proxy's own answers
  (`/api/config`, `/api/health`, its 404s and the 502) still carry
  the ETag that Express writes for them, now beside `no-store`. A
  type such as `application/problem+json` or `text/json` comes back
  as plain text; no backend sends one, and Angular reads the body as
  JSON whatever the type says. An HTML answer comes back as plain
  text, so the error pages that nginx and HAProxy write on the way
  do, and the masterpod's `GET /` stays plain text; the wallet reads
  only their status. A 204 comes back as a 204 with the plain text
  type and no body. Accept-Encoding stops at the proxy, so a backend
  that compresses when it is asked to is no longer asked; a backend
  that compressed unasked would arrive unreadable, because its
  Content-Encoding is dropped with the rest, and no backend does. A
  path in capitals (`/API/anos/1/...`) gets the proxy's own 404 with
  the three headers, since Express takes `/api` in any case and the
  forwards do not. A caller that asks to keep its connection, as a
  browser straight on port 4300 does, is now answered `keep-alive`
  after every forwarded call; until now a call to the masterpod, a
  keyholder or a signing server answered it `close` and closed.
- Readings where the plan left a detail open. The wording of the two
  comments, of the two points of section 2, of the two dated clauses
  in the note of 2026-11-11 and of the README is this build's. The
  empty lines around the new pieces are those of the planning chat's
  own trial file, which the built file equals but for the three
  comment places. In section 2 the whole of decision 7 stands in the
  first point, the side of nginx included, and the point on the
  connections is as it was. In the README the one clause became two
  sentences, and "A backend that does not answer" now begins a
  sentence of its own.
- Places this step leaves out of date that the plan does not name:
  three, all in older notes of this section. The build's first report
  listed them as left and put them to the user. The note "Step 4, the
  web app scaffold" (2026-10-25) says of its check "with the browser's
  Origin passed through (CORS header `http://localhost:4200` came
  back)"; the Origin still goes out, the backend's CORS header no
  longer comes back. In the note of 2026-11-11 the point "Spec" names
  "the one exception to "Headers go through as received"", and the
  point "Checked" says "After a validator call the proxy answered
  nginx `Connection: keep-alive` and left that connection open". Put
  right on the user's word of 2026-11-19 ("go ahead and update the
  comments"), after this step was committed (dffb5a2), in a commit of
  its own: each of the three has a dated clause in brackets beside it,
  beginning "Since 2026-11-19" and naming the plan's file, as the
  plan's two have. The old words stay; where a clause stands in the
  middle of a line, the words after it moved on to the next lines.
- Checked. `git status --short` showed a clean tree at f58c65c at the
  start, and this step's three files and no others at the end:
  `server/app.js`, this file and `README.md`. `node --check
  server/app.js` passes. The four code blocks of the plan's 1.1 were
  looked for in `server/app.js` by a script: each is there once, line
  for line. Then one throwaway run on loopback, on the user's Mac,
  Node v24.22.0, with express 5.3.0, http-proxy-middleware 3.0.10 and
  http-proxy 1.18.1 from `node_modules`: the real `createApp` of the
  working tree in front of five made-up backends (a masterpod, two
  validators, a keyholder, a signing server) and one address where
  nothing listens. The script is in the build chat's scratchpad and
  nothing of it is in the repo. No dev server and no `ng serve` ran,
  and no real server was called. Each call came in the way nginx sends
  it: HTTP/1.1, the Host of the wallet's name, `Connection: close`,
  and a new connection for every call. 92 checks, all as expected. The
  four the plan asks for:
  1. A made-up web page (`text/html`, two cookies and thirteen other
     headers of its own) asked for as `/api/anos/1/page` came back 200
     as `text/plain; charset=utf-8`, with no cookie and none of those
     thirteen, under the three headers of `API_HEADERS`. Its length
     and its 98 bytes were unchanged.
  2. Of a call that carried thirty headers, a validator, a keyholder,
     the masterpod and a signing server each saw five: Content-Type,
     Content-Length and Origin as the browser sent them, and Host and

     three. The cookie, the Referer, the browser's name, the languages

  3. A body of 8 MB arrived whole, once sent with its length, once in

  4. Three calls to a validator one after the other went down one

  Besides the four: a redirect came back 302 with no Location; a

  eight answers (`/api/config`, `/api/health`, `/api`, an unknown
  path, an unknown validator, keyholder and signing server, and the
  502 for the address where nothing listens) carried the three
  headers; of fourteen paths written in odd ways none reached a
  backend around the two pieces of middleware; after a call from a

### The page's plain safety headers (2026-11-19)

Built from `forclaude/wallet-headers-plan-1.md` (FINAL, 2026-11-19), its
step 2 of four, its section 2, one commit, on main at a2a6a89, on top of
step 1 (dffb5a2, the note above), which was not pushed or deployed when
this was built. The look of 2026-11-19 had found the wallet's page sent
with no safety header at all: no `X-Content-Type-Options`, no
`X-Frame-Options`, no `Referrer-Policy` and no
`Strict-Transport-Security` on any of the three wallet names, where the
validator monitor sends them all. This step adds those four. Three are
set by the proxy, on every answer it gives, and the fourth by the nginx
site of the wallet servers. There is no route, no line of
`network/wallet.env`, no npm package and no change under `src/`. The
validators, the doormen, the masterpod, the keyholders and the signing
servers are not touched, and no validator has to pull. The page's
content security policy is the plan's steps 3 and 4 and is not in this
build.

- `server/app.js`, as the plan's 2.1 gives it. The constant
  `PAGE_HEADERS` with its comment, in front of `API_HEADERS`. In
  `createApp` one piece of middleware with no path, right after
  `app.disable('x-powered-by')` and in front of step 1's `/api` lines,
  which sets the three headers on every answer. The comment at the top
  of the file gains one sentence.
- `deploy/nginx/wallet.conf`, as the plan's 2.2 gives it. The line
  `add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000" always;`
  nine times, three for each of the three wallet names: in the name's
  `server` block after its `access_log` line, and inside its
  `location = /closed.html` and inside its `location /launch/`, in
  both after the `add_header Cache-Control` line. It is the monitor's
  line, character for character
  (`monitorsoftware/deploy/nginx/monitor.conf`). The two locations
  need their own copy, because an `add_header` inside a `location`
  switches off the `add_header` lines of the `server` block for that
  location, and each of the two has one already. The block that
  answers 444 and the port 80 block get nothing. The comment at the
  top of the file gains a paragraph on it.
- The proxy's three headers (the plan's decision 10), with the
  monitor's values. `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`: the browser
  does not guess a file's type. `X-Frame-Options: DENY`: no other site
  can show the wallet inside its own page.
  `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`: the browser does not tell another
  site which wallet page the person came from. Under `/api` they stand
  beside step 1's three; `nosniff` is in both lists and is sent once.
- The https-only header (decisions 11 and 12). nginx adds
  `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000` to every answer under
  the three names, the proxy's answers and its own. A browser that has
  seen it uses https only for that name for a year. Accepted by the
  plan with it: if the certificate of a wallet name ever runs out,
  such a browser shows an error with no way to go on, where a browser
  that has not seen the header shows a warning a person can click
  through. The monitor already works that way. The proxy does not set
  this header, so nothing on a development machine is told to use
  https only.
- Not copied, and left out on purpose (decisions 13 and 19). The
  monitor's `X-Robots-Tag` is not copied: it is no safety header, and
  the monitor is a private page where the wallet is a public one. The
  closed page and the folder `/launch/`, which nginx serves itself,
  get the https-only header and none of the proxy's three. The closed
  page takes nothing from a person and shows nothing from a backend,
  and it carries its own script inside the page, so a policy for it
  would be a piece of work of its own.
- What follows from the plan's code, written here so that it is not
  taken for a fault. Each was seen in the run below. The three headers
  are on every answer the program writes, not only on the page: on a
  file's 304 and 206, on the answer to a HEAD, on the JSON 404 for a
  call outside `/api` that is no GET, on the plain text 404 of a
  folder with no build, and on an answer that Express writes itself
  (seen by making `index.html` a folder, so that sending it fails: an
  HTML 404 under Express's own policy `default-src 'none'`). The page
  gets no content security policy and no `no-store`: those two stay
  with `/api`. The page's `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0`, its ETag
  and its Last-Modified are as before. A path that is no file of the
  build still gets `index.html`, as `text/html`. Under `nosniff` a
  browser takes a script only under a script type and a style sheet
  only as `text/css`; the proxy sends the build's script as
  `text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and its style sheet as
  `text/css; charset=utf-8`. A backend cannot write the three either:
  a made-up page that sent `X-Content-Type-Options: made-up`,
  `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` and `Referrer-Policy: unsafe-url` came
  back under the proxy's values, since step 1 drops a backend's
  headers.
- Read from the rules, not seen, since no browser and no nginx ran.
  `no-referrer` holds for the wallet's own calls too: the browser
  sends no Referer to the wallet servers either, so nginx's
  `wallet-access.log` shows `-` in that place for a call that comes
  from a wallet page, where it showed the page's address. Under
  `ng serve` on port 4200 the page comes from Angular's own server,

  file, the script stops there: nginx keeps running with the file it
  had, and the three units are not restarted, so the program of
  before keeps running too. A wallet page that was open before the
  deploy keeps working.

### The first key blob, and the passkey's answer to the signing servers (2026-11-20)

Built from `forclaude/second-key-and-signing-passkey-plan-1.md` (FINAL,
2026-11-20), its step 2 of four, its section 2, one commit, on main at
f4dd6a8, the working tree clean. Step 1, the masterpod, was built and
committed the same day (masterpodsoftware bcf89c7). Steps 3, the
signing server, and 4, the records, come after this one. Why, in the
user's words of 2026-11-19: "only giving the user the first anos key
when they log in, and not their second", the second key being "really
just there so you can ensure you can leave a wallet"; and "Making so the
signing server required the user to use their passkey before the signing
server would sign the transaction." The aim: "a hacker who got a user's
unencrypted data that exists while the user is using the site only get's
the first key, and that the hacker can't use the first key alone to send
anos. The hacker would also need control of the user's actual passkey."
Wallet only: no line of `network/wallet.env` and no npm package; the
proxy (`server/`), the validators, the doormen, the keyholders and the
signing servers are not touched by this step.

What it is. An anos account has three signing pairs, and the validators
take any two. Pair one and pair two are the person's own; the third is
the wallet pair, which the signing servers hold. The wallet got both of
the person's pairs at every login, in one blob per account, and a
signing server signed for whoever showed pair one's signatures, so a
copy of what an open tab holds was enough to move the person's anos.
The plan closes that in two halves, and neither works alone. This step
is the wallet's part of both. First: at a login the wallet makes a
small blob with pair one alone for each account that has none, the
first key blob, and the masterpod stores it and from then on hands the
wallet only that one (4.11). Second: at every button that ends in a
signing server's signature, the thing is built first, the passkey
answers for exactly what was built, and the answer goes to the signing
server with the request (section 3; 8.9). The signing servers check
that answer from their own step on. Until then nothing is enforced.

The order of the deploys is the masterpod, the wallet, the signing
servers, and nothing breaks in between. This wallet works with today's
signing servers, which read only `transaction` and `creation` of a
request. It works with a masterpod of before as well: that one says
`firstKeyOnly` for no account, so the wallet opens the blob with both
pairs as before and stores nothing.

What a person sees. Nothing new on a normal day. In the Send box of an
account's page and in the Start box of a marketplace chat's card, the
box's button is grey for a moment after the box opens, usually under a
second, with a thin moving bar under the box's lines; a read that fails
says "No latest transaction on the ledger yet" in red in the box, and
the button stays grey. And one new sentence, where a page shows its
other errors: "The passkey could not be checked just now, so nothing
was sent. Try again in a moment."

- Safari. The note of 2026-11-19 and several comments said that the
  passkey has to be asked straight from the click, before any other
  wait, because Safari opens the passkey sheet only for a tap. That
  rule is of 2020 (webkit.org/blog/11312). A reply marked Apple Staff
  on Apple's developer forum (developer.apple.com/forums/thread/747036,
  March 2024) says the requirement was removed as of iOS 17.4 and macOS
  14.4, with a limit on requests that come too close together in its
  place. An iPhone needs iOS 18 for the wallet's passkeys. So no device
  that can use the wallet has the rule, and nothing in this step is
  shaped around it (the plan's decision 17, read by the planning chat
  on 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20; this build did not read the pages
  again). The read of the account's latest transaction id when the box
  opens stays for its other reason: the box's button then answers at
  once. Not looked up: how Safari's limit behaves when a person sends
  many times in a row. This step asks for the passkey as often as the
  wallet did before it.

### A note for each account of a transfer between own accounts (2026-11-20)

No plan file: found and decided in chat on 2026-11-20. The user had sent
anos from one of their accounts to another and noted the transfer twice,
in the first account's history ("Transferred to own account") and in the
second's ("Transferred from own account"). The Noted transactions page
showed one row. Why: such a transfer is one transaction with one id,
standing in both accounts' histories. The masterpod kept one note per pod
and transaction (4.6; decision 10 of forclaude/wallet-notes-plan-1.md),
and the history page looked a note up by the transaction id alone. So the
second account's row already carried the first account's note, with Edit
in the place of "Add a note", and saving there replaced the private part
of that one note, while its account and its sign stayed the first
account's. The Noted transactions page listed what it was given: one
note. Decision 3 of the same plan gives the two sides a kind each, which
needs a note on each. The masterpod's change of the same day is in its
spec, section 11.

- `services/notes.service.ts`: `byTransaction` is gone. In its place are
  a private map by transaction id and account id, and
  `noteOf(transactionId, accountId)`, the account's note on a transaction
  or null.
- `pages/transaction-history.page.ts`: `noteOf(row)` asks the service
  with the page's account. A row shows this account's note only. Without
  one it has "Add a note", which presets the kind as before: "Transferred
  to own account" on the sender's history, "Transferred from own account"
  on the receiver's.
- Nothing else changed: not the note form, the Noted transactions page,
  its CSV or the words. That page shows one row per note, as it always
  did, so such a transfer now shows as two rows, the sent one first (the
  masterpod's order).
- A note made before this day stays on the account it was made on, with
  the words saved last. A person who noted such a transfer from both
  sides edits it in the first account's history and adds the second in
  the other's.
- The order of a deploy: the masterpod first, the wallet after it. This
  wallet on a masterpod of before shows "Add a note" in the second
  account's history and reads "/add-noted-transaction: HTTP 409: already
  noted" in red on Save. The wallet of before on the new masterpod
  behaves as before.
- Comments brought in line in the same change, said to the user before
  the first edit: the class comment of `NotesService` and the comment of
  the page's `noteOf`. In this spec: 4.6 (the rule, the table, the two
  routes), 8.2 (the last sentences of the history's note paragraph), 8.3
  (the `notes.service` line), and a dated clause in the note of step 2 of
  2026-11-07 above, whose other words stay as the record of their day.
- Checked: `npx ng build`, clean with no warnings, built into a scratch
  folder. Seen here in a development build served from a scratch folder,
  at 390 pixels wide, with a made-up session of three accounts, a made-up
  ledger (one transfer between two of the accounts, one receipt from
  outside) and a stand-in masterpod in the page that keeps the new rule.
  On the sender's row "Add a note" preset "Transferred to own account"
  and saved. The receiver's history showed the same transfer with no
  note and "Add a note", preset "Transferred from own account", and
  saved. The sender's row still showed its own note. The Noted
  transactions page showed two rows: "Transferred to own account", −5
  anos, Spending account, and "Transferred from own account", +5 anos,
  Vault account. With the stand-in set to the old rule, Save on the
  second account showed the red 409 line. Not run against a real
  masterpod or validator, not with a passkey, and not seen on a phone:
  the user's run-through after the deploy.

### The listing limit in plain words, and Show more on the marketplace's first page (2026-11-20)

Step 2 of forclaude/listing-limit-plan-1.md (FINAL 2026-11-20), built
2026-11-20 on main at 26c581f, the working tree clean. Why: nothing
limited how many listings one pod opens, and the marketplace's first
page stopped at 200 listings with no way to see the rest. The user,
2026-11-20: "it hasn't happened yet, but I'm sure some one is going to
spam and make like 30 marketplace listings. We should limit how many
total can be open at 1 time." And on the page: "Is there like a scroll
more if 200 is not enough for some one? Or like a fetch more or
something." The limit itself is the masterpod's, step 1 of the plan (its
spec's section 23; here 4.12): at most 10 open listings per pod. This
step is the wallet's two halves: the refusal said in one sentence, and
Show more. No new npm package, no setting, nothing in server/. Either
order of the two deploys is safe (the plan's section 4). With the
masterpod alone deployed, a wallet of before shows the refusal as "HTTP
403: listing limit reached". This wallet on a masterpod of before never
meets the refusal, and Show more works there, because /list-listings
has always taken offset.

- `services/marketplace.service.ts`: `load(filters, offset = 0)` sends
  the offset with every read of Browse. The comment of `BROWSE_LIMIT`
  says what the number is now: the listings of one read.
- `pages/marketplace.page.ts`: under the cards, in front of the round +
  button, a red line for a refused Show more and the button Show more (a
  `mat-button` with the class `more` and the DAO page's one style line).
  Five new fields: `more`, `busy`, `moreError`, `reads` and `fetched`.
  `load()` became three methods. `filters()` gives the chips as the
  service's filters. `load()` reads the first 200 in place of the
  listings shown; Show more is away while it runs, and its answer is
  dropped when a later first read was started after it. That last part
  changes a thing of before: two quick chip changes could leave the
  older answer on the screen. `loadMore()` reads the next 200 from where
  the reads so far ended and adds the listings not shown yet, by
  `listingId`. Its answer is dropped when a chip changed meanwhile, and
  a refusal goes to `moreError`, with the button left in place.
- `pages/listing-new.page.ts`: in `create()`, right after the call of
  /create-listing, a 403 whose reason holds "listing limit reached" is
  thrown as the sentence `listingNew.limit`. The page's own `run()`
  shows it in red above Create listing, as it shows "Pick a currency and
  a country". Every other refusal shows as before. There is no counter,
  no hint ahead of time and no button under the sentence: the person
  reaches their listings by the back arrow and the Your listings row.
- The words. `en.ts`, letter for letter as the plan has them:
  `marketplace.showMore`, "Show more", after `noMatch`, and
  `listingNew.limit`, "You have reached the limit of open listings.
  Close one of your listings to create a new one.", after `pickBoth`.
  `th.ts`, in the same places: `marketplace.showMore`, "แสดงเพิ่มเติม",
  the words of the three other Show more buttons, and
  `listingNew.limit`, in full:

      คุณมีประกาศที่เปิดอยู่ครบจำนวนที่อนุญาตแล้ว ปิดประกาศของคุณหนึ่งรายการเพื่อสร้างประกาศใหม่

  The build wrote it by the style and the glossary of
  forclaude/wallet-languages-plan-1.md 1.6, from words `th.ts` already
  has. A listing is "ประกาศ". An open one is "เปิดอยู่"
  (`marketplace.mineLine`). "Reached the limit" is
  "ครบจำนวนที่อนุญาตแล้ว", the words of `wallet.accountLimit`. Closing

### The public selfie is the middle of the picture as a square of 320 pixels (2026-11-21)

No plan file: asked for and decided in chat on 2026-11-20 and 21, built
2026-11-21 on main at 67ac8b3, the working tree clean. Why: a public
selfie went out as the camera's whole picture, 1280 by 720 at JPEG 0.92,
170 to 220 KB, and every page that draws a face read that. The user,
2026-11-20: "I just noticed that the selfie pictures are all in the
hundreds of kilobytes ... they don't need to be loading in big
pictures." And on 2026-11-21: "Ok, middle square at 320 pixels sounds
good." No new npm package, no setting, nothing in server/, and no
masterpod change: the masterpod takes any true picture of at most 4096
pixels a side. What this reaches: the selfies of anoPods created after
the wallet's deploy. The selfies already stored stay as heavy as they
are. Making those small is a one-time job on the masterpod's database,
not planned when this was written.

- Why the middle, as a square. Every place that draws a public selfie
  is a square or a round box with `object-fit: cover`, and such a box
  shows the middle of the picture: the avatar, the found person on the
  new-chat page and in a chat room's invite, the attestor's list, the
  Vouching page, the dispute case and the three case pages. The strips
  beside the middle were never on a screen. A phone held upright gives a
  tall picture, and then the top and the bottom are the strips.
- Why 320, and why one picture. The largest boxes are 160 pixels (the
  case pages), 96 (the Vouching page) and 72 (Vouch requests). A phone
  draws about 3 of its own pixels for each pixel of the page, so the two
  vouching photos, which the user named as the ones that matter, need
  288 and 216. A second, smaller copy for the lists was talked through
  and left: it needs the masterpod, and it can be made later from a 320
  pixel picture.
- `src/app/images.ts`: two new functions, and `redrawImage` is
  unchanged. `squareJpeg(source, width, height, side, jpeg)`: the
  largest square that fits in `source`, taken from its middle, drawn on
  white to `side` by `side` pixels, or to the square's own size when
  that is smaller, encoded with `toBlob('image/jpeg', jpeg)`; null when
  a canvas gives no context or `toBlob` answers null. Every canvas it
  made is set to 0 by 0 in a `finally`. `redrawSquare(file, side,
  jpeg)`: a chosen file decoded with `createImageBitmap(file, {
  imageOrientation: 'from-image' })`, as `redrawImage` decodes it, then
  `squareJpeg`; null when the browser cannot decode the file.
- The halvings, found in the build. `squareJpeg` makes the square
  smaller in halvings, with one last step of less than a halving. A
  phone's own photo is 3024 by 4032, about ten times as wide as the
  square. Drawn that much smaller in one step its fine lines break up
  into speckle: a test sheet of fine rings came out 67 from a clean
  reduction (on the scale of 0 to 255) in Safari with the smoothing set
  to low and to high alike, and in Chrome from one canvas to another;
  in halvings it came out 7 in both, and its JPEG weighed 20 KB in
  Safari where the one step's weighed 68 KB. The first version of the
  function drew in one step with `imageSmoothingQuality = 'high'`, which
  was clean in Chrome and speckled in Safari.
- `components/camera.component.ts`: `CameraQuality` has a third value,
  `publicSelfie`, and its entry in `SIZES` is `{ width: 1280, height:
  720, jpeg: 0.8, square: 320 }`. The camera is asked for 1280 by 720 as
  before. `takePhoto` hands the video to `squareJpeg` when the quality
  has a `square`, and `fileChosen` calls `redrawSquare` in place of
  `redrawImage`. A new signal `square` puts the class `square` on the
  video and on the photo taken: the video is 320 pixels wide at most and
  as high as wide, so the camera shows what is kept; the photo taken is
  160 pixels. For `normal` and `high` no line that runs has changed.
- `pages/create.page.ts`: the camera's `quality` is `publicSelfie`. The
  three cameras of the account recovery pages are as they were.
- Calls made in the build. Told to the user before it, with no word
  against them: JPEG 0.8; a picture smaller than 320 is not made larger;
  the photo taken is shown as the square. Made in the build: the photo
  taken is shown at 160 pixels and not at the camera's 320, because a
  320 pixel picture drawn 320 wide is stretched three times on a phone
  and looks soft, which the stored picture does on no page; and the
  halvings above.
- Checked. `npx ng build` from the web_app folder, with the output in
