### The sentences on what a verdict does, turned the right way round (2026-11-21)

One small fix, built on the user's word in the chat that found it
("Yes, fix them"), with no plan file, one commit, on top of the commit
of the note above. Why: the user reported a dispute on the live
attestor site: "When two attestors signed success the coins should have
been released back to the seller, instead they went to the buyer." The
validators did what a success verdict means to them (anossoftware's
`docs/schemas.md`, 4.2). An escrow is the seller's transfer to the
buyer. Two approved `success` verdicts have it written, and the anos go
to the buyer. Two approved `cancel` verdicts close it, and the anos
stay with the seller. The wallet signs the choice as it was picked, and
the masterpod counts it as it was signed. Three sentences of the wallet
said the opposite, and had since the attestor edition was built
(2026-10-26, 13.7). So an attestor who means the seller to have the
anos, and goes by the sentence over the Verdict form, picks Success.
Wallet only: six strings of the two dictionaries, no code, no server
change.

- `src/app/i18n/en.ts`, `disputeCase.verdictText`, the sentence over
  the Verdict form of the attestor's dispute case page (13.3): "Success
  releases the escrow to the buyer, cancel returns it to the seller."
  It read "to the seller" and then "to the buyer". The rest of the
  string is as it was.
- `src/app/i18n/en.ts`, `myCase.decidedSuccess` and
  `myCase.decidedCancel`, the status in words of a trader's own case
  page once a dispute is decided (13.3, My case): "Decided: success,
  the escrow is released to the buyer." and "Decided: cancel, the
  escrow returns to the seller." The two sides stood the other way
  round.
- `src/app/i18n/th.ts`: the same three strings. In each the words for
  seller and buyer changed places, spelled as the dictionary's own
  `sides` has them.
- Unchanged: the two choices of the Verdict form, "Success" and
  "Cancel", and that the form starts on Success; the escrow trade page
  (8.2), whose words on a verdict were right already ("1 to release",
  "The anos are being released to the buyer."); every other word of the
  dictionaries. No place of this specification quoted the three
  sentences, so this note is its only change.
- Checked: `npx ng build` clean, no warning. The built script holds the
  three new English sentences and none of the old, and each of the
  three Thai lines names the side its English names. Not seen in a
  browser: both pages sit behind a passkey login and need a real
  dispute. The dispute of the report was not looked at.
- Not undone by this fix: a transfer that was written stays written.

### The wallet on the Home Screen (2026-11-21)

Built from `forclaude/security-alerts-plan-1.md` (FINAL, 2026-11-21),
its step 2 of five, its section 2, one commit, on main at 824a30e, the
working tree clean. That plan brings security alerts: an email and a
notification on the phone when a transfer starts to wait in a guarded,
a vault or an assisted account, when a recovery is started, and when a
person's alert list changes. Its step 1 is the masterpod's
(masterpodsoftware 93e8f43, section 25 of its spec); this step needs
nothing of it. Why this is a step of its own: on an iPhone a website
can send notifications only when it was added to the Home Screen, and
before iOS 26 a site opens from there as an app only when it carries a
manifest. Whether the wallet's passkey login works inside such an app
on iOS 18 had never been tried. So these files go out alone, and the
user tries the login on real phones before the page is built (the
plan's 6.3). Four new files in `public/` and four lines in
`src/index.html`. No line of TypeScript, no word in the dictionaries,
no npm package, nothing in `server/`, no line of `network/wallet.env`.
The masterpod, the validators, the doormen, the keyholders and the
signing servers are not touched, and no validator has to pull.

- The plan's decision 11 (the user, 2026-11-20: "1. Yes"). The wallet
  becomes an app on the Home Screen, in its smallest form: a file that
  says "I am an app", and a part that waits for a notification and
  shows it. No part keeps a copy of the wallet on the phone, so every
  load still comes from our servers. This step is the file. The part
  that waits is the plan's step 3.
- The plan's decision 12. The login from the Home Screen works on the
  user's iPhone 15 with iOS 27, tried by the user on 2026-11-20 with
  nothing built: "It runs as an app, the login went through and I
  could see my accounts". The iPhone 11 with iOS 18 and an Android
  phone are tried after this step. If the login fails on either, the
  build stops and comes back to the user.
- The plan's decision 20. The name under the icon is "anoPod", and the
  picture is the wallet's logo, from a larger picture the user brought.
- The pictures (the plan's 2.1). The user's picture is
  `forclaude/app-icon.png` beside the repos, the black triangle with
  the pale line, on white: a PNG of 1024 by 1024 pixels, sha256
  b03fc7d6ae428aaca96f60d87c7d5ef0e0d4d01ececd06bbc0e22f57274b7a72.
  `sips -g pixelWidth -g pixelHeight -g hasAlpha` answered 1024, 1024
  and `hasAlpha: yes`. The plan asks for a filled background, and the
  picture has one: the file carries a channel for see-through pixels,
  and every pixel in it is solid, the four corners and the whole edge
  white. From it, with `sips -z`: `public/icon-192.png` (192 by 192,
  9,040 bytes), `public/icon-512.png` (512 by 512, 31,936 bytes) and
  `public/apple-touch-icon.png` (180 by 180, 8,432 bytes). In each of
  the three every pixel is solid too, and no dark pixel lies outside
  the rounded square an iPhone cuts an icon to (counted against the
  curve |x|^5 + |y|^5 = 1 and against a square with a corner of 22.37
  percent of its side). `sips` carries over from the user's file its
  colour profile (Display P3), its 132 dots an inch and the title
  "Untitled Artwork" in two small text blocks; no name, no date and no
  place is in them. The picture in `forclaude` stays where it is.
  `public/logo.png` and `public/favicon.ico` are byte for byte as they
  were.
- `public/manifest.webmanifest`, new, letter for letter as the plan's
  2.2 has it (13 lines, 341 bytes; compared with the plan's own lines).
  Section 2 says what is in it.
- `src/index.html`: the four lines of the plan's 2.3, after the line
  of the favicon. The title "Wallet" stays. The build writes them into
  the built page with `/>` where the source has ` />`.
- What follows from the files, written here so that it is not taken
  for a fault. The proxy answers the four files with `Cache-Control:
  public, max-age=0` and an ETag, as every file of the build, so a
  browser asks again at each load and a changed manifest reaches it
  then. An address that is no file is answered with the page, so
  `/manifest.json` is a 200 with the page in it, not a 404. While the
  closed page shows (the file `/etc/wallet/closed`, or a proxy that
  does not answer), nginx answers the four files' addresses with that
  page and a 503, as it answers the wallet's own pages, so a wallet
  that is added to a Home Screen in that time gets no manifest and no
  picture. The two pictures of the manifest have no `purpose`, which
  makes them of the kind `any`: by the manifest's standard a phone
  shows such a picture whole and does not cut it to a shape of its
  own (not seen on an Android phone). As a `maskable` picture this
  one would lose the tips of the triangle: 8 percent of its dark
  pixels lie outside the circle that fits inside the picture, which
  is what a launcher with round icons cuts. An app on an iPhone's Home
  Screen is a browser of its own, with storage apart from Safari's. So
  the four small things the wallet keeps on a device, all in
  localStorage and none of them secret, start empty in the app: the
  chat positions seen (a chat that was read in Safari shows as unread
  once), the country and the currency picked last in the marketplace,
  the seen ids behind the numbers on Attesting and Moderation, and the
  sound's switch (a sound that was switched off in Safari plays until
  it is switched off in the app). A passkey is the phone's and not the
  browser's, so the same passkey logs in from the app. The three
  editions are three addresses, so each is an icon of its own, with
  the same name and the same picture.
- Readings where the plan left a detail open. The wording of section

  build's. The paragraph stands after the routes of section 2, under

### Security alerts (2026-11-21)

Built from `forclaude/security-alerts-plan-1.md` (FINAL, 2026-11-21),
its step 3 of five, its section 3, one commit, on main at b9ae5eb, the
working tree clean. The plan was written against 824a30e; since then
came c3b0177, the plan's own step 2 (the note above), and b9ae5eb, 18
lines of this file, so every place the plan names stood as the plan has
it. That plan brings security alerts: the masterpod tells a pod by email
and by a notification on the phone when a transfer starts to wait in a
guarded, a vault or an assisted account, when a recovery is started for
the pod and when the pod's alert list changes, so that a transfer that
is not the owner's can be cancelled in time. Step 1 is the masterpod's
(masterpodsoftware 93e8f43, section 25 of its spec), deployed 2026-11-21
with the alerts off. Step 2 put the wallet on the Home Screen, and the
login from there went through on the user's three phones (the note

### The shell is as high as the screen shows, and the Username label of the create page is whole (2026-11-22)

Two small fixes of the look, three lines in two files, with no plan
file, one commit, on top of the commit of the note above (31de4b6).
Built on the user's word ("let's build them") after two reviews in one
chat. The first read the code and walked the wallet on phones at
824a30e, on 2026-11-21. The second did the same at 31de4b6, on
2026-11-22, after the Home Screen step and the Security alerts page had
gone live, because the user asked for it: "before you make these fixes
will need to review again, to make sure it won't conflict with the new
changes and will still work on everything." Wallet only: no server
change, no new package.

Why the first fix: `100vh` is the height of a browser's view with the
browser's own bars drawn back. While its bars are out, a phone's
browser shows less: 77.5 points less in Safari on iOS 18.6 (iPhone SE),
40 on iOS 26.5 and 27.0, 80 pixels in Chrome on Android, and 110 points
in Safari on an iPhone 17 held sideways. The wallet's shell was that
much higher than what the phone showed. So the end of every long page
lay behind the browser's bar, and the whole page could be pushed up by
that much: by a finger at the end of a page, by the keyboard, or by a
scroll call of the page itself. The wallet's top bar then left the
screen. The note of 2026-11-18 on the recover walk-through met this as
its one fault and changed one word for it.

Why the second fix: the Username box is the first thing in step 2, and
the stepper's own frame for a step's content
(`mat-vertical-stepper-content`) cuts what stands above it. The box's
label, once it has moved up into the box's top line, stands 6.8 pixels
above the box (6.7 on Android), so the top of the word "Username" was
cut off. No other step begins with a box: steps 1, 3 and 4 begin with a
sentence.

- `src/app/app.css`, line 4, the shell (`:host`, the `app-root`
  element): `height: 100dvh;` where it read `height: 100vh;` since the
  app's first build. `100dvh` is the height the browser shows at that
  moment, so the shell ends at the screen's edge and the whole page has
  nowhere to go.
- `src/app/pages/create.page.ts`, line 50: the Username box of step 2
  carries `class="first"`. Line 97, new, in the page's styles:

### Chat: the Members list scrolls and can be searched, and older messages load on scrolling up (2026-11-22)

Four changes to the conversation page, in four files, with no plan
file, one commit, on top of 83d4c94. Built on the user's word ("Yes,
build it") after a talk in the same chat. The talk began with the
user's report: "When viewing the members of a chat group, you can
scroll to see them all. You can for chat, but not for members." (read
as: you cannot), "when the chat room loads up, I believe every single
chat is fetched? That's too much. It should probably be limited to the
last 50. And then scrolling up fetches more.", and "We probably also
want to add a search members function." Their answers settled it: the
list scrolls and gets a search box ("1. yes."), older messages load on
scrolling up and the button stays ("2. yes."), and the largest room has
about 100 people ("Right now about 100."), which is more than the 50
above which the list was to be drawn in pieces. Wallet only: no server
change, no new package.

What was wrong with the Members list: it was a column as long as the
room has people, with no scroll of its own, inside a conversation that
is as high as the screen and cuts what does not fit. In a room of 120
members and 5 invited, on a screen of 360 by 560, a build of the commit
before measured: the list 4,261 pixels high in a frame that ends at
546; 12 of the 125 rows on the screen; 24 pixels left for the thread;
the message box at 4,415, out of reach; and all 125 faces read at once.

What was already so for the messages: since 2026-11-05 a conversation
opens with its newest 50 messages, and "Load older messages" reads 50
more. Not every message was fetched. What was missing is the read on
scrolling up.

- Changed, `src/app/pages/chat-room.page.ts`, the Members list. Its
  panel is `.people` (it was `panel members`; the attestors' panel
  keeps those classes): at most half the conversation high
  (`max-height: 50%`), not shrinking, and its rows scroll inside it
  (`.people .members`). When the room has more than 10 people, members
  and invited together (`SEARCH_ABOVE`, `searchable`), a box "Search
  members" stands on top of the rows. It narrows the rows to the
  usernames that hold what was typed, capitals aside, members and
  invited alike (`memberSearch`, `foundPeople`); "No members found."
  when none does; a change of the box starts the list at its top. The
  list draws 50 rows (`MEMBERS_PAGE`), the members before the invited,
  and 50 more each time the reader comes within 200 pixels of its end
  (`membersShown`, `membersScrolled`); the search looks through
  everyone. So the faces (8.6) are read for the rows drawn only: 50,
  then 100, then 125 in the room above. The menu's Members calls
  `toggleMembers()`, which empties the box and starts at 50 rows.
- Changed, the same file, older messages. When the thread comes within
  300 pixels of its top (`OLDER_PX`), the page does what "Load older
  messages" does (`threadScrolled`), once per arrival there
  (`olderArmed`): a read that fails shows the error line, as the
  button's does, and is not asked for again until the reader has left
  the top and come back. Not while another action runs. The button
  stays: for a thread that does not fill its frame, and after a read
  that failed. The two scroll listeners are the browser's own, added in
  two effects, not the template's, so a scroll alone draws nothing
  again.
- Changed, the same file, how the reader's place is kept when older
  messages are drawn (`loadOlder`). The distance to the thread's END is
  read before and set again after; it was: the thread's growth added to
  its scroll. Why: Chrome, and Safari from iOS 27, keep a reader's
  place by themselves when something is put in above it, and the old
  way then added the same distance a second time. In a build of the
  commit before, with the button pressed while the thread stood 100 to
  1,200 pixels under its top, the reader's message was moved by 2,718
  to 1,618 pixels in Chrome 157 and by 2,922 to 1,822 in Safari on iOS
  27.0, down to the thread's end; at 0, 5 and 30 pixels it stayed. The
  button is on the screen only within about 50 pixels of the top, so
  this never showed. A read that starts 300 pixels under the top would
  have met it every time.
- Changed, the same file: older messages are drawn only once the thread
  is at rest (`threadAtRest`): it has not scrolled for 150 milliseconds
  (`REST_MS`), and has still not scrolled 40 milliseconds after that
  was found (`REST_CHECK_MS`). Why: in Safari on iOS 27.0, after a
  flick, the older messages were drawn while the thread still glided,
  and the glide went on from the place it had before. The reader then
  stood on the page just drawn, still near the top, the next page was
  read, and so on: six pages in two seconds, and message 100 where
  message 352 had been. On iOS 18.6 and 26.5 the same flick ended the
  glide and the place held. A finger that rests on the thread does not
  hold the drawing back.
- Changed, `src/app/constants.ts`: `MEMBERS_PAGE = 50`, after
  `MESSAGES_PAGE`. Changed, `src/app/i18n/en.ts` and `th.ts`, group
  `chatRoom`: `searchMembers` ("Search members", "ค้นหาสมาชิก") and
  `noMembersFound` ("No members found.", "ไม่พบสมาชิก"). The Thai is
  the build chat's.
- Checked: `ng build` of a scratch copy of the working files, clean.
  Built from the wallet folder with exactly this step's files the
  script is `main-D746HKNK.js`, byte for byte the copy's (2,311,588
  bytes).
- Checked by a look, on a development build of that copy behind a
  trial file server on the build's Mac: a made-up session, and made-up
  chats answered inside the page with real ciphertexts (a public room
  of 120 members and 5 invited with 400 messages, a chat of three with
  60, a chat of two with 12). No passkey, no server of ours. Five
  browsers: Chrome 157 with no window (500 by 613, and 1280 by 713);
  Safari on a simulated iPhone 16 with iOS 18.6 (393 by 659), on an
  iPhone 17 with iOS 26.5 (402 by 714) and on an iPhone SE with iOS
  27.0 (375 by 549); Chrome 149 on an Android 17 emulator (360 by 536).
  In all five: the Members list of the large room is half the
  conversation high (241 of 448 pixels on the smallest screen), shows
  50 rows, then 100, then 125 at its end, with the message box inside
  the frame; "pod01" finds 10 people, "Mai" finds mai and maiyada,
  "zzz" brings "No members found."; opened again, the box is empty. And
  with the thread's scroll set by a script 250 pixels under its top, at
  its top and at its top again: one read each time, 50 more messages,
  and the reader's first message 0 pixels from where it stood.
- Checked with a real finger (the simulator tool's touch path; on
  Android `input motionevent` and `input swipe`), on the three iPhones
  and on Android. A finger held on the thread while a read's answer was
  held back for a second and a half: the older messages were drawn
  under the finger, the message under it stayed where it was, and the
  thread went on following the finger. A flick: one page, drawn after
  the thread had stopped (on iOS 27.0 with the rest rule above), and
  the reader's message in its place, within 2 pixels on Android. The
  last change, the search box above 10 people only, came after these
  tries and left the scroll's code as it was; with it the Members list
  and the scripted scroll were walked again in all five browsers, and
  the flick on iOS 27.0 and on Android.
- Checked in Chrome 157 also: the button pressed at seven places from
  0 to 1,200 pixels under the top, 0 pixels moved at each (the same in
  Safari on iOS 27.0). A read that fails: the error line, one read,
  none while the reader stays near the top, a second after leaving and
  coming back; the button then loads and the line goes. The page left,
  and another chat opened, while a read ran: no error, and the other
  chat shows its own messages. A chat of 60 messages: 50, then 60 and
  no button. Two reads of the chat list while the Members list stood
  scrolled: the list did not move. Another chat opened with the list
  open and a search in it: the list is closed, and opened there it
  shows all its rows. Thai: both strings.
- Checked, small rooms: with 2 and with 3 people, with nothing or with

- Seen in the look and mended before the commit. With the search box
  in every room, a room of two on a screen of 360 by 560, with a block
  of 250 pixels in the card's place, had its Members rows squeezed to

  the box shows above 10 people only, and the panel does not shrink.
- Seen and left as it is. The search box is one more box in which a
  phone's keyboard may write a capital and offer other words (the

- Brought in line on the user's word ("Yes, update them"), in this

- Not checked: a real phone; an iPad, Safari on a Mac and Firefox; the

Step 2 of `~/Desktop/Z-TestNet/forclaude/public-rooms-plan-1.md` (FINAL,
2026-11-22), its section 2, built on the user's word ("Yes, build it")
on top of f599958, the working tree clean. Five source files and this
spec, one commit. Why: the user, 2026-11-22: "1. Public rooms are
searchable. 2. Upload an image for the public room. 3. Should we make
it so that public rooms have to have unique names. Somehow facebook
doesn't have a problem with this. I'm on the fence. One issue is that
like 20 people have already made a room called anoTH. So now people are
asking for public group names to be unique." The talk's answer, which
the user took: names stay free; a search, the biggest rooms first and a
picture tell rooms of one name apart, and a hint shows the rooms that
exist before another is made. The masterpod's part of the search is the
plan's step 1 (4.14; the masterpod's spec, section 26), committed there
the same day as 6ba4826. The picture is the plan's steps 3 and 4 and is
not built. This step is the wallet's alone: no server change, no new
package, nothing in server/.

### A word that is longer than its line may break (2026-11-23)

No plan file. The user asked why text runs out of its borders in
places, and which CSS rules are set wrong. Five kinds of mistake were
named from the code. This is the first of them, built on the user's
word ("Yes, the one line") on top of 0996e9c, the working tree clean.
One commit: `src/styles.css` and this note. No line of script changed.

- `src/styles.css`: the `body` rule gains `overflow-wrap: break-word`,
  with a comment over it. Until now nothing set `overflow-wrap` for the
  whole wallet, so the browser's `normal` held: a line broke only at a
  space, and a word that holds no space (a transaction id, a username,
  an address) ran on in one piece, out of its card and off the screen.
  The property is inherited, so the one rule reaches every page and
  every box, sheet and menu laid over a page. A rule that sets
  `overflow-wrap`, `word-break` or `white-space: nowrap` for its own
  element still holds there: the five `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, `code`
  and `.value` with `word-break: break-all`, a button, a tab, a row of
  one line.
- What it changes: a word that is longer than the whole line of its
  box, and nothing else. Such a word breaks at the box's edge and goes
  on in the next line. `break-word` and not `anywhere`: `anywhere` also
  counts when the parts of a row are sized, so a tight row would begin
  to break its short words in the middle.
- What it does not mend: a long word in a part of a flex row, in a grid
  column written `1fr` or in a table cell. Such a part is never
  narrower than its longest word (`min-width: auto`), so the word is
  not longer than its line, and the part itself runs out. Those places
  need `min-width: 0` on the part (`minmax(0, 1fr)` in a grid) as well.
  None of that is changed here, nor the three other kinds named to the
  user: a least width in bare pixels, big letters on the body's 20 px
  lines, and the one-line room under an input box.
- Seen here, in a development build of the wallet folder served from a
  scratch folder, in Google Chrome 158 run without a window, with a
  made-up session and no server (only `/api/config` was asked, and
  answered 404): 44 pages (the four pages before a login; 37 addresses
  of a logged-in person, the ones with an id in them under a made-up
  id; Home and Wallet once more with balances; an account right after
  a send) at 320, 360, 390, 430 and 1280 px wide, in English and in
  Thai. Every piece of text was measured with the declaration taken
  out of the page's style sheet and put back: 440 looks, 14,735 texts.
  One thing differs, on one page: the green line under the Send form,
  "accepted: <the transaction id>". Without the rule the id stands in
  one piece on the line after "accepted:" and ends 207, 167, 137 and
  97 px right of the screen's edge at 320, 360, 390 and 430 px, and
  the page can be pushed sideways by as much. With the rule the id
  breaks at the card's edge and takes two lines, nothing stands right
  of the card, and the page cannot be pushed sideways; the four texts
  under the line stand 20 px lower. At 1280 px the line fits and
  nothing differs.
- Not seen: a list filled with data, on any page but Home, Wallet and
  the account; a long username or a long name; the attestor's and the
  moderator's editions, which load the same style sheet; Safari; a
  phone; the live wallet.
- `npx ng build` from the wallet folder into a scratch folder: clean,
  no warning. The script is `main-HNH3CYZO.js`, byte for byte the one
  built at 0996e9c (`cmp`). The style sheet is `styles-HGVKDO6M.css`:
  the one of 0996e9c with the 25 characters `;overflow-wrap:break-word`
  put in (8,560 bytes for 8,535).
- Spec: this note only. README unchanged.
- For the deploy: the wallet alone, the user's two lines on wallet1 and
  then on wallet2, with no `npm ci` (no package file changed).

### A box with a least width in pixels is no wider than its row (2026-11-23)

No plan file. The second of the five kinds of mistake named to the
user (the note "A word that is longer than its line may break" above
has the first), built on the user's word ("Yes, pixel widths") on top
of 2879195, the working tree clean. One commit: ten page files and
this file. Twelve style lines; no line of script and no word of the
dictionaries changes.

- The mistake: a box was told `min-width: 260px`, `280px`, `320px` or
  `360px`, and a least width in pixels holds whatever the room is. A
  card leaves its content the screen's width less 66 px, and a step of
  a vertical stepper in a card the width less 150 px. So on a phone
  the box was wider than its row: it passed its card, was cut off by
  the step's frame, or let the page be pushed sideways.
- Ten lines get `min-width: min(Npx, 100%)` where they had
  `min-width: Npx`, the form that `.wide` of `account.page.ts` has had
  since 2026-11-19: N px at the least, or the row's whole width where
  the row is narrower. They are `.dates` (280) in
  `src/app/pages/noted-transactions.page.ts` and
  `transaction-history.page.ts`; `.wide` (360) in `attesting.page.ts`,
  `attesting-trade-case.page.ts`, `attesting-recovery-case.page.ts`,
  `attesting-dispute-case.page.ts` and `moderation-case.page.ts`;
  `.filter` (320) in `attesting.page.ts` and `moderation.page.ts`;
  `.column` (280) in `attesting-dispute-case.page.ts`. Each of these
  boxes is a part of a flex row.
- Two lines get `mat-form-field { width: 260px; max-width: 100%; }`
  where they had `mat-form-field { min-width: 260px; }`, the form that
  `recover-open.page.ts` has had since 2026-11-10: `create.page.ts`
  and `account-recovery.page.ts`. The first form is not enough there.
  Three of their boxes are no part of a flex row (Username on the
  create page, Email and Phone number on the recovery page), and such

  its step has the room and as wide as the step where not, in a flex

### A line of big letters is as high as its letters (2026-11-23)

No plan file. The third of the five kinds of mistake that gets built
(the note "A word that is longer than its line may break" above names
them), on the user's word ("Yes, line heights") on top of e074a03, the
working tree clean. One commit: five page files and this file. Five
style lines; no line of script and no word of the dictionaries
changes.

- The mistake: `src/material-theme.scss` gives `body` the font
  `var(--mat-sys-body-medium)`, which the built style sheet holds as
  `400 .875rem / 1.25rem Roboto`. The line height in it is a length,
  so every element inherits 20 px, whatever the size of its letters. A
  rule that makes the letters bigger than that and sets no line height
  of its own gets lines 20 px apart for letters whose own box is
  higher. On one line nothing shows. On two lines the second line is
  written into the first.
- Five rules gain `line-height: 1.3`: `.headline` (2rem, 32 px) in
  `src/app/pages/vouching.page.ts`; `.large` (1.6rem, 25.6 px) in
  `dao-proposal.page.ts` and in `guardian-proposal.page.ts`; `.price`
  (1.6rem) in `listing.page.ts`; `.greeting h2` (24 px) in
  `home.page.ts`. A number with no unit, so the line follows the size
  of the letters. 1.3 is what `.title` of `landing.page.ts` has; the
  two balances (`balance-card.component.ts`, `wallet.page.ts`) have
  1.2. These five hold words, in Thai too, and Thai writes marks over
  and under a letter, so they get the bigger of the two. Both values
  were looked at in pictures of the five texts, in English and in
  Thai; both keep the lines apart.
- What it changes on two lines: the lines stand 41.6, 33.3 and 31.2 px
  apart (1.3 times 32, 25.6 and 24 px) where they stood 20 px apart.
  The letters' own boxes are 38, 30 and 28 px high, so until now the
  second line lay 18, 10 and 8 px into the first. Now it does not.
- What it changes on one line: the text's box is as high as its line
  (41.6, 33.3 and 31.2 px) where it was 20 px, so what stands under it
  stands lower. Under the headline of the Get vouched page 21.6 px;
  under the vote line of a proposal in its vote (the DAO's and the
  fund's) and under a listing's price 13.3 px. On Home nothing moves:
  the greeting's row is 56 px high from the picture beside it, and one
  line stands in its middle as before. With two lines it is 43.2 px
  under the headline, 26.5 px under a vote line or a price, and on
  Home the row is 62.4 px high, the picture in it stands 3.2 px lower
  and everything under the row 6.4 px lower.

### The line under an input box takes the room it needs (2026-11-24)

No plan file. The fourth of the five kinds of mistake that gets built
(the note "A word that is longer than its line may break" above names
them), after the user moved the two kinds that were still open to a
fresh chat, on top of ae917ec, the working tree clean. One commit: two
files of `src/app` and this file. Two lines of two templates; no style
line and no word of the dictionaries changes.

- The mistake: Angular Material keeps room for one line of small text
  under an input box, 20 px (`subscriptSizing` is `fixed` unless it is
  set), and lays the small text (`<mat-hint>`) over that room with
  `position: absolute`. A text of two lines is then written over
  whatever stands under the box. With `subscriptSizing="dynamic"` the
  text stands in the flow, and the box is as high as its lines.
- The count: the wallet has 87 `mat-form-field`. 31 have
  `subscriptSizing="dynamic"` and 56 have not. Of the 56, five have a
  line under them, each a `<mat-hint>` (the wallet has no `<mat-error>`
  and no `hintLabel`); the other 51 show no small text and cannot have
  the flaw. Each of the five was looked at in a page: two are mended
  and three are left as they are.
- `src/app/pages/create.page.ts`: the Username box has
  `subscriptSizing="dynamic"`. Its line is never empty: the rule,
  "checking…", the answer to the check, or a refusal.
- `src/app/components/identity-form.component.ts`: each of the seven
  text boxes of the birth record form has `[subscriptSizing]` bound to
  `hasBar(state().texts()[field.key]) ? 'dynamic' : 'fixed'`. The red
  line under such a box ("The bar character | is not allowed") is
  there only while the box holds a bar. Angular Material has no
  setting for "one line of room at the least, more when the text needs
  it", and plain `dynamic` drops the empty room as well: in a first
  trial at 360 px each of the seven boxes was 56 px high where it is
  76, and what stands under the form stood 140 px higher. So a box
  stays `fixed` while it has no line and is `dynamic` while it has
  one. One line of small text is 20 px high, as much as the room that
  `fixed` keeps, so nothing moves until the line takes a second line.
- Left as they are, three of the five: the Name box of a new passkey
  (`account-passkeys.page.ts`, "For example: Spare security key") and
  the two boxes of New proposal (`dao-new.page.ts`, the counters,
  "100/100" and "5000/5000" at the most). Each is one line at every
  width in both languages, and with `dynamic` tried on them nothing
  moved.
- What was wrong on the create page. The Username box is as wide as
  its step and 260 px at the most: 170, 210, 225 and 240 px at 320,
  360, 375 and 390 px. Its line has 32 px less than the box.
  - The masterpod's refusal of a name it does not take, "HTTP 400:
    invalid username: 3 to 32 characters, a-z, 0-9 and _": two lines

  - "<username> is available": two lines from a name of 10 letters at

  - One line at every width, in both languages: the rule ("3 to 32

  The lines stand 16 px apart, and every line after the first stood

- What was wrong in the birth record form. On the locked-out page

- What changes. While a line is one line, and while a box of the form

### The chat list: only what is new (2026-11-24)

Step 2 of `~/Desktop/Z-TestNet/forclaude/chat-list-plan-1.md` (FINAL,

the card "Chat list, step 2: the wallet's part") on top of 605f0ca, the
working tree clean. Six files of `src/app` and this file, one commit.
Why: the user, 2026-11-23: "I believe currently, every 5 seconds, the
wallet is sending all the person's chats data to the phone. This is
insane. Usually the user's phone would check to see if there's new data
it doesn't have and grab that." The masterpod's part is the plan's step
1 (4.17; the masterpod's spec, section 29), committed there the same day
as 975c1e7. No template, no style and no word changed. No new package,
nothing in `server/` and nothing new under `deploy/`.

- Changed, `src/app/services/masterpod-api.service.ts`, as 8.3 now says:
  the types `RoomNews`, `RoomsRead`, `SeenItem` and `MessagesAnswer`;
  `seenSince` on `MessagesQuery`; `listChatRooms(quiet, since)`;
  `listMessages` answers a `MessagesAnswer`. The comments of
  `RoomsAnswer` and of `RoomMember.seenPosition`.
- Changed, `src/app/services/session.service.ts`: the field
  `chatRoomsSeq`, which `close()` sets to null, and the comment of

  `refreshRooms()` puts its answer in through `putWhole()`; new are

  asks with `seenSince` and takes the positions before its return for

  8.2 the chat list, "One conversation" and Notifications; in 8.3 the
  rows of session.service, masterpod-api.service and chat.service; one
  item of section 10; this note. `README.md` unchanged.
- Readings where the plan left a small point open, each the smallest
  way seen:
  1. Where the code is. The list and its number stay in
     session.service. Everything that changes the list is in
     chat.service, and the rules of an answer with `since` are plain
     functions beside the class. No new file.
  2. A conversation's opening read carries `seenSince` 0, so the
     positions are there with the first messages and not 3 seconds
     later. Load older messages and the pinned card's read carry none.
  3. A seen position in the list is only ever raised. The plan's work
     note named two ways for an answer of the chat list that arrives
     after a newer answer of the conversation's read: keep the higher
     position of each member, or ask once more with `seenSince` 0. The
     first is built, and it holds wherever a room's entry is put in: an
     answer with `since`, a read of the whole list, and `seen`. One
     case then differs from the masterpod. A member who left a room and
     came back between two reads of this wallet keeps the position of
     before in this wallet's list, until the page is loaded again,
     where the masterpod has 0 for the new membership. That person did
     see the message.
  4. An answer that leads to a read of the whole list is put in first,
     since what came is true, and the list's number is left as it was.
     So a read of the whole list that fails is asked for again by the
     next read.
  5. An answer with no `seq` leaves the list without a number, so the
     next read asks for the whole list. An answer with `seq` and no
     `counts` is taken the same way: the masterpod sends both or
     neither.
  6. The answer handed to the caller is the last read's. When a read
     with `since` led to a read of the whole list that was refused, the
     Chat page shows that refusal, as it showed a refused read before.
  7. The words that depend on today's date (4.17). This is not in the
     plan. The plan's rule "when nothing came, the list in memory is
     not set anew" took something away that nobody had named: until
     this step, a row's time and a conversation's day line were drawn
     again every 5 seconds only because the list was set anew. It was
     tried before it was mended (below, "Midnight"). The mend is the
     signal `today` in chat.service, set by `refreshNews()` and read by
     the chat list's `rooms` and the conversation's `thread`: ten lines
     of script in three files. The day headings of the transaction
     history and of Noted transactions and the time on a marketplace
     card use the same two functions of chat.service. They never
     followed a change of the day by themselves, and this step leaves
     them so.

  5. Which reads count for the red line: a conversation's opening and
     Load older messages put such a line up, and every read of the
     messages that succeeds takes it away. The page notes the line when
     a read puts it up and forgets the note at the person's next
     action, so a later line with the same words is not taken for it.
  6. The answer to a read that was asked for before the thread was
     begun anew is dropped. A thread is begun anew when a conversation
     opens and when a copy is dropped after a full answer; the page
     counts them (`opening`). Without this a 3-second read, or a read
     of older messages, that was on its way at a full answer put its
     rows into the newest 50.
  7. The thread is kept in the order of the positions, so a row that
     comes a second time changes nothing. See "Found in the trial",
     below.
  8. Nothing is kept for a room that is not in the chat list in
     memory, so an answer that was on its way while the person left a
     room brings no deleted copy back.
  9. A copy is handed over after a read of older messages too, so they
     stay while the page lives and count among the newest 200 of the
     browser's database.
  10. When a copy of a room waits to be written and a newer one comes,
     only the newer one is written. `stored()` waits for the writes
     that are on their way, and a copy that was handed over while it
     read is taken in its place.
  11. At a full answer the room's newest 50 are read from the room's
     `lastPosition` as it was when the conversation opened, as the
     request of before does.
  12. After rows that were read without the room's key the page hands
     no copy over until a thread is begun anew; the copy stays as it
     was before that read, with its highest position, so the same rows
     are read again at the next opening.
  13. An entry that does not open, or that holds another version or a
     part of another form, is not used and is not deleted: the next
     copy of the room takes its place.
  14. The look of `keepOnly` into the browser's database makes that
     database when it is not there, so a browser has it, empty, from a
     login's first whole chat list on.

## 12. Recovery and the moderator edition

Design settled 2026-10-26 (`~/Desktop/Z/forclaude/recovery-and-moderator.md`
records the chat). The masterpod's part of this specification is
`~/Desktop/Z/masterpodsoftware/docs/schemas.md` section 12 (the tables, the
routes, the statuses and events, the client crypto in its 12.6); this
section is the app's part. Three builds in three fresh chats, planned in
`~/Desktop/Z/forclaude/build-1-case-and-recovery-pod.md`,
`build-2-moderation.md` and `build-3-delivery-and-finish.md`. Section 10's
"Recover account: coming soon" ends with build 1.

### 12.1 One codebase, two editions

The moderator app is this app with a moderator section switched on. The
proxy reads `EDITION` (`wallet` or `moderator`, default `wallet`) and
answers it in `GET /api/config` as `edition`; `ConfigService` exposes it.
`moderatorwallet.masterpod.com` is a second proxy with `EDITION=moderator`
pointing at the same backends; the masterpod lists both origins in
`WEB_ORIGIN`. On this machine the user restarts the proxy with
`EDITION=moderator npm run server` to work as a moderator; both editions
live on 4200 through the same `proxy.conf.json`, one at a time.

What the edition changes: the navigation shows Moderation (12.3) when the
edition is moderator and a session is open; the landing card's title says
Moderator wallet (as built, 12.7: the toolbar's brand; since 2026-11-24
it reads "Moderator", section 11); and, since 2026-11-12 (section 11),
the wallet reads
the recovery cases that are open or in review every 15 seconds, for the
number on the Moderation entry (8.1; work-badge.service, 8.3). Nothing
else. A moderator's pod is an ordinary pod
(username starting with `moderator`, vouched by a super seed, setup
complete, a spending account staked 1000 anos for moderator through the
account page's Send, as today); every other page works as it does.

### 12.2 Routes and guards

    /recover                 Recover account: I'm locked out, or Continue a recovery
    /recover/open            the walk-through "Find your passkey first", then the locked-out stepper (12.3)
    /recover/case            my recovery: the case, its progress, the finish
    /moderation              the cases (moderator edition)
    /moderation/:caseId      one case: profile, events, buckets, sign-off, dismissal, banker packet

`/recover` and `/recover/open` need nothing. `/recover/case` needs a
recovery session (`RecoveryService.hasSession`), else `/recover`.
`/moderation` and `/moderation/:caseId` need a session (`sessionGuard`) and
the moderator edition; a pod that is not a moderator sees the masterpod's
`403 not a moderator` as "This anoPod is not a moderator" on the page.

### 12.3 The screens

**Recover** (`/recover`). Two cards. "I'm locked out": since 2026-11-18
(section 11) the card begins with a paragraph of its own, "Try Log in
first. Your passkey is saved on the phone or computer where you made
your anoPod. If Log in works there, you are not locked out and you do
not need this."
Then: "If your passkey is gone for good, we can get you back in.
You'll need your birth record, and an email and a phone number where
a moderator can reach you. A moderator will meet you on a video call
and check your security buckets before anything is released." (its
first sentence since 2026-11-18, section 11: until then "If you lost
the device with your passkey, we can get you back in.", which
invited a person whose phone is lost and whose passkey is still with
their Apple or Google account; the phone number in it since
2026-11-12, section 11; until then "your birth record and an
email"). Button: Start, to `/recover/open`, which since 2026-11-18
opens with the walk-through below.
"Continue
a recovery": "Already opened a case on this device? Unlock it with the
passkey you made then." Button: Continue, which runs `/challenge`
(unlockCase), the passkey assertion with the PRF salt,
`/unlock-recovery-pod`, derives `KEK_prf`, opens `hybridKeyBlob`, and goes
to `/recover/case`. The platform's picker shows the passkeys; with none
the authenticator's message shows.

**Locked out** (`/recover/open`), a walk-through and then a linear stepper

The walk-through (2026-11-18, section 11; the plan is
forclaude/recover-walkthrough-plan-1.md). The page opens with it,
and the stepper below shows only once the person has gone through
it in this visit. Nothing keeps that: a reload, a new visit or the
page's own address starts the walk-through again. Why: six people
of the first days of production opened a case without having lost
their passkey, and the check at "Open my case" (step 3) sees only
the device in the person's hand, at the last tap. It is a component
of its own (12.4): a card titled "Find your passkey first", with
"1 of 5" to "5 of 5" under the title, one screen at a time. Each
screen names one place a passkey may be. Screens 2 to 4 ask with
two buttons: the filled one ends the walk because the passkey is
found, the outlined one goes on. The answer that ends the walk puts
the screen's ending in the place of the question and its buttons,
and Back on an ending shows the question again. Back on a question
shows the screen before; on screen 1 it opens `/recover`. A new
screen or view starts at its top: the page scrolls there. No host
name is typed into a sentence: <site> below is the configuration's
`rpId`, the name a password list shows, and <address> is the page's
own host; in the wallet edition both read wallet.anocloud.com.

1 of 5, "Try your passkey here": "There is no password, so there is
nothing to reset. You made a passkey when you made your anoPod. Your
device keeps it and opens it with your face, your fingerprint or
your screen lock." and "Tap the button. Your device shows the
passkey with your username. Pick it." The button "Try Log in now"
runs the start page's Log in (`unlockWithPasskey`, 8.2), under a
progress bar and "Logging in…", with the screen's buttons off. A try
that works opens the session and goes where the start page's Log in
goes. A try that does not shows one sentence above the button, and
the row of buttons is scrolled back onto the screen. The device
used no passkey (the browser's NotAllowedError: the passkey box was
closed, the device has none for the site, or the browser does not
allow passkeys where the page is shown): "No passkey was used. If
your device showed none for <site>, your passkey may not be on this
device." The passkey opens no anoPod (`/unlock` answered 401 unknown
passkey, which the masterpod also answers for the passkey of an open
recovery case): "That passkey does not open an anoPod. It may be an
old one. If your device offers another, try it. If you already
opened a recovery case, go back and tap Continue." Both in the
ordinary text colour. Anything else, in red: "Log in did not go
through (<what was thrown>). Try again in a moment." After the first
try that did not log the person in, and not before, the outlined
button "It did not work here" stands beside "Try Log in now" and
opens screen 2. The page never shows the start page's "No passkey
for this site on this device? Create an anoPod instead."

2 of 5, "The device where you made your anoPod": "Your passkey was
saved on the phone or computer where you made your anoPod.", then
"Did you come here from a link inside another app, like the Google
app? Then this page cannot reach your passkey. Open Safari or Chrome
and go to <address> there." (bug 4 of the phase 2 list: inside the
Google app on an iPhone making a passkey fails), then the question
"Did you make your anoPod on a different phone or computer, and do
you still have it?" with "Yes, I still have it" and "No". Yes ends
the walk: "Your passkey is on that device. Open <address> there and
tap Log in. You are not locked out. If Log in does not work there,
start this check again on that device.", with the button "Back to
the start page", to `/`. No button leads on from there. No opens
screen 3.

3 of 5, "Your Apple or Google account": "A passkey made on a phone
is kept with your Apple or Google account, not only on that phone.
If your phone was lost or broken, another device signed in to the
same account still has your passkey.", then both of these, always:
"Apple: on an iPhone, iPad or Mac, open the Passwords app and look
for <site>. Every Apple device signed in to the same Apple Account
has the same list." and "Google: on an Android phone or in Chrome,
open Google Password Manager and tap Passkeys. Every device signed
in to the same Google account has the same list. On a new device
Google asks for the screen lock of your old phone." (read on Apple's
and Google's own help pages on 2026-11-18), then "Do you keep your
passwords in another app? Look there too." The buttons "I found it"
and "It is not there". Found: "On this device? Tap the button. On
another device? Open <address> there and tap Log in.", with "Try
Log in now" as on screen 1. Not there opens screen 4.

4 of 5, "A spare passkey": "Did you add a second passkey under
Account, Passkeys? It can be a spare security key, or a passkey kept
with Apple when your first one is kept with Google. Every passkey of
your anoPod logs you in." The buttons "I have one" and "I have no
spare". I have one: "Put in your security key, or take the device
that has the spare.", the sentence "On this device? ..." of screen 3
and "Try Log in now". No spare opens screen 5.

5 of 5, "What a recovery is": "A recovery is not a password reset.
This is what happens:" and a numbered list of four. "A moderator
meets you on a video call and checks that it is really you." "Then
you wait for the bankers. They are separate people who each keep one
part of your key. 6 of them have to send their part.", the number
being `shareThreshold` of `/api/config`. "Then you get back in. Your
money is moved to new accounts, and two attestors have to sign each
move." "Money in a guarded account then waits 7 days, and money in a
vault account 30 days.", the two being `guardedLockMinutes` and
`vaultLockMinutes` in words (the dictionary's `minutes()`), the lock
alone, without the offset. When the configuration has not loaded or
the proxy sent no lock numbers, the second line ends "Enough of them
have to send their part." and the fourth reads "Money in a guarded
or vault account then waits out its lock." Under the list a box to
tick, "I tried all of these. My passkey is gone.", and the button
Next, off until the box is ticked. Next shows the stepper, at its
top. Leaving the screen unticks the box.

1. Your birth record: the nine fields of `docs/public-ledger-id.md` as the
   identity page has them (the same form, moved into a component the two
   pages share, 12.4), "We turn this into the same lookup id you made at

   `lookupId` with `identityIdsOf`, drops the public ledger id, then,

   (since 2026-11-08): `SharesService.findOwner` asks every keyholder
   `/get-owner` at once (section 6), and the first `200` names the anoPod
   id; `/challenge` (openCase, that id) answers the pod's username (this
   challenge is never used: it is too short-lived to carry to step 3, and
   the masterpod sweeps it with the expired ones). Found, the answers are
   dropped and the stepper moves on. Not found, the page stays on step 1
   with the answers in the form, so one field can be fixed and Next
   pressed again: "No account was set up with this birth record. Check
   each field against your birth certificate and try again." No keyholder
   answered: "The keyholders could not be reached. Try again in a moment."
   A masterpod refusal shows as `/challenge: <reason>`. Once found, with
   the form empty, a line says the account was found and the answers
   dropped, and that filling the form in again starts over.
   Since 2026-11-18 (4.9, section 11) the `/challenge` request carries
   the lookup id too. When a case is already open for it the masterpod
   answers `409`, and the page shows, in red as every line there, "A

   No passkey is made.
2. Your account: "We found your account: alice", then "Give an email
   address and a phone number. Both are needed. A moderator will text you
   first, and will email you if a text is not possible." and two boxes,
   the second under the first: Contact email, and Phone number with the
   hint "With the country code, for example +66 81 234 5678." (the line
   and the phone box since 2026-11-12, section 11; until then the email

   characters with an `@` that is not first; a phone of 6 to 32

3. Open my case: one button. `/challenge` (openCase, the anoPod id) gives
   a fresh challenge and the username; the passkey registration with the

   session is open, both contacts are kept in `RecoveryService` (12.4)

   refusals shown: "A recovery case is already open for this account. Go
   back and tap Continue to carry on with it." (409), a
   masterpod refusal as `/challenge: <reason>` or `/open-recovery-case:

   Since 2026-11-18 (4.9, section 11): under the step's text stands a
   second paragraph, "Open a case only if Log in does not work for you.
   The new passkey made here can take the place of your own passkey, and
   your own is then gone for good." The `/challenge` request carries the

   The `credentialIds` of its answer go to the passkey registration as
   the exclude list (8.3). A device that already holds one of the
   anoPod's passkeys then makes no new one, and the page shows "This
   device already has your passkey. You are not locked out. Go back and

**My recovery** (`/recover/case`). The case id (short, with Copy), the
status in words ("Open: a moderator will contact you at <contact> and
meet you on a video call", "In review", "Approved: the bankers are
sending your keys", the Delivering line below, "Completed",
"Dismissed: <reason in words>"), the timeline from the events the person
may see (scheduled with the meeting link as a link, approved, dismissed,
recovered, completed), a Refresh button (`/get-recovery-pod`; also polled
every 15 s while the page is open). "Keep this device: you unlock this case
with the passkey you just made."

The contact in the Open line (2026-11-12, section 11; until then the
email) is the email and the phone the case has, joined by a comma and a
space, "alice@example.com, +66 81 234 5678". A case opened since both
are required has both; a case of before may have one of the two, and
the line then shows that one. When the page knows neither, which is the
moment between
Continue a recovery and the first `/get-recovery-pod` answer, it says
"the contact you gave" (until 2026-11-12 "your email").

The Delivering line counts both kinds of shares (2026-11-12, section 11;
decision 10 of `forclaude/wallet-case-chats-plan-1.md`): "Delivering:
the key the bankers keep has 2 of 4 shares. 1 of 3 account keys are
complete." The first pair is the backup code: the largest group of
`backupcode` shares of one `keyId`, and `shareThreshold` from
`/api/config`. The second pair is the account keys. Each anos account
has a break-glass key of its own, deposited as `breakglasskey` under a
`keyId` of its own when the account is made (section 6; 8.2, Wallet),
so an account key is complete when one `breakglasskey` `keyId` has at
least `shareThreshold` shares, and the number to wait for is
`anosAccounts` of the `/get-recovery-pod` answer: the anos accounts the
anoPod made up to the opening of the case, sent in every status of the
case (masterpod 12.4.3 and 18). The new accounts that Move your money
makes are newer than the case and are not in the number, so it stays
the same through the finish (the last note of 2026-11-12 in section 11;
as the masterpod first built it that day the number was every anos
account the anoPod has, and it went up in the middle of the finish).
The count of complete keys is never shown above that
number. When `anosAccounts` is 0, or is missing because the masterpod is
one of before, the line is the one of before, the backup code's count
alone: "Delivering: 2 of 4 key shares received".

The finish appears as a second stepper on the same page when the case
takes it (approved or delivering) and both are in: the backup code has
`shareThreshold` shares of one `keyId`, and at least as many account
keys are complete as `anosAccounts` says. Until 2026-11-12 the backup
code's shares alone decided, and they still do when the masterpod sends
no `anosAccounts`. Why both: the bankers send the rows they tick in
their GUI, so the two kinds of shares can arrive at different times, and
Move your money moves the accounts whose key came back and says nothing
of an account whose key did not, whose money then stays behind. Once
Combine has run in the tab the finish stays. Known and left as it is: a
break-glass key whose account was never finished counts as an account
key, so in that rare case the finish can open one key early.

The person never sees a backup code,
here or on Setup (2026-11-10, section 11): on these screens it is "the
key the bankers keep", "the rebuilt key" or "the key". The steps stand in
this order since 2026-11-10 (`forclaude/recovery-finish-order-plan-1.md`,
section 11): Combine, Get back in, Move your money, New key for the
bankers, Done. Until then the new key was third and the money fourth, and
a reload after the new key had landed shut the person out of the money
step: Get back in opens the masterpod's blob2 with the old key, which
fails once the masterpod holds the new one, so the anos stayed in the old
accounts until a new recovery case. Move your money needs nothing from
the new key.

1. Combine: opens every share with the recovery hybrid private key, groups
   by `keyId`, combines each group of three; the backup code and the
   break-glass seeds are in RAM. Shows "key rebuilt" and "n break-glass
   seeds recovered".
2. Get back in: `KEK_backup` and the backup code keys from the code;
   `blob2` from the last `/get-recovery-pod` answer (masterpod 12.4.3 hands
   it over once the case is approved) opened with `KEK_backup` gives the
   encryption key; `newBlob1` = the encryption key under `KEK_prf`;
   `/challenge` (recover); the payload `{ challenge, caseId, newBlob1 }`
   signed with the backup code keys; `/recover-with-backup-code`. Then the
   ordinary unlock (`/challenge` unlock, the assertion, `/unlock`), which
   opens the normal session in this tab with the same passkey: `blob1`,
   the chat keys, the identity blob, the status.
3. Move your money (2026-11-08, `forclaude/break-glass-plan-1.md` step 5,
   section 11; in place of the "Break-glass keys" step that stood third
   from 2026-10-26, which matched each recovered seed to its account and
   stored it there with `/store-break-glass-blob`, and left with step 4 of
   that plan; it stood fourth, after the new key, until 2026-11-10): "Your
   old accounts' keys are gone with the lost passkey. For each account
   that holds anos the wallet opens a new account of the same type and
   files a move signed by its break-glass key. Two attestors check you and
   sign; a guarded or vault account's move also waits out its lock." The
   button Move my money runs, in this order since 2026-11-10 (the read of
   a held move and the filing of each move by itself are that day's,
   section 11): (1) `/list-anos-accounts` into the session; each
   recovered seed's two break-glass public keys find the account whose
   `creation.payload.publicKeys` names them, and a seed that matches none
   is unmatched; (2) an account whose move `/list-my-break-glass-moves`
   already lists is filed and skipped; (3) the reads, every one before
   any write: every other matched account is read with
   `/get-assisted-transfer` and `/get-account` (5.4), both signed by its
   break-glass pair (the validators accept it since the user keys are
   gone, anossoftware 22). A held transfer whose `type` is
   `breakGlassTransfer` is a move to file, with the held transfer's
   `transactionId` and `accountIdTo`: an earlier run posted it and its
   filing never reached the masterpod. Else a balance of 0 is empty and
   skipped. Else the account is one to move, with its balance and its
   latest transaction id. An account the validators do not know never
   reached the ledger, so it holds nothing: when its first read is
   refused with `401` and a reason saying `unknown account` (the test
   `balances.service` uses for an account that has not landed), it is
   empty too, its second read is not made, and the next account is read.
   Every other refused read stops the step; (4) each move to file is
   filed, and no new account is made for its old account; (5) for
   each account to move, a new account of the same type through
   `account-creation.service` (8.3), waited for on the ledger, then the
   `breakGlassTransfer` of the whole balance into it, chained on the
   latest transaction id read, dated now plus the type's minutes ahead
   (guarded and vault the lock plus the offset by the proxy's numbers,
   else 0), signed by the break-glass pair alone and posted to
   `/anos-transfer`, no signing server. When the validator refuses the
   post or gives no answer, `/get-assisted-transfer` is read again with
   the break-glass pair: a `breakGlassTransfer` there is the move, with
   the validator's `transactionId` and `accountIdTo`; anything else stops
   the step with "The validator refused the move out of <account>:
   <reason>", the reason being the post's. Then the move is filed, before
   the next account is touched; (6) the seeds wiped and dropped from
   `RecoveryService`. Filing a move is `/file-break-glass-moves` with the
   case id and that one move, a call per move, made as soon as the move
   is on the validators: an ok answer or a `409 move already filed`
   counts as filed, anything else stops the step as
   `/file-break-glass-moves: <reason>`. So a step that stops half way has
   filed every move it posted, and the 20 moves one call may carry are no
   limit. A validator's "already there" by itself does not count as
   filed: an old account with a transaction of its own still waiting on
   the validators (a guarded or vault transfer in its lock, an open
   escrow trade, an assisted transfer) stops the step with the
   validator's words, and the step can be run again in the same case once
   that transaction is done. Until 2026-11-10 the moves of a run went to
   the masterpod in one call after the last account, so anything that
   stopped the step before that call lost them; on Retry the validator's
   refusal of a second move for the account then counted as filed with
   nothing filed, after another new account had been made. The result:
   "2 moves filed, 1 account was empty, 0 seeds matched no account", or
   "No break-glass seeds were recovered, so there is nothing to move."
   The step is complete when the run ended without an error, even with
   nothing to move; Retry runs it again and skips what is filed. This is
   the one place in the wallet that uses a break-glass key: no card,
   account page or Account entry offers one. The old accounts' key blobs
   do not open under the new passkey's key blob key (section 7), so the
   wallet shows them as lost, with the move's progress (8.2).
4. New key for the bankers (until 2026-11-10 "New backup code", which
   showed the new code once as on Setup and waited for "I have written it
   down, complete"; it stood third, before the money, until 2026-11-10):
   one button, "Make the new key". It makes a new code without showing
   it, with `newBlob2` and the new backup code keys, when none is held
   yet. Then, the keyholders first since 2026-11-10 (section 11): the
   page checks that the old key is still in the tab, before anything is
   deposited, since the masterpod call needs it for the proof ("The
   rebuilt key is not in this tab: combine and get back in first."); the
   deposit as `backupcode` through `SharesService.deposit`, a new
   `keyId`, made once; then `/rotate-backup-code` with `newBlob2`, the
   new keys and the proof by the old keys. When that call is refused or
   gets no answer, the page reads the case again (`/get-recovery-pod`,
   quietly, an ok answer kept as the poll keeps one): if the blob2 the
   masterpod holds is the new one, the rotation landed and the step is
   done; otherwise the refusal shows as `/rotate-backup-code: <reason>`.
   The button reads "Make the new key" at first, "Retry the deposit"
   after a failed deposit (it deposits the same new key again under a
   fresh key id) and "Retry" when only the masterpod call is left (it
   repeats that call alone). "The old key is now worthless." Until
   2026-11-10 the masterpod was told first and the deposit came second,
   and between the two the new key lived only in the tab: a tab closed
   there, or a lost answer of the masterpod (Retry then signed with the
   old key and got `401 bad signature`), left an anoPod whose shares
   rebuild the old key, which opens nothing and which the masterpod
   refuses, and the wallet could not mend it later. Setup already
   deposits first (8.2).
5. Done: `/complete-recovery-case`; "You're back in." Continue to
   `/wallet`.

Each step keeps its result in RAM and can be retried; a refresh of the
page loses the combined code and the seeds, and the person starts the
finish again from Combine after unlocking the recovery pod (Move your
money then skips the moves already filed, and files a move the
validators hold that was not filed yet, without a second new account).

**Moderation** (`/moderation`). The cases from `/list-recovery-cases`, a
status filter (the four open statuses by default, plus completed and
dismissed), each row: username, names, status, approvals, opened. A row
opens `/moderation/:caseId`. Since 2026-11-12 (section 11) a good read
hands the ids of the cases it read that are open or in review to
work-badge.service (8.3, `seeModeration`): they are what the number on
the Moderation entry counts (8.1), and this device has seen them all
then, so the number clears when the page is opened.

**Case** (`/moderation/:caseId`), from `/get-recovery-case`, refreshed by a
button and every 15 s

- The person: public selfie, username, names, the Email row with Copy
  when the case has an email, the Phone row under it with Copy when the
  case has a phone (2026-11-12, section 11; a case opened since both are
  required has both, a case of before has at least one of the two, and
  until then the Email row always showed), the lookup id with Copy, the
  status.
- The timeline: every event, the acting moderator's username, the details
  in words (a note shown as typed).
- Schedule: a date-time and a meeting link, Save (`/schedule-recovery-case`).
- Bucket one: a Pull key button. The moderator picks one of their anos
  accounts (the spending account that holds the stake; the keyholders
  refuse the others with `403 not a moderator`, shown as "this account
  holds no moderator stake"). The page makes a one-time hybrid pair, signs
  the account envelope for `/get-security-bucket-one-key` with pair one
  from the account's `keyBlob`, asks every keyholder in parallel, opens
  the shares with aad `lookupId || shareType || keyId`, groups by `keyId`
  and combines the newest group with at least `shareThreshold` shares.
  Then `/list-case-security-records` (bucket 1), decrypts the rows whose
  `keyId` matches and shows the images. `404 unknown lookup id` from the
  keyholders shows as "the keyholders know no identity with this lookup
  id". Bucket two: the same with `/get-security-bucket-two-key` and bucket
  2, images and texts, every key the keyholders answered.
- Sign off: the account picker, Approve or Reject, a note, Sign. The sign-
  off message of masterpod 12.6 signed by pair one,
  `/sign-off-recovery-case`. The page shows who has signed what. Since
  2026-11-19 (section 11; decision 10 of
  forclaude/wallet-chat-and-passkey-plan-1.md) the passkey line stands
  under the heading and the line of who has signed, over the form: "To
  confirm, this phone or computer will ask for your passkey, the one you
  log in with." Sign first asks the device for the passkey that opened
  the session (the passkey check, 8.9), before pair one is opened; a
  check that does not pass shows its sentence in red under the button,
  and nothing is signed.
- Dismiss: the preset reason, a note, Dismiss (`/dismiss-recovery-case`),
  behind a confirmation.
- Banker packet, shown when the status is approved or delivering: the
  lookup id, the URL and the hybrid key as JSON `{ "x25519": ..., "mlkem":
  ... }`, each with Copy and one Copy all, laid out as the bankers' GUI
  takes them. Shares received listed below it, by keyholder and type.

### 12.4 Services and state, new or changed

    recovery.service        the recovery session, apart from SessionService: caseId, the recovery session keys,
                            the PRF output and KEK_prf, the recovery hybrid private key, the last /get-recovery-pod
                            answer, the combined backup code and seeds while the finish runs; sign(path, body)
                            builds the recovery envelope (caseId as the signer); everything in RAM; the contact
                            email and the contact phone are two signals, each a string or null (the phone since
                            2026-11-12), set by the locked-out stepper at the open and by every /get-recovery-pod
                            answer (applyPod), emptied by close(); RecoveryPodAnswer carries contactPhone and
                            anosAccounts, both optional, since a masterpod of before sends neither
    masterpod-api.service   one method per new route (masterpod 12.4); challenge() takes the three new purposes,
                            openCase with the anoPod id the keyholders named, and answers its username
                            (2026-11-08); since 2026-11-18 (4.9) challenge() takes the lookup id too for
                            openCase, and its answer carries credentialIds; listAnosAccounts items carry
                            breakGlassBlob; listMyBreakGlassMoves and fileBreakGlassMoves (masterpod 14.4.1,
                            2026-11-08)
    anos-api.service        getAccountAs(envelope, quiet) (2026-11-08): /get-account with an envelope the caller
                            signed, the break-glass pair's at the finish; getAccount calls it;
                            getAssistedTransferAs(envelope, quiet) (2026-11-10): /get-assisted-transfer the same
                            way, the finish's read of a break-glass move the validators already hold;
                            getAssistedTransfer calls it; HeldAssistedTransfer carries type, as the validator
                            answers it (5.4)
    account-creation.service
                            the new accounts of Move your money, opened as the Wallet page opens one (8.3;
                            2026-11-08)
    keyholder-api.service   getSecurityBucketOneKey(n, envelope), getSecurityBucketTwoKey(n, envelope): the
                            keyholder's moderator routes, the account envelope as the body; getOwner(n, lookupId,
                            timeoutMs) (2026-11-08): the keyholder's /get-owner, level none, quiet in the log
    shares.service          findOwner(lookupId) (2026-11-08): every keyholder asked /get-owner at once with the
                            deposit's 15 second limit; { found: true, anopodId } on the first 200, else { found:
                            false, answered }, answered the keyholders that said unknown lookup id (zero: none
                            could be reached)
    crypto.service          generateHybridKeys(), wrapHybridPrivateKey / unwrapHybridPrivateKey (124-byte blob),
                            decryptFromHybrid (the mirror of encryptToHybrid: X25519 and ML-KEM-1024 decapsulation,
                            the same HKDF and aad), combineShares (shamir-secret-sharing combine), signSignOff
                            (pair one over the canonical sign-off), backupCodeProof (the backup code keys over a
                            canonical payload); buildBreakGlassTransferTransaction and
                            signAccountEnvelopeAsBreakGlass (2026-11-08): the break-glass move and the account
                            envelope signed by the break-glass pair, signAccountEnvelopeWith behind both envelopes;
                            everything else reused as it is
    config.service          edition in WalletConfig
    identity form           the nine-field form of the identity page becomes a component both the identity page
                            and the locked-out stepper use; the identity page's behaviour does not change
    find passkey            the walk-through in front of the locked-out stepper (2026-11-18), a component the
                            locked-out page shows first: five screens, the start page's unlockWithPasskey behind
                            "Try Log in now", and done, at which the page shows its stepper; it keeps nothing, and
                            it asks the masterpod only what a Log in asks
    shell                   Moderation in the navigation when edition is moderator and a session is open

### 12.5 Running it on this machine

    masterpod       npm run db:setup (the new tables and alters), restart; WEB_ORIGIN unchanged locally
    keyholders      RECOVERY_POD_HOSTS default (localhost) already covers the masterpod
    the proxy       npm run server as today; EDITION=moderator npm run server to work as a moderator
    pods            a person's pod with setup, both buckets and an anos account or two (its break-glass
                    seeds deposited); a moderator pod moderatorjoy vouched by the super seed, setup complete,
                    a spending account funded from another account and staked 1000 anos for moderator; a
                    second moderator pod for the second signature
    the bankers     the keyholder GUI on the Windows machine with the two YubiKeys, pointed at the banker
                    packet; the keyholders on this machine do the posting

The person's side is tested in a browser or profile that does not hold the
person's pod's passkey, or with that passkey given up (masterpod 12.6, last
paragraph).

### 12.6 Out of scope, not built

- Email or any message to the person; the app is the channel.
- A cancel of a break-glass move by either key (`breakGlassCancel` by the
  break-glass pair, `assistedTransferCancel` by the owner's own keys, both
  accepted by the validators since 2026-11-08) and the owner's dispute
  path (a cached key blob, a "Dispute a recovery" button, a warning): a
  later plan. Moving anos with the recovered break-glass keys was built
  2026-11-08 (12.3, Move your money; section 11).
- A moderator's history, several moderators on a call, a reject rule.
- Any change to the bankers' GUI; it takes the packet as it is.

### 12.7 Build notes

Filled in by each build chat, one subsection per build.

#### Build 1, the locked-out flow and the recovery pod (2026-10-26)

Built from `~/Desktop/Z/forclaude/build-1-case-and-recovery-pod.md`;
`ng build` clean. What this section left open and how it was decided:

- The identity form became
  `src/app/components/identity-form.component.ts`: the seven texts with
  Known / Unknown, the country select, the date picker and the guidance
  paragraph, rendering an `IdentityFormState` the page owns (signals for
  the answers, `complete`, `countryName`, `dateText`, `answers()`,
  `reset()`), so the answers survive a pane change on the identity page
  and its review pane reads them as before. The identity page keeps its
  why, review and action markup; nothing it does changed.
- `RecoveryService` (`services/recovery.service.ts`) holds the recovery
  session apart from `SessionService`: the case id, status, username,
  email and lookup id as signals, the last `/get-recovery-pod` answer, and
  in plain fields the session keys, the PRF output, `KEK_prf` and the
  hybrid private key; `sign(path, body)` builds the 12.4.1 envelope.
  `RECOVERY_POLL_MS` (15 s) lives there, not in `constants.ts`.
- `MasterpodApiService.challenge(purpose, username?)`; `openRecoveryCase`
  and `unlockRecoveryPod` take the self-signed envelope;
  `getRecoveryPod(envelope, quiet)` takes the recovery envelope from
  `RecoveryService.sign`, so the API service does not depend on the
  recovery service.
- `CryptoService` additions: `HybridKeys`, `generateHybridKeys`,
  `hybridKeysFromSecret`, `hybridPublicKeyOf`, `wrapHybridPrivateKey`,
  `unwrapHybridPrivateKey` (x25519 secret (32) || ml-kem seed (64) under
  `KEK_prf`, 124 bytes); nothing else touched.
- The locked-out stepper: step 1's Next computes the lookup id, drops the
  public ledger id and the answers (the identity page's rule), then
  advances; the linear stepper only moves once the step's `completed`
  binding has rendered, so the page waits for the next render
  (`afterNextRender`) before `stepper.next()`. Back to step 1 shows an
  empty form; Next then moves on with the computed id unless the form is
  filled in again. The recovery passkey is registered with the username
  as both name and display name (the person's names are not kept). The
  local assertion for the PRF output, when the registration returned
  none, is `PasskeyService.assert` with a random challenge; the platform's
  picker then shows every passkey of the site and the person picks the
  one just made.
- Refusals in words: `409` on open as "A case is already open for this
  identity", `404` from `/challenge` as "No anoPod has that username",
  `401 unknown passkey` on Continue as "This passkey belongs to no
  recovery case" with the hint that the person is not locked out on this
  device. The contact email is checked as the masterpod does (3 to 254
  characters, an `@` not first).
- My recovery: the status sentences of 12.3 ("Delivering: n of 3" counts
  the largest group of backupcode shares by `keyId`, the threshold from
  `/api/config`); the timeline shows `opened` as "Case opened" (the
  masterpod answers it), `scheduled` with the meeting link as a link,
  `approved`, `dismissed` with the preset reason in words, `recovered`,
  `completed`. The poll stops on completed and dismissed; a 401 says the
  recovery session has ended. The finish stepper's place is a comment in
  the template (build 3).
- Checked on the user's 4200 in the built-in browser: `/recover`;
  `/recover/open` with the form filled, the lookup id computed and the
  stepper advancing, the username lookup against the live masterpod
  ("quinnkoch found"), step 3 reached; `/recover/case` without a session
  goes to `/recover`. Opening a case needs the restarted masterpod and a
  passkey ceremony: the user's run-through, on a browser profile that does
  not hold the pod's passkey (masterpod 12.6, last paragraph).

#### Build 2, the moderator edition and the moderation pages (2026-10-26)

Built from `~/Desktop/Z/forclaude/build-2-moderation.md`; `ng build`
clean. What this section left open and how it was decided:

- `EDITION` is read by `server/config.js` through a `oneOf` helper:
  `wallet` or `moderator`, `wallet` by default, anything else refused at
  boot (`EDITION must be one of wallet, moderator, got "x"`); `server/app.js`
  answers it in `/api/config` as `edition`. `ConfigService` gets the
  `Edition` type, `edition` in `WalletConfig` and a `moderatorEdition`
  computed. A proxy started before this build answers no `edition`, which
  the app reads as the wallet edition.
- The shell: `Moderation` (icon `gavel`) after the status entries and
  before Notifications, when the edition is moderator and a session is
  open; the toolbar's brand reads "Moderator wallet" in that edition
  (since 2026-11-24 "Moderator", section 11).
  Approved change 5 placed "the landing card's title" in the shell; the
  landing page's own card title ("Your anoPod") lives in
